title: [EuiBadge][COLOR CONTRAST]: It is difficult to see selected text when I click and drag or select all with the keyboard
body: **Describe the problem** This issue was raised in a thread in the EUI slack channel where the user was having trouble determining when text was selected using their mouse. After some discussion, we determined the text was being selected, but the default `::selection` CSS background color was almost identical to our `EuiBadge` background color. I did some more experimenting with the `EuiBadge` component in light and dark themes. The screenshots below show most of our badges make it difficult to see selected text with Chrome's default CSS. **Light theme, all text selected, Chrome latest, MacOS** --- **Dark theme, all text selected, Chrome latest, MacOS** ## Environment * MacOS Ventura * Chrome latest * https://eui.elastic.co/#/display/badge ## Proposed solution We should review these badges and add custom CSS for the `::selection` pseudo-class. This selector is supported in all evergreen browsers and would be a big improvement for accessibility. See [MDN ::selection entry](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/::selection) for more information and browser support. ## WCAG or Vendor Guidance (optional) - [Understanding SC 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum) (Level AA)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html) - [MDN ::selection accessibility concerns](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/::selection#accessibility_concerns)

author: ryankeairns
title: [EuiCollapsibleNavBeta] Add popover capability to EuiCollapsibleNavGroup
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
For the new nav, we believe the discoverability of the solution switcher will be greater in the left nav than its current location in the top nav (breadcrumb).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Currently, their is a bespoke [nav group](https://eui.elastic.co/storybook/index.html/iframe.html?args=&id=navigation-euicollapsiblenav-euicollapsiblenavbeta-group--playground) with no interactivity. It was designed with the special 'solution' groups in mind and it works well for this purpose (i.e. no accordion actions; always open; visually prominent). These aspects/this design remains relevant but we now desire to add the option to show a popover menu from this special group header. In other words, it will continue to not be an accordion, but it will need to provide a means for switching between solution menus.

Side note: we don't have a current use case for the purely static version, so we'll leave it up to the implementor as to keeping this functionality. In other words, making the popover interaction an option on top of what exists today.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
As noted above, we're using breadcrumb today but feel the discoverability is inferior to placing the switcher in the left nav which is what is ultimately where the menu change occurs. We also explored an icon only button alongside the group title but this felt like it would display options for the current solution as opposed to switching. For those reasons, the preference is for a full width, dropdown-like experience that uses a popover menu.

**Desired timeline**
Where doing an 'internal' release for 8.14 (FF April 16th). However, users won't get access to this until 8.15. If we could get this in Kibana by end of April, that would give us ample time to try it ourselves in QA, dogfood the final design, and continue getting feedback from Elastic users.

**Additional context**
- Selection of an icon has been challenging. For now, it is `layers` but that could change and/or we will create a new icon. For this reason, it would be great if we can set it to any EUI icon.
- Prefer the no arrow look when the nav is expanded; but show it when collapsed. If that's a pain, an arrow in expanded mode can work.
- For the collapsed mode, we would like to have two buttons (today it is one). The first would be the solution group / loog and would open the same popover. The second (`apps` icon button) would show the full menu just as it does today; no change in the content of this popover menu.

## Designs

_These can also be found in the related [epic](https://github.com/elastic/kibana-team/issues/719)_

author: mgadewoll
title: [Storybook] Update utils to ensure properly merged story configs
body:
## Summary

Our storybook utils to disable/hide/move component props in the controls table are currently generating and returning objects without context of any existing entries on the config it adds to (component or story level). While Storybook does merge configs (component and story level - story level overwrites component level) this can still result in the utils output potentially overwriting existing prop control definitions - e.g. when we call multiple utils on the same prop and in the same level (e.g. story level).

We want to update the utils to ensure they update the existing config instead of overwriting it.

💬 See this [conversation](https://github.com/elastic/eui/pull/7569#discussion_r1523658858) for more information.

## Acceptance criterea
* utils (`hideStorybookControls`, `disableStorybookControls` and `moveStorybookControlsToCategory`) don't overwrite other config entries but mutate the existing config while respecting existing entries
* props that are adjusted in the controls panel via utils are properly output (e.g. moved and disabled)

author: JasonStoltz
title: [Meta] Runtime performance baseline and monitoring
body:
As our library continues to grow and evolve, we must evaluate and monitor how we're impacting performance in consuming projects -- particularly in Kibana.

[This PR](https://github.com/elastic/eui/pull/7374#issuecomment-1821861724) raised concerns about the potential performance impacts of the Emotion conversion.

We encountered some performance related issues in Kibana related to Emotion, but most of them have been mitigated by an effort to memoize emotion styles. At the time of writing this issue, we have about 80% of the library converted to Emotion, so we do not anticipate many more performance issues related to Emotion.

However, we must consider how we prevent future performance degredation and manage to a baseline level of performance in the EUI library on an ongoing basis.

The foundational task that we'd need to accomplish as part of this Meta issue is establishing that baseline, and putting a system in place to continually monitor it.

author: tkajtoch
title: [Epic] New documentation site M1
body:
> [!Note]
> This meta issue tracks the effort of developing the new EUI documentation site only. Check out the [Elastic Design System - Milestone 2](https://github.com/elastic/eui-private/issues/218) for more.

# Summary

With the transition to EUI being a part of the Elastic Design System, we want to improve how we create, maintain, and publish our docs.

# Goals

* Replace the current website with a shiny new one based on docusaurus ([check out the ADR why we chose docusaurus](https://github.com/elastic/ux-madr/blob/main/decisions/eui/0001-use-docusaurus.md) - Elastic internal only) while keeping the content mostly the same
  * We plan to reorganize and rewrite content in further milestones
* Reduce the complexity of writing and maintaining docs by converting them to MDX
* Convert all component examples to use interactive component previews based on react-live (or similar)
* Add full-text search capabilities
* Add Storybook playgrounds for all EUI components

# Definition of Done

* The new documentation site is deployed in place of the current one (https://eui.elastic.co) and is publicly accessible
* The new documentation site passes manual QA and accessibility tests
* Buildkite pipelines are updated to build and publish the new website on every EUI release

author: 1Copenut
title: [EuiIconTip] Ensure `aria-hidden` attribute is suppressed to avoid axe (accessibility) errors in loading cycle
body: **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** Our `icon_tip.tsx` file adds a `tabindex=0` to [the child EuiIcon on line 66](https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/main/src/components/tool_tip/icon_tip.tsx#L66). This is causing an accessibility violation in Kibana just now because icons with `aria-hidden="true"` have a `tabindex` that allows them to be reached by keyboard focus before the finished icon has been loaded. **Describe the solution you'd like** I'd like to find a way to signal to `EuiIconTip` that it should not be ARIA hidden by its nature. Maybe we could explicitly set the attribute `undefined` ? ```diff ``` **Additional context** Kibana is tracking this error in https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/172598. There may be others that haven't been discovered yet. The Buildkite error logs showed this snippet, that suggests the scan is running while icons are not fully loaded: ``` ```

author: julianrosado
title: [EuiText] Remove img's from styling
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

[EuiText] adds a margin-bottom to a number of text elements and also `img`'s . See [styles](https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/86e67023e83c7f098df55ef203f58816b4d025e1/src/components/text/text.styles.ts#L144-L152). Presumably this is to account for `img` float's as described in [EUI documentation](https://eui.elastic.co/#/display/image#float-images-within-text).

This has an unintended side effect of add margin's to images that are added to things such as [callouts](https://eui.elastic.co/#/display/callout), necessitating some style overrides.

While, admittedly, images in callouts are not a common feature, I would argue image floats in Kibana are an even rarer bird. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Remove `img` 's from having their styles modified by EuiText

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The one went with was a recommendation by @cee-chen to override the margin with `!important` styles.

**Desired timeline**
No specific deadline

Reach out if you want an image!

author: JasonStoltz
title: Add clear guidance on how to mark fields as Optional
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We received a question in Slack about how to mark fields as "required". It wasn't apparent to the user that our guidance is to mark optional fields instead of required fields, and beyond that, what the standard is for marking fields as optional.

In our guidance for forms, we say the following:

> Use a label (and description if needed) for each form field. All form fields should be considered required unless stated alongside the label.

Reference: https://eui.elastic.co/#/forms/form-layouts/guidelines

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We should add additional guidance, or better yet, an example, of how to indicate form fields as "Optional".

We should first validate this by analyzing current usage in Kibana, but it would appear that the going pattern is to use the text "(Optional)" at the end of a form field.

Example: Stack Management > Rules > Create rule

![image (7)](https://github.com/elastic/eui/assets/1427475/030baf10-2464-46da-8b24-7ad9a4cce014)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
N/A

**Desired timeline**
There is no rush to do this, but at the same time, it should be an easy thing to add to alleviate future confusion.

**Additional context**
https://uxdesign.cc/form-field-required-vs-optional-9b4d7cdbf400
https://uxmovement.com/forms/always-mark-optional-form-fields-not-required-ones/

author: MichaelMarcialis
title: [EuiDatePicker] Add `compressed` prop
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, `EuiDatePicker` is one of the few (if not the only) components that doesn't offer a `compressed` size option. This presents consistency issues when attempting to add a simple date picker to a form that utilizes compressed form elements. Strangely enough, this does not apply to the the more complex `EuiSuperDatePicker` component, as it does offer a compressed size.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add a `compressed` size prop for the `EuiDatePicker` component.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could likely achieve the compressed look with some CSS overrides, but given that all other EUI form components have the compressed option baked in as a prop, it would be good if this component did the same for consistency.

**Desired timeline**
This isn't a super urgent request, given that it only creates a minor visual inconsistency at worst. But given the simplicity of the request, hopefully it's something that can be completed in a reasonable timeframe and not booted to the end of the backlog.

**Additional context**
CCing @drewdaemon, as this was brought up during our review here: https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/163346#pullrequestreview-1631797889

author: cee-chen
title: [Emotion] Figure out what exports we do and don't want to make public
body:
Currently, every single `*.styles.ts` component file is being exported in EUI as well as typed in `eui.d.ts`. As a team, we should tackle the following behaviors:

1. Determine whether or not we as a team want to make component styles publicly 
    - After a brief discussion in a team sync, we decided "not". Our current styles are incredibly specific to Emotion (due to the usage of ``` css`` ``` syntax - if we had used [object styles](https://emotion.sh/docs/object-styles) instead, this would potentially be different/more flexible). It currently doesn't make much sense to make them reusable.
    - _NOTE: If you have strong thoughts on/against the above, please feel free to leave a comment in this issue - we're open to discussing it!_
    - Make it clear in our documentation that we only offer styled components going forward, not styles themselves (or rather, the style utilities we offer should be very broad and intentional and generally not component-specific)
    - **However**, before we can remove all `.styles.ts` files from being exported, we first need to account for consumers who are using Sass/CSS-in-JS variables & mixins that are component specific:

2. Some components have style-related **variables** that may need to be reused by consumers, or even by other components within EUI. Examples of these are [`euiFormVariables`](https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/d39c0e988409f90f62af57174590044664b2bfce/src/components/form/form.styles.ts#L19) and [`euiHeaderVariables`](https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/3e950bf7605c6fea31f75cd7f2aedfe233d5607e/src/components/header/header.styles.ts#L20).
Instead of moving these style variables outside our `.styles.ts` files and continuing to export them publicly, @tkajtoch has suggested switching them to CSS variables instead. This will involve:
    1. Declaring these component style vars once at the top level in our [global styles](https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/3ab325b45049d65899d6c2f0f6cb86dadcd6f1d0/src/global_styling/reset/global_styles.tsx#L122) (ensuring consumers have access to the default vars everywhere in the app)
    2. Each component usage should check if `modify` exists in the nearest `EuiThemeProvider` and if it does, render new scoped definitions for each CSS var
    3. @tkajtoch also suggested adding a hook that exports the style vars later, although I'm not totally sure what his vision was in mind for that

3. In our [compile-eui](https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/1cb498a07e1edef04389602afc7f2ac8a458fe29/scripts/compile-eui.js) and [dtsgenerator](https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/1cb498a07e1edef04389602afc7f2ac8a458fe29/scripts/dtsgenerator.js) scripts, ignore/skip all `*.styles.ts` files

4. Audit & standardize all exported `global_stylings/` mixins/functions
EUI currently has several Emotion “hooks” we’re exporting, several decisions (or lack therefore) are confusing around them:
    1. Why some of them are hooks and some are not (we should likely eliminate all hooks and simply require the `euiThemeContext` to be passed in, this is also frankly easier for [Emotion theme usage](https://emotion.sh/docs/theming))
    2. Why some mixins/functions are in `global_stylings` and some are in `theme/amsterdam`
    3. Which should even be publicly available, and which we should make internal/EUI-only

author: Heenawter
title: [EuiListGroupItem] Give full control over tooltip props
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** As part of the navigation embeddable in Kibana, we are rendering a list of links using the `EuiListGroup` component. We want to be able to add more complicated tooltips to the links, including (a) choosing the position of the tooltip and (b) giving the tooltip a custom title. **Describe the solution you'd like** Allow the consumer of the `EuiListGroupItem` to send in **all** (or, at the very least, a specific subset - including, at bare minimum, `title` and `position`) of the tooltip props. **Describe alternatives you've considered** Right now, we are sending in a custom tooltip via the `label` prop of the `EuiListGroupItem`: ```typescript label={ {/* Setting `title=""` so that the native browser tooltip is disabled */}
{linkLabel}
} ``` This gives the following result: https://github.com/elastic/eui/assets/8698078/5004a0bc-314a-4972-8f4f-99d8ed921c7f The problem is, this means that the tooltip is only attached to the **text** of the button and not the button itself. We want to be able to send in the tooltip information through `EuiListGroupItem` prop(s) so that the tooltip can instead wrap the button, just like it would if we were using the `showTooltip` and `toolTipText` props.

body:
As per the documentation for EuiRange:

> Maximum of 20 ticks allowed

While this is a fine limit in general, hardcoding it seems unnecessarily limiting. I'm working on a project with very wide range sliders (think full screen width) with very narrow ticks (labels are 1 character each), and it could easily fit many many more than 20 ticks that way.
Additionally, a hardcoded limit of 20 doesn't really help when the sliders is very short.

As such, I'd like to request an option to override this limit.

author: 1Copenut
title: [EuiTable][SCREEN READER]: Screen readers cannot access parent row when a child row is expanded
body:
## Description
I discovered a bug with our `EuiTable` [expanding rows feature](https://eui.elastic.co/#/tabular-content/tables#expanding-rows) where screen readers will allow users to expand a child row, access that child row content, but not be able to access the parent row. If I expand the first row for example, I can read out the new "second" row, but my screen reader focus skips over the previous first row and goes back to the heading.

I've attached a short MP4 movie showing this behavior with VoiceOver + Safari. I've observed this behavior with NVDA + Chrome also.

## WCAG guidance
* [SC 1.3.1: Info and Relationships (Level A)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html)

author: JasonStoltz
title: [Meta] Storybook
body:
As part of a larger effort to replace the existing EUI documentation and build up EUI into a more robust design system, we would like to build out a [storybook](https://storybook.js.org/) for EUI.

Storybook spike: https://github.com/elastic/eui/issues/6583
Related https://github.com/elastic/eui/pull/6816, https://github.com/elastic/eui/issues/6652

## Why add a storybook?

- Better Developer Experience for our users -- we can better illustrate various use cases and states for components and create a space for them to explore the effect of various props and options.
- Better testing for ourselves -- We will be able to visually diff our stories as we roll out updates, giving us more confidence that we are not breaking UX and causing regressions.
- Better Developer Experience for EUI contributors -- Having an isolated space to develop components will be a huge improvement for our own development workflows.
- Embeddable examples for our Design System website -- by creating a Storybook for EUI, authors documenting patterns and components in our upcoming Design System website will be able to embed functional examples hosted in Storybook.
- Predictable discovery for Kibana developers - 30+ Storybooks are deployed across Kibana already, having our library in the [same format and colocated](https://ci-artifacts.kibana.dev/storybooks/main/latest/index.html) will help developers find the components they need.


## Some considerations

- Our current docs system lets us dynamically switch library versions via a path parameter. We'd like to have a similar setup with the new storybook. This helps us compare visuals between versions and identify regressions.
- Individual stories will be embedded into a larger documentation system. Most of the design guidance will live in that documentation site, so this storybook will primarily be a tool for our developers, not designers.


TODO: Task this out. Is the creation of individual stories a separate effort?

title: [EuiColorPicker][SCREEN READER]: Provide additional instructions for NVDA/JAWS about how to interact with 1 and 2-axis pickers
body:
## Description
The `EuiColorPicker` [component](https://eui.elastic.co/#/forms/color-selection#color-picker) was previously flagged as being inaccessible for NVDA users in #2195. I retested the component and found it was accessible, but [required me to toggle into **Focus mode**](https://github.com/elastic/eui/issues/2195#issuecomment-1494344185). I feel adding an `aria-desribedby` set of instructions would help users understand they may need to toggle into Focus/Forms mode to use the picker. This would probably use our `EuiScreenReaderOnly` component and a unique ID that points to the input. Should be an easy change, non-breaking.

body:

**To reproduce**

author: Heenawter
title: (Accessibility) [EuiSelectable] Unable to make selections when second interactable element in focus
body:
For Dashboard input controls, we give users the ability to both search **and** filter the items in the `EuiSelectable` component as part of the creation/editing process:

![Screenshot 2023-03-02 at 9 12 57 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8698078/222486059-66342cc6-bd34-4eea-b502-752888612368.png)

To accomplish this, we are currently using the `searchable` prop and adding our filter component between the native `search` and `list`, like so:

```typescript
<EuiSelectable
  searchable
  ...
>
{(list, search) => (
  <>
    {search}
    <EuiSpacer size={'s'} />
    {fieldTypeFilter} // this is our custom filter component
    <EuiSpacer size={'s'} />
    {list}
  </>
)}
</EuiSelectable>
```

Unfortunately, this messes with the `a11y` support that was added to the `EuiSelectable` component, since it seems to assume that **all** children should retain focus as the user navigates the list. This works great when the `search` is in focus, but it gives a confusing experience when the `fieldTypeFilter` is in focus, like so:

![Mar-02-2023 09-28-26](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8698078/222490903-d1a72afc-00c2-47df-9e4a-aa5831b3f411.gif)

In the above GIF, you can see that, while the `fieldTypeFilter` is in focus, the user is **unable** to make selections in the `list` despite it giving the appearance that they should be able to. It would be nice if **only** the `search` child retained focus in this way, whereas any other children did not - or, perhaps, if there was a way to control whether or not a child retained focus.

author: elizabetdev
title: Box shadows hooks and tokens should be more performant and only use one shadow
body: Currently, we had an issue https://github.com/elastic/eui/pull/6604 originated by a CSS filter having multiple `drop-shadow()`. In this PR we found out that we also have **box-shadows** with multiple [shadows](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/box-shadow#setting_three_shadows) defined. For example `useEuiShadow('l');` has four shadows defined: ``` box-shadow: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.10) 0px 1px 5px, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07) 0px 3.6px 13px, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06) 0px 8.4px 23px, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05) 0px 23px 35px; ``` Can we improve our current shadow `tokens` and `hooks` to only use one shadow and maintain the same visual aspect? This will make the CSS more performant.

author: MichaelMarcialis
title: Alert & Error Icon Follow-up Considerations
body:
As a follow-up to a recent PR that updates the `alert` icon and adds a new `error` icon (#6550), I think it may be wise to consider the following:

- Consider deprecating/removing the `crossInACircleFilled` icon for two reasons: 1) It's very close to the new `error` icon, and 2) it perpetuates a problematic pattern where some EUI icons offer regular/circled/filled variants, which often lead to a lot of interface inconsistencies. I imagine it can be replaced with either a regular `cross` or `error` icon, as the context dictates.
- Consider changing the current `alert` icon's name to `warning`. Doing so will make it clearer to developers that we have specific icons to use for error and warning cases.

Curious to know the team's thoughts on these suggestions. Thanks!

author: 1Copenut
title: [EuiTableRow][SCREEN READER]: Rows with a `tabIndex` are not traversable when Firefox is paired with VoiceOver
body:
## Description
Our [EuiTableRow#L97](https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/22b9f61e4185eee7ddf63b00cc377b57d0ab7139/src/components/table/table_row.tsx#L97) has a `tabIndex={0}` attribute that prevents users from traversing tables when they're using Firefox with VoiceOver on MacOS.

This issue should be tested in a Windows environment with NVDA and JAWS to determine the scope of the issue before proceeding with a potentially breaking change.

## Possible fix
Removing the `tabIndex` attribute restores the natural ability to traverse by row using `Ctrl + Opt + LEFT | RIGHT Arrow` and by column using `Ctrl + Opt + UP | DOWN Arrow`. This may not be a perfect solution if upstream consumers are wiring tables to perform some action based on an event listener attached to the row. An alternative would be to add a `<button>` into one of the cells and have that trigger the row action.

```diff
<tr
  className={classes}
  onClick={onClick}
  onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
  onKeyUp={onKeyUp}
- tabIndex={0}
  {...rest}
>
+   <th>
+      <button onClick={yourRowAction}>Click me!</button>
+      Table row header text
+    </th>
</tr>
```

## WCAG guidance
* [SC 1.3.1: Info and Relationships (Level A)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html)

author: 1Copenut
title: [EuiKeyPadMenuItem] `aria-pressed` attribute requires a button to be turned "on" or "off" like a toggle
body: ## Description While adding a11y tests to `EuiKeyPadMenu` in #6495 I observed the menu pad item buttons had an `aria-pressed` attribute. I could click the button and the attribute shifted from `false` to `true` as expected, but I couldn't click the button again and toggle back to `false`. I looked through relevant documentation and came up with this [guidance from MDN on aria-pressed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-pressed): > Adding aria-pressed to an element with a role of [button](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Roles/button_role) turns the button into a toggle button. The `aria-pressed` attribute is only relevant for toggle buttons. It represents the button's current "pressed" state. > ... > Toggle buttons require a full press-and-release cycle to change their value. Pressing and releasing it once changes the value to `true`. If it's pressed and released again, the value changes back to `false`. I think we should add the ability to truly toggle our Key Pad Menu Item buttons, so multiple can be toggled on or off. By adding the ability to reverse the button state, I think we prevent a breaking change and make it more of a custom filterable control. ## WCAG guidance * [SC 1.3.1: Info and Relationships](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html) ---

author: i-a-n
title: [Icons] Icon request: "Book"
body: Hey there. As part of our big Knowledge Centric Support initiative, we're adding tons of knowledge functionality to the [Elastic Support Portal](/elastic/support-portal). The big new feature we're launching soon is the concept of a "Book", which will be a collection of knowledge articles, collated together to guide users in a specific area of our products. Thus far we've been using the `documents` icon to indicate books, but we'd like to ask if you would be able to create a special `book` icon for EUI that we could use in the Elastic Knowledge System. The only real direction I could offer is that the current `documents` icon is generally pretty close to what we're imagining, but doesn't feel like a unique representation of a book. Something like the Material Design "menu book" icon or Bootstrap "journal-text" icon feels much more in tune with what we're going for. Thanks for considering!

author: i-a-n
title: [Icons] Icon request: "Case" or "Issue"
body: Hey there. As part of our big Knowledge Centric Support initiative, we're adding tons of knowledge functionality to the [Elastic Support Portal](/elastic/support-portal). One of the main categories of search results and linked content will be the support case, where customers talk to our support engineers to get help. Thus far we've been using the `tableDensityExpanded` icon to indicate a case, but we'd like to ask if you would be able to create a special `case` or `issue` icon for EUI that we could use in the Support Portal. The only real direction I could offer is that the current `tableDensityExpanded` icon is generally pretty close to what we're imagining, but doesn't quite represent a back-and-forth, dynamic conversation. Something like the Material Design "forum" or Bootstrap "receipt" might be closer to conveying what a support issue actually is? Thanks for considering!

author: elizabetdev
title: [euiTextTruncate utility] Support multi-line truncation
body:
This suggestion was shared by @evangelia-mitsopoulou in our EUI slack channel:

> I noticed in most cloud tables, the names are not truncated and are occupying a lot of vertical space on resizing. I think if we add a  multi-line ellipsis utility class would be beneficial not only for my "specific flyout" but for most tables in wider contexts as well. Our views will look tidy and the information compact

So we should consider enhance our [`euiTextTruncate` functionality](https://eui.elastic.co/#/theming/typography/utilities#wrapping) to support multi-line text truncation.

Here's an article that shows how we can support this:
https://css-tricks.com/line-clampin/

title: [EuiTourStep] `anchor` and `isStepOpen`

`EuiTourStep` attempts to find the `anchor` element on mount or when the prop value changes.

https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/f7c05f957dbdfc02f611748ce80ec2110221e8a5/src/components/tour/tour_step.tsx#L173-L185

author: krithika369
title: [EuiSearchBar] field_value_selection filter with multiSelect disabled does not produce the search query
body:
When setting `multiSelect` to `false`, it can be seen that the `onChange` handler of the [EuiSearchBar](https://elastic.github.io/eui/#/forms/search-bar#search-bar-filters) does not include the field anymore (`test_filter` below); it works with multiSelect set to `"and"` / `"or"`. 

```javascript
{
        type: "field_value_selection",
        field: "test_filter",
        name: "Test filter",
        multiSelect: false,
        options: [...]
}

title: [EuiResizableContainer] Add support for `onResizeStart` and `onResizeEnd` callback props
body:
While implementing a resizable layout in Discover using `EuiResizableContainer`, we ran into some conflicts with `react-reverse-portal`. We were able to implement a workaround, but it involved setting up our own event listeners to watch for when resizing starts and ends.

It would simplify our use case a lot, and would probably be generally useful, if `EuiResizableContainer` accepted callback props for `onResizeStart` and `onResizeEnd` that would allow consumers to easily listen for when resizing starts and ends.

For our use case it's only important to listen for resizing triggered by a mouse click, but it might be worth considering whether these callbacks would apply to keyboard based resizing as well.

title: [SearchBar] Leading zeroes on string values removed by filter
body:
When setting a filter like `case:00750140` in the search bar, it gets rewritten as `case:750140` when the search text is rewritten by changing filters.


A) In the UI, this can be worked around by using `case:"00750140"`.   However, programatically , the behaviour is not the same:

B) Original programmatic problem: 
```
  setQuery(
        query.addSimpleFieldValue(
          'case',
          caseNumber
        )
      );
```

C) Attempted workaround:

```
  setQuery(
        query.addSimpleFieldValue(
          'case',
          `"${caseNumber}"`
        )
      );
```

However the workaround unexpectedly produced a different result than doing the same in the UI.   When using toESQuery(), the result from A was ES Query DSL like : `case: "00750140"`, as expected.   However the result from C was `case: "\"00750140\""`

Interestingly, even after C runs, I could convert the bahaviour back to that of A by pressing the space bar in the search box after the existing text, so there must be some transformation onKeyPress.

This would have otherwise been a bind, but I switched to use `addOrFieldValue`, which doesn't exhibit the bug

author: anthonyhastings
title: EuiFormRow and EuiDatePickerRange focus behaviour
body:
Hi team,

I've encountered an issue when using `EuiDatePickerRange` as the nested component within `EuiFormRow`. 

**Reproducible Example:**
https://codesandbox.io/s/mystifying-frost-80hfqv

**Reproduction Steps:**
1. Focus into either the start or end date control which adds focus state to the row component and highlights the label.
2. Click outside the controls to trigger blur and observe the row components focus state disappears as expected.
3. Focus into either date picker which adds focus state to the row component.
4. Choose a date and notice that when the date picker closes, the focus state of the row component remains.

**Initial Investigation:**
`EuiFormRow` expects a single child component, which it [clones](https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/8d07a5a93b885ba2354091782af8596830b05582/src/components/form/form_row/form_row.tsx#L280-L287) and supplies with [monkey patched](https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/8d07a5a93b885ba2354091782af8596830b05582/src/components/form/form_row/form_row.tsx#L123-L151) `onBlur` and `onFocus` events. It uses these monkey patched handlers to manage internal focus state, which is in turn used to [show the focused state](https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/8d07a5a93b885ba2354091782af8596830b05582/src/components/form/form_row/form_row.tsx#L236) on the field label.

`EuiFormRow` expects it's child component to either explicitly or implicitly apply the `onBlur` and `onFocus` handlers onto a form control contained within which would keep the focus state in sync with any interactions on the form element. When the row component has a child such as `EuiDatePicker` or `EuiFieldText` things work fine as those components implicitly [spread the props](https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/8d07a5a93b885ba2354091782af8596830b05582/src/components/form/field_text/field_text.tsx#L96) onto the input.

Whenever `EuiDatePickerRange` is used as the child component things get sketchy; this component [implicitly applies those handlers](https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/4ce30ba24b148485dfad2f37a1ed26be298e69a5/src/components/date_picker/date_picker_range.tsx#L137) onto a wrapper div element and not an actual form element. I'm surprised anything here actually works as to my own knowledge, only a div that had tabindex would actually be able to trigger blur and focus events. When the datepickers handle the selection of a date, no blur seems to emit from the div element and the row components state becomes frozen.

**Potential Solution:**
Locally I have a potential fix - I updated `EuiDatePickerRange` component to no longer spread `onBlur` and `onFocus` props onto the div container element. I then apply those handlers onto both the start and end date components (ensuring if they have handlers of their own that they get monkey patched). This means the handlers go to the form controls themselves, and now the rows focus state is in sync with the date pickers as they open/close/select values.

I'd be happy to PR properly if it sounds feasible!

Many Thanks

author: dokmic
title: [EuiGlobalToastList] Persistent toasts disappear immediately
body:
By default, the Kibana Core's notification service [sets](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/blob/main/src/core/public/notifications/toasts/global_toast_list.tsx#L65:L65) the `toastLifeTimeMs` prop to `Infinity`. It is supposed to keep toasts without this parameter until the user explicitly closes them. There is a use-case when we actually need this, but it does not work (elastic/kibana#128316 / elastic/kibana#133351). 

The problem lies in the `Timer` [implementation](https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/main/src/services/time/timer.ts#L18). Whenever we pass the `Infinity` value, it is automatically fired. That is the correct behavior of the `setTimeout` function (see [HTML5 spec](https://www.w3.org/TR/2011/WD-html5-20110525/timers.html)):
> If timeout is an Infinity value, a Not-a-Number (NaN) value, or negative, let timeout be zero.

If we try to pass the maximum possible value like in elastic/kibana#131402, then the toast disappears almost instantly:
```
  toastLifeTimeMs: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER - Date.now(),
```
That is because a single millisecond overflows the [`finishTime`](https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/main/src/services/time/timer.ts#L20) value.

Is it possible to either change the `Timer` implementation to support `Infinity` on input or don't use timers when the `toastLifeTimeMs` is `Infinity`? But we should keep in mind that the second option will not solve the bug with integer value overflow.

author: cee-chen
title: Add keyboard usage instructions to screen reader popover dialogue
body:
Per Zuhair's **EuiPopover** recommendation in https://github.com/elastic/eui/pull/5784#issuecomment-1101345252:

> I would suggest [...] adding context specific text (if possible) advising what the user needs to do to get to the first focusable element (like pressing the tab key, using the arrows etc.). If there are no focusable elements, then the text should naturally not be spoken. This should at least prompt the user to initiate action to interact with the popover, letting them know that they don't have to listen to the entire content.

Generally, **EuiPopover**s should use the `tabbable` library to check if there are tabbable elements, and also if `ownFocus` is true on the popover (otherwise tab will not behave as expected). If both conditions are met, an additional dialogue sentence should be added instructing screen readers to use the Tab key to reach the first interactable element.

Special components that will need specific instructions:

- **EuiTour** - does not apparently use ownFocus, should be double checked to confirm no tab instructions read out
- **EuiSelectableTemplateSitewide** - tab key closes popover, up/down arrow keys should be used
- **EuiComboBox** - tab key closes popover, up/down arrow keys should be used
- **EuiSuggest** - tab key closes popover, up/down arrow keys should be used
- **EuiSuperSelect** - tab key does nothing, up/down arrow keys should be used
- **EuiRange/EuiDualRange** with EuiInputPopover - tab key does nothing, up/down arrow keys should be used
- **EuiAutoRefresh** with EuiInputPopover - tab key behaves weirdly and should not be used(?)
- **EuiContextMenu** - tab key and up/down arrow keys can be used (eventually tab might be removed)
- **EuiSearchBar** tags dropdown(?) - user must tab into EuiSelectable, confirm EuiSelectable reads out arrow key navigation

author: 1Copenut
title: [EuiContextMenu][COGNITION]: Consider refactoring the EUI Context Menu to WAI spec for navigation menu button
body:
## Description
I'd like to consider refactoring our EUI Context Menu component to use the WAI-ARIA pattern for a [navigation menu button](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-practices/examples/menu-button/menu-button-links.html). This pattern can be easily composed into a [WAI-ARIA menubar](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-practices/#menu).

The current implementation announces the context "flyout" menu as a modal dialog, 

This is an improvement ticket based on my [comment on PR 5719](https://github.com/elastic/eui/pull/5719#issuecomment-1072846039).

## Background
**[From the linked comment:](https://github.com/elastic/eui/pull/5719#issuecomment-1072846039)**

> After taking a longer look at our EuiContextMenu and the [WAI guidelines for menus and menubars](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-practices/#menu), I have some better guidance. True [menu](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#menu)s and menubars behave like OS menus, which is a subtle but important distinction:
>
> > A menu is a widget that offers a list of choices to the user, such as a set of actions or functions. Menu widgets behave like native operating system menus, such as the menus that pull down from the menubars commonly found at the top of many desktop application windows.
> > [3.15 Menu or Menu bar](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-practices/#menu)
>
> This is where it's open to interpretation, but reading the spec a second and third time, it sounds like this pattern expects a menubar that has several links/buttons to expose menu elements. The EuiContextMenu doesn't appear to rise to this level, but does seem to be a good example of a [WAI navigation menu button](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-practices/examples/menu-button/menu-button-links.html) pattern. I think we could improve the handling of our component by doing a few things:

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Assume the menu "trigger" is always a button and add `aria-haspopup` and `aria-controls` attributes
- [ ] Adjust the menu of elements to not announce as a dialog, and add proper `menu` and `menuitem` ARIA attributes
- [ ] Wrap each `menuitem` in a span or something and do not allow them to take keyboard focus. We would use roving tabindex like radio buttons do with arrow keys, per the spec.
- [ ] Pressing `TAB` closes the menu and sets focus on the next focusable element on the page

## Guidance
- [Understanding Success Criterion 4.1.2: Name, Role, Value](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/name-role-value.html)

author: thompsongl
title: Pre-release validation for Kibana upgrades
body:
To improve the process of upgrading Kibana with new versions of EUI, we should implement a pre-release process to validate that no type errors or bugs have been introduced. Kibana CI is required to do so, which necessitates that non-local build of EUI be used. We have a couple options:

* Introduce alpha/beta releases to the release script
* Script to `build-pack` and commit on a branch
  * Point [`package.json` to the `.tar` file](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v8/configuring-npm/package-json#dependencies) 
  * `--no-validate` flag (required for `.tar` deps) may be a blocker for this approach
  * Could look simiilar to `backport` (i.e., clone of the repo in a separate directory)

In either case the end result should be a draft PR in Kibana that runs CI on a pre-release build of EUI.

Note that `yarn scripts/type_check` can be run using a local build `.tar`, but running the full suite of Jest tests is no longer feasible.

author: cchaos
title: [EuiDataGrid] Expansion popover initial focus
body: I'd like to discuss the behavior of cell popovers' initial focus behavior. To be honest, this may even apply more broadly to **EuiPopover** in general, but the problem is very highlighted in the **EuiDataGrid**. When clicking on a cell with simple text, or a single interactive element, or plain text with a cell action, the behavior feels good to initially focus on the first focusable element. ## The problem Where it breaks down is when there is more complex cell contents, like in the [row heights example](https://eui.elastic.co/pr_5681/#/tabular-content/data-grid-row-heights-options#overriding-specific-row-heights). When there's an interactive element within the cell contents that possibly very far down, that's what gets focused and therefore the popover auto-scrolls to this element: This isn't great for the specific reason that it feels buggy to not show the **start** of the contents. ## Possible solution: Auto-focus the popover instead It's already part of the tab order, just make it the first focused item. We might want to consider how we handle the visible focus ring, but this feels much clearer and expected. ### Pros: - For complex content this will keep the start of the content visible - Screen readers should be able to now read the full cell contents instead of jumping to a random link within - For simple content with cell actions, screen-readers will read the full cell contents instead of jumping to the cell action which may not provide context ### Cons: - For simple content, the extra focus may be visually distracting - ??

author: i-a-n
title: [EuiMarkdownEditor] `getCursorNode` function throws error in some cases
body:
while developing our own custom plugin for `EuiMarkdownEditor` we noticed that any markdown AST node that 1. has children and 2. isn't of `type === 'text'` will throw errors in the console. this can be replicated most simply by creating a multiline blockquote and then typing around in it:

```md
> foo
> bar
```

![Screen Shot 2021-12-22 at 9 29 23 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1937355/147133254-0b1ff406-2e61-4c4f-a315-b32fa9496e7a.png)

the `getCursorNode` function fails here: https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/main/src/components/markdown_editor/markdown_editor.tsx#L300

```js
for (let i = 0; i < node.children.length; i++) {
              const child = node.children[i];
              if (
                child.position.start.offset < selectionStart &&
```

...as it assumes that every _non-text node_ with children should be drilled down into, and each of those child nodes is expected to have `.position.start.offset` present. this isn't the case for nodes like, say `blockquote`, which can have child nodes like `type: 'break'`. we discovered this during development of our own plugin because it also creates child nodes who have no position.

my first instinct would be to safeguard those object properties, something like `child.position?.start?.offset`, which would hopefully just cause that node to be bypassed. but I'm not totally familiar with AST traversal and its implementation here, so I wanted to make sure developers who know this component better than me (like @miukimiu and @chandlerprall  ) would approve of this fix, or have other ideas.

thanks!

author: andrew-goldstein
title: [EuiDataGrid] Quickly pressing the arrow keys triggers an infinite loop
body:
Quickly pressing the arrow keys when a cell in `EuiDataGrid` has focus sometimes causes cell focus to infinitely loop randomly between cells.

- Once the looping starts, clicking on a cell with the mouse exagerates the random looping behavior, but does not stop it
- Pressing the arrow keys doesn't stop the looping

To reproduce (tested with EUI `v36.0.0` in Chome `92.0.4515.107` on OSX `11.4`):

1) Navigate to the `Data Grid` example page: https://eui.elastic.co/#/tabular-content/data-grid

2) Click on an `Account` cell near the center of the table to give it keyboard focus

3) Using the keyboard, rapidly press the arrow keys to enter the [Konami Code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konami_Code):

⬆️  ⬆️  ⬇️  ⬇️  ⬅️  ➡️  ⬅️  ➡️

`UP` `UP` `DOWN` `DOWN` `LEFT` `RIGHT` `LEFT` `RIGHT`

**Expected Results**

- 30 lives
- After the last keypress, the originally selected cell is once-again focused

**Actual Results**

- `G A M E  O V E R`: Focus infinitely loops randomly between cells
- Once the looping starts, clicking on a cell with the mouse exagerates the random looping behavior, but does not stop it
- Pressing the arrow keys doesn't stop the looping

![konami_code](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4459398/126567145-72cf20c9-d70b-433b-81d2-5809e65a14c1.gif)

![up up down down left right left right](https://media.giphy.com/media/4hnQDVKVARZ6w/giphy.gif)

body:
**EuiContextMenu** right now is designed to render inside of a popover (but doesn't strictly need to be). With this, it relies on the consuming developer to put it in **EuiPopover** which can provide some flexibility in styling but also can provide some headache as demonstrated when we were [improving our focus states](https://github.com/elastic/eui/pull/4876#discussion_r651814253).

author: thompsongl
title: [EuiFlyout] Complex types and `styled-components`
body:
_The issue is broader than just EuiFlyout, but it is currently the only one impacted._

EuiFlyout has a very complex type definition. It accepts an element type generic, uses an `as` prop to set the underlying element, and uses `forwardRef`.
In Kibana, it is sometimes _also_ styled with the `styled-components` `styled` API, which incorrectly infers its types and requires some manual type assertion. The error is somewhat opaque, but the fix is to assert with

```ts
const styledFlyout: StyledComponent<typeof EuiFlyout, {}, { children?: ReactNode }> = styled(
  EuiFlyout
)`[...]`
```

Unsure if a solution exists, but a current idea is to also include `PropsWithChildren` in EuiFlyout's type definition.

author: cchaos
title: [Meta][CSS in JS] Possible accessibility features/options to build in
body:
The transfer to applying a theme via JS, gives us the opportunity to have more user-level settings that can affect all of the application. Here are a few:

### Easy:

- [ ] **Font family**: Some disabilities make it hard to read specific font families or their experience can be improved by allowing them to provide a font-family of their choice. Example: Dislexia
- [ ] **Focus rings always on**: Some none keyboard users still might have a better experience if they can always see the current focus.
- [ ] **No motion**: Without relying on an OS-wide setting, they can turn off all transitions/animations.

### Hard:

- [ ] **Increased contrast**: Allow the user to ask for higher than the AA recommended level. This is hard mainly because it requires lots of testing

author: pickypg
title: [EuiCard] onClick loses MouseEvent details
body:
While integrating an EUI with React Router 5.1, I noticed that opening `EuiCard`-based links (by clicking the card itself) in new tabs resulted in the current tab also navigating to the link even though I was actively ignoring `onClick` using the suggested mechanism:

```ts
const isModifiedEvent = (event: MouseEvent) =>
  !!(event.metaKey || event.altKey || event.ctrlKey || event.shiftKey);
```

Upon deeper inspection, I realized that it simply did not recognize that any of those were pressed (on Windows it's normal for `metaKey` to be ignored, but on macOS that's the Command key). Looking at the code, it appears to be because the onClick handler calls the `link.click`, which itself appears unable to passthrough the `MouseEvent`:

As a minor workaround, at the expense of functionality, I have temporarily removed the `href` and `onClick` properties from `EuiCard` and simply leave it to a button in the `footer`.

author: myasonik
title: [EuiSelectableTemplateSitewide] should allow for customizing the `searchValue`
body:
In Kibana, we're adding some advance search options to our global search bar. (https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/74290)

No UI changes, just allowing for some basic query syntax.

Trying to make these changes uncovers two problems:

1. **EuiSelectable** always does its own filtering. This wasn't a problem before when the API was returning results that had a string match to the value so the filtering just returned everything back but with query syntax in the mix, EUI's string match filtering breaks down. This can be mostly turned off by passing in `onSearch: () => {}` into `searchProps` but a filter EUI-side technically does still happen on `componentDidMount` which, though isn't an issue for Kibana now, is still not really desired. 

	_Proposed solution_: add a boolean flag which controls whether or not EUI filters options (flag name totally up in the air, maybe `optionFiltering`?).
	
	_Alternative_: key off of whether or not `onSearch` is passed in and use that as a de facto flag for the above (i.e., if `onSearch` is passed in, disable EUI-side filtering).

2. Using the `onSearch` workaround mentioned above, the rendered options lose the ability to highlight the `searchValue` because `searchValue` as **EuiSelectable** understands it is no longer correct. 
	
	_Proposed solution_: Allow passing in a `searchValue` which will get used in the rendered options for highlighting. (Actually, just implementing this could let us not disable the filtering happening above. This way, basically forcing results to have some representation that can be highlighted from the search value which is probably a good thing.) @cchaos did I understand from the EUI meeting that this is your preferred way forward?

	_Alternative_: If EUI exported `euiSelectableTemplateSitewideRenderOptions` then Kibana could use it as the `renderOption` but pass in any `searchValue` it wants.

CC @chandlerprall @ryankeairns @pgayvallet 

I can start on a PR once I understand what the preferred way forward is.

author: timroes
title: [EuiDataGrid] Separate rendering and sorting from each other
body:
Data grid currently has imho one fundamental technical flaw: we cannot sort on actual values, but only on the "rendered" content of a cell. That makes it at the moment nearly impossible to display and sort any kind of formatted numbers (without doing very large workarounds).

The sorting happens via the `comperator` function of a schema attached to a column. This will get as input the `renderCellValue` output, which actually needs to produce the component that's displayed within the cell. E.g. if you have a column shown a percentage value, the `renderCellValue` will format it as percentage and thus output a value like `0,5 %` (I assumed a German locale here). This will now be put intot he comperator and there is no chance of sorting those values, without trying to string parse them back to numbres, which gets really hard with different locales or more complex cases like percentage formatting. By default it will instead just do the string comparison, which does not sort numbers anyhow meaningful.

Since the sorting has no access to the raw values atm, it's rather useless for anything except strings imho. I think we need to spend some time trying to rethink how this could work and I'd see the following two options:

### Option 1 - The "proper" solution

I think one of the most proper solutions would be, to actually replace `renderCellValue` by a `getCellValue` method, that needs to return the raw value for a specific cell, and instead give the Column Schema a `renderValue(value: T, rowIndex: number)` method instead, that will be used to format a value within this cell. The decorator in this case would get the return value of the `getCellValue` and thus the raw value for sorting and formatting happens only afterwards.

Also it keeps formatting a bit better separated. Currently to have columns with different formatting, you'll often end up with a long `switch` in the `renderCellValue` to cover the different render types.

### Option 2 - The "less breaking" solution

Option 1 will break quit some APIs, and potentially require quite some refactoring. I think there might be an quicker solution, though slightly less clean, that would still make sorting possible. In this case we would extend the `comperator` function to get access to (part of) the `EuiDataGridCellValueElementProps` passed into the `renderCellValue`, so it'll be able to retrieve the raw value itself via the similar logic `renderCellValue` already got it. I think `rowIndex` and `columnId` would already be enough. So the new interface would look like:

```ts
type CellInfoLite = { rowIndex: number; columnId: string; };
// or potentially instead of 
comparator?: (a: string, b: string, direction: 'asc' | 'desc', rawInfo: { a: CellInfoLite, b: CellInfoLite }) => -1 | 0 | 1;
```

This has the advantage we're not breaking any APIs, but therefore still not having a clear separation between value and formatting in data grid.

cc @chandlerprall @kertal

When there's a vertical scrollbar in `EuiDataGrid` it seems like each column width doesn't take this into account and assigns more width per column than the one that's actually available (i.e. 100% - vertical scrollbar width).

We first noticed this in @kertal's datagrid branch for Discover but it's also reproducible in the docs. If you go to the **"Data grid adapts to its container example"** and set it to have only 2 columns you'll see that a horizontal scrollbar is added when it is not needed.

![Screen Recording 2020-10-20 at 11 56 58 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4016496/96631708-83925b00-12cb-11eb-8f9d-8e9a4dfab78b.gif)

author: myasonik
title: [EuiBasicTable] row actions are inaccessible
body: ## Summary When row actions are define, **EuiBasicTable** sets `role=button` onto each `` (which are natively of `role=row` and are within the fairly strict rules of table semantics). The solution largely works for keyboard users but can cause a muck for screen reader users. ## Proposed solutions The ideal solution for clickable rows looks something: ```jsx {name} {phoneNumber} {rowActionButton} ``` With some CSS, you make the rows appear clickable for mouse users but screen reader and keyboard users get deferred to button within a cell. (Also makes the action more obvious to mouse users.) ## Other solutions Defining a structure like that might be a pretty big breaking change for EUI so I'm not sure about the practicalities of it. At the very least, it would be nice if EUI had an official way to create the accessible pattern. Other options that could be explored are visually hidden buttons (but those can cause havoc for keyboard only users, so maybe something like a skiplink where it comes into view on focus?) or some custom gymnastics with a lot of `aria-live` (but this can be brittle and cause further confusion if not clear from the gate).

author: smhutch
title: [EuiSelectable] list not filtered when `onChange` or `onSearch` included in searchProps
body:
When `searchable` and one or more of `searchProps.onChange` and `searchProps.onSearch` is passed to `EuiSelectable`, the options are not correctly filtered in the UI. I created a [sandbox showing both issues](https://codesandbox.io/s/eui-searchprops-issue-report-te3b4?file=/src/index.js).

## Code

I believe in both cases the `searchProps` are being spread over more important props, which seems unintended.

### onChange

https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/01c6986afdd7321f8e86b433be4892345aa7c0fe/src/components/selectable/selectable.tsx#L534-L551

- `onChange={this.onSearchChange}` appears to be key to updating the selectable internal state
- `{...cleanedSearchProps}` overrides it

### onSearch

I'm less sure about the cause of this issue, but have a feeling it could be:

https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/01c6986afdd7321f8e86b433be4892345aa7c0fe/src/components/selectable/selectable_search/selectable_search.tsx#L113-L125

- Same problem as above, where `onSearch` can exist in `...rest` (which comes from `cleanedSearchProps` above), overriding the important call to `this.onSearchChange`

## Context

The feature I'm working on extends the `EuiSelectable` component, by adding "Select all" and "Select none" buttons above the `searchable` `EuiSelectable`. Here's [an example of the UI](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7217244/95881011-04070800-0d70-11eb-8948-0375e052d0a7.png).

This works without any hassle. I update the local `options` state when a user clicks on either button, and pass this state down to `EuiSelectable`. After building this, I realized that it would be a better UX to combine this behaviour with the client-side search offered by adding `searchable`. In my current implementation the user could filter (let's say to view 5 of 100 items), then click "Select all". This would select not only the visible/filtered options, but all of them.

To fix this UX issue, I tried to access the currently filtered items. I found I could do this as shown:

```ts
searchProps={{
  onChange: (filteredOptions) => {
     // here I set some local state. Implementation details not important.
  },
}}
```

Elsewhere, I could use this data to compare the `filteredOptions` and `options`, and work out which `options` should be updated when a user clicks on one of the Select all/none buttons. Again, no problems here.

I believe the data-flow is working fine using the existing props, and the only issue is that my combination of props prevents the `EuiSelectable` from accurately reflecting the search filters in the UI.

author: pgayvallet
title: [EuiInMemoryTable] Add the ability to inject arbitrary content between the searchbar and the table
body:
`EuiInMemoryTable` does not allow to inject content between the search bar and the table components.

In some cases, consumers may need to add an additional section of controls in-between

Adding an additional property to the `EuiInMemoryTable` props to allow to prepend arbitrary react elements before the table, like it is commonly done for many EUI components, such as `toolsLeft` / `toolsRight` for `EuiSearchBar` or `labelAppend` for `EuiFormRow` would answer this need.

related code: https://github.com/elastic/eui/blob/master/src/components/basic_table/in_memory_table.tsx#L678-L683

Context: for Kibana's SavedObjects tagging feature, it is expected to have the number of selected items and the batch actions between the search bar and the table. Implementing this would allow us to be able to use `EuiInMemoryTable` for that instead of reimplementing most of its features just to separate the searchbar from the table.

cc @ryankeairns

author: cchaos
title: Add an EuiTextTruncate component
body:
I've seen a lot of usages of adding our `.euiTextTruncate` or similar mixin or custom implementation in Kibana. Most of these implementations don't add any sort of tooltip or `title` attribute to let users view the whole thing. 

We could provide a utility component that helps users by not just applying the CSS class utility, but also wrapping with an EuiTooltip to always provide the user the ability to read the whole text.

One requirement would mostly likely be that it's children can only be a string because of the way `text-overflow` works.

author: alvarezmelissa87
title: EuiInMemoryTable - request ability to set pageIndex and pageSize externally
body:
We've run into an issue in ML where the `EuiInMemory` table always gets reset to page index `0` regardless of what props are passed in. As a workaround, we've had to use the `EuiBasicTable` with the `EuiSearchBar` and have done our own handling of the search, sorting, and pagination functionality. This results in a lot of extra code the aim of which is to be able to pass in what page index the table should be on when it renders. We've had to add this in 3 places in ML as well as Transforms.

E.g. in the anomaly detection jobs list https://github.com/elastic/kibana/blob/master/x-pack/plugins/ml/public/application/jobs/jobs_list/components/jobs_list/jobs_list.js#L77

It's challenging to maintain a stable items reference as, in ML and Transforms, we do want to keep the jobs/transforms list as up-to-date as possible and we re-fetch the table items frequently resulting in pagination being reset when the contents change at all.

It feels like an indicator that maybe it would be more efficient to have this functionality built into the `EuiInMemoryTable`


#### Docs example use case:

The **In-memory table with search and external state** example in the [docs](https://elastic.github.io/eui/#/tabular-content/in-memory-tables) has an **Online/Offline** column. In the case where you're re-fetching the table items and nothing changes but the **Online/Offline** property - you'd want to be able to update that property and maintain the current page index/size since the items themselves aren't changing.

author: chandlerprall
title: [EuiDataGrid] Document what props cause rows to re-render
body:
There are quite a few props which could cause **EuiDataGrid** to re-render all of the rows (and if `inMemory` is enabled this would be _all_ rows, not only paginated/visible ones). Most are probably not obvious, and debugging which one is causing a performance issue is tedious. These should be documented.

This list is affected by the in-progress virtualization #4170 

The internal `rows` representation is recomputed if these change (struck out items are internal-only and should be more limited in scope),
rowCount,
columns,
inMemory.skipColumns,
renderCellValue,
onCellRender,
~visibleRowIndices~,
~rowMap~,
leadingControlColumns,
trailingControlColumns,
columns,
schema,
popoverContents,
columnWidths,
defaultColumnWidth,
~focusedCell~,
onCellFocus,
~interactiveCellId~,

The impact of each should be evaluated and documented.

author: oatkiller
title: `EUIRadio` with a `label` and no `id` behaves unexpectedly
body:
Hi there. Thanks for the work on EUI. I've really been enjoying using it. I found some behavior that I think is unexpected and threw me for a loop.

If you define an `EuiRadio` with a `label` and no `id`, `onChange` will not be triggered from a click.

```tsx
    <EuiRadio
      label="EUIRadio with a label and no ID"
      onChange={useCallback(() => alert("changed"), [])}
    />
```

Check my [codesandbox](https://codesandbox.io/s/working-eui-3syk0) to see the example.

If the `label` property is passed an HTML `<label />` element will entirely obscure the `<input />` element. The `<label />` element isn't the parent of the `<input />` and so if no `id` attribute associates them, the `click` event on the `<label />` will not trigger a `change` event on the `<input />`.

# Reproduce this
* Create an `EUIRadio` with `label` and `onChange` properties. The `onChange` property should be a function which calls `alert` or runs some other code that you can use to assert that the function ran.
* Load the code in a browser and click the `EUIRadio` component.
* The function will not have run, and no `alert` will be shown.

# Expected
* If the `onChange` property is provided it will be run, even if `label` is provided and `id` is not.
* OR, the `id` should be required if `label` is passed.
* OR, the behavior should be documented

author: mdutourgeerling
title: [EuiOverlayMask] EuiOverlayMask is being mounted twice when using CRA dev server
body:
The EuiOverlayMask div is being mounted twice in the DOM when using Elastic UI with the create-react-app development server. The first one that is mounted is uncontrollable and can't be unmounted anymore.

It seems to be caused because EuiOverlayMask calls `document.body.appendChild(this.overlayMaskNode)` in its constructor instead of in `componentDidMount`.

This issue only occurs when using the create-react-app development server and doesn't occur when the app is built. This makes me think that something like `react-hot-loader` is creating an extra instance of EuiOverlayMask without mounting it anywhere. 

I was able to fix it by changing EuiOverlayMask to call `appendChild` in `componentDidMount` instead.

The issue also occurs with other components that use a portal and mount it in the constructor (e.g. EuiPortal).

author: pranshuchittora
title: Publish individual components as scoped packages
body:
**Description**
Shipping `eui` components as scoped packages.

---

Right now the `eui` ships as a single unit which has a huge surface area of `45.5MB`, as per NPM.
![Screenshot from 2020-03-30 01-07-10](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32242596/77858752-1467f300-7223-11ea-8f04-b856d3bf10e5.png)

Say someone wants to just consume the button component, but he's been shipped with table components as well. Though he can use tree shaking to remove unused code, this depends on the user's configuration. This would also help eui to be served over cdn, where we can ask for individual components on demand by adding script tags.

This would also allow to colocate any bugs into individual components, which can be fixed and released independently. 

The idea is to break the entire codebase into smaller packages, possibly lerna packages which can colocate in the same mono-repo and published individually.
```
-- packages
 -- @eui/icons
 -- @eui/form
 -- @eui/table
 -- ..
 -- @eui/core
```

Dividing the dependency into scoped packages will make it more reasonable and feasible.

Would love to discuss :loudspeaker:

title: [EuiProgress] Allow `max` property to be undefined
body:
Spent some time chatting in Slack about this, and was advised to make an issue. Here's the summary of the problem:

The `max` property alleges that it accepts either a number, or undefined, which checks out when I do either of these:
```js
<EuiProgress max={100} />
<EuiProgress max={undefined} />
```

.. but TypeScript fails to compile when I do this:
```js
<EuiProgress max={someCondition ? 100 : undefined} />
```

This doesn't seem to be a TypeScript bug or anything, since this [pared-down example](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play/?jsx=2&ssl=20&ssc=13&pln=20&pc=22#code/LAKAlgtgDg9gTgFwAQCUCmBDAxsgZnGCJAcjkx2IG5RQ0APWRJMAOwTTl2zSQAUCoAZyQBvUEiQB6AFTSkAFQAWPAK6COxYSwwQe0yeKTbdALiSCEcVgHMkAHyQqWAEzS5WaZ9RABfGiCwYFgs+KzYAOR00M3RsBAA6ADEAYQAefhghAD4kAF4kAAooAUEASjycsRAJMgQVOBZCwwlU5zAANyzmiSRUqCyRYszBeOM0H1TJfu7Jts7DUtA-EFBA4ORBQjRkoLaEMCC8pC4AG3VvVaCQgGVFGAB3AFV1OBjyBJT0kpz8opLy3KVbq1eqNL6sBCRXRGKK5ETmLY7FxgfaHAD8SAAROFPJikGYnK53CxPD4pF1fP4gA) still works.

I was able to solve this temporarily by just doing this:
```js
{someCondition ? (
  <EuiProgress max={100} />
) : (
   <EuiProgress />
)}
```

But I'd like to request that `max` really would accept `undefined` so that `max={someCondition ? 100 : undefined}` would work. Thanks!

author: pranshuchittora
title: feat: Add debouncing to all the input components.
body:
### Description
Debouncing is a common technique used to decrease the frequent calls to the heavy functions/callbacks.

### How it can be used in `eui`?
As forms are one of the core building blocks of the UI, there can be a lot of fields(input) and those filed might react to the user input. Sometimes the performing those changes might take time.
Like
- API calls based on user input
- Search/Filter


As JavaScript is a single-threaded language, their frequent callbacks will push a lot of functions calls to the call stack which in turn decrease the performance & may create jitterily UI and in worst case freeze the UI.

Most vulnerable components are `Sliders`, components reacting to resizing...

### How to solve the above-mentioned problem?
The problem can be easily solved by passing those on change calls via the debounce function.


`onChange -> debounce() -> handleChange `

author: chandlerprall
title: EuiResizeObserver fallback does not work for pure resizing
body:
Discovered while working on #2991

Safari and IE11 are the two browsers we support which do not have `ResizeObserver`. For those, we fall back to a `MutationObserver` watching for all changes. While that catches when mutation cause a different size, it incorrectly:

* misses size changes caused by a window resize
* catches content changes that do not affect size
* misses size changes caused by changes in a document's CSS

I don't think we should try addressing the third one, but wanted to include it for completeness. The other two should be fixed by changing the fallback to:

* listen for `resize` events
* confirm that a newly computed size is, in fact, different from the previously known one

author: myasonik
title: `NavDrawer` is too restrictive about its child element
body:
## Summary
`NavDrawer` only allows a specific whitelist of children (not sure exactly what it is) primarily: `< />` and `NavDrawerGroup`.

This makes it difficult to break up large navs because you can't wrap parts of it in a component even if that component returns a `NavDrawerGroup`.

One workaround is to call the component as a function instead of trying to render it as a component. Other than looking hacky and being difficult to debug, I'm not sure if there are any other React-related side effects to doing that.

## Pseudo-example
Given a component:
```jsx
function Group() { return <EuiNavDrawerGroup /> };
```

This works:
```jsx
function Nav() {
	return <EuiNavDrawer>{Group()}</EuiNavDrawer>
}
```

While this does not:
```jsx
function Nav() {
	return <EuiNavDrawer><Group /></EuiNavDrawer>
}
```

title: [Data Grid] Data grid overflows in flex box

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/230104/70517526-fde54100-1b38-11ea-9584-351599555840.png)

Within `EuiFlexItem`, the data grid only adapts to the container width if the flex item has a hard coded width. If the width is not set or a percentage, data grid will outgrow it.

----

title: Indicating external links in EUI
body:
The Cloud docs team have expressed a wish for us to have a clear indication in the UI for when a link is going to an External site.

It's my opinion that this is something that should be better handled in EUI, perhaps as simple as an optional "opt-in" `external` prop on `euiLink` or an "opt-out" prop on `euiLink` whenever there's a `target='_blank'`. We discussed it briefly in the latest Design meeting and it seems as though this is something that other products have struggled with too.

Cloud devs have already put together a solution that can be used in the short term until we're able to get a longer-term solution into EUI that can ensure more consistency across all our products.

author: snide
title: [WIP SPEC] Inline markdown+ editor that supports embeddable content
body:
Strawman for conversation. This is a work in progress

## Summary

We need a block level editor that aids in displaying written (markdown) text next to included embeddables from within Kibana applications. The primary use case is for user commenting and incident note taking during an investigation, but this component should be generic enough to work as a drop in anytime we're asking the user to add text content into our applications.

## Basic feature list

### Markdown should be the primary method for composition

From an editing level, we'd like to use markdown for composition, likely using Github flavored markdown if possible. We already have the styling CSS for the render level for this in Kibana and should be able to re-utilize that work.

### We should support syntax highlighting by default for any code blocks in the content

Writing code snippets will likely be common in this interface. We should make sure that syntax highlighting is provided be default. My guess is we might want to overtake the markdown rendered and replace it with `EuiCodeBlock` similar to how we overtake `EuiLink` within Kibana now when rendering markdown.

### There should be two distinct modes (edit mode, render mode)

We are not providing a traditional WYSIWYG experience where you edit inside of a rendered view. The two modes will be distinct, and you should do your editing while within the edit mode. When viewing that content, you would do that in the render mode, switching between the two modes until you are happy with the result.

While in edit mode you essentially have two things you can do:

1. Write markdown content
2. Include or arrange `embeds` that are self-contained content coming from an outside source (presumably a kibana application).

In the render view we would handle the rendering of the markdown, but provide the necessary api layer to transpile your `embed` snippet contained in the edit code into a provided render layer. At its simplest, this render layer might just be the embed `type` and the the `id`, but at its most complex would have a prop like interface for providing various attributes to augment that embed . 

### We should assume "block" level editing and rearranging

We should assume this editor creates linear "blocks" of content that might need to be reordered during composition within a known container. You should be able to drag and drop these blocks after composition into an order that makes sense.

![image](http://snid.es/51b182615e2a/Screen%252520Recording%2525202019-06-17%252520at%25252009.59%252520AM.gif)

### Available embeds need to be discoverable through menus, and probably should have a special, limited render type within edit mode

We should not assume composers will know the shorthand to compose embeds, and therefor need to provide menu systems within composition that direct people to the available embeds for this particular usage of the editor.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/324519/59623804-014bc280-90ea-11e9-818f-af1bf9ad345f.png)

My guess is that we'd want to show these embed snippets in the editor in a way that can not be directly edited through the code, doing something to the below where we represent the embed as some sort of un-editable tag.

![](http://snid.es/3bc503f839a5/Screen%252520Recording%2525202019-06-17%252520at%25252010.43%252520AM.gif)

![](http://snid.es/f4edee269a89/Screen%252520Recording%2525202019-06-17%252520at%25252010.29%252520AM.gif)

### Embeds should display live content

Embeds should render live on request. The idea is that this content is reference based and if you change the reference, or the data that backs it, the embed itself should reflect the change. We are not storing copies of the content.

### Data should be an AST format

Again, we don't want to follow the traditional WYSIWYG pattern of storing and rendering HTML in a content editable way. Let's use AST trees for this and allow the consuming en
