author: anirudha
title: RFC: OpenSearch Dashboards MCP Server (OSD-MCP)
body:
## 1. Summary

Build a **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** server for **OpenSearch Dashboards** that enables LLM agents and AI copilots to **discover, query, explain, create, and fix** observability assets (logs/metrics/traces) with **PPL** and DQL—safely and efficiently—while honoring **Dashboards multi-tenancy** and OpenSearch Security RBAC.


- Treating **PPL** as a first-class query language (logs/metrics/traces).
- Exposing **Saved Objects** (dashboards, visualizations, saved searches, data views) with **summary / property / patch** ergonomics across all types, not only dashboards.
- Providing **tenant-aware** operations 
- Shipping **Observability-specific tools** (Trace Analytics, Alerts/Monitors, Annotations).
- Publishing **context-efficient resources** (field caps, schema samples, compact summaries) to minimize LLM token usage.

---

## 2. Motivation

- **AI-native workflows need APIs shaped for LLMs.** Current REST APIs are too verbose; LLMs benefit from summaries, small property fetches, and safe patch tools.
- **PPL coverage is missing in existing MCP servers.** OD-MCP unlocks OpenSearch Observability with native PPL.
- **Multi-tenancy and RBAC are table stakes.** We require tenant/space scoping and least-privilege defaults.
- **Operator safety.** Guardrails (time-bounded queries, byte/row caps, dry-runs) reduce blast radius.

---

## 3. Goals & Non-Goals

### Goals
- First-class **PPL** execution with explainers and safe defaults.
- Read/write access to **Saved Objects** using **summary → property → patch** flows.
- **Tenant-aware** RBAC with optional SigV4.
- Observability surfaces: **Trace Analytics**, **Alerts/Monitors**, **Annotations**.
- Link helpers for **Discover** and **Dashboards** with prefilled queries/time.

### Non-Goals
- Full parity with every Dashboards plugin at GA.
- Arbitrary raw storage admin (index mgmt, cluster admin).
- Language-model hosting or prompt-engineering guidance (client concern).

---

## 4. User Stories

1. **Triage an incident** with an AI agent:
   - Agent lists top erroring services (PPL), opens a Discover link scoped to 24h, adds an annotation.
2. **Fix a dashboard title/panel** safely:
   - Agent fetches dashboard summary, reads a single property via JSONPath, produces a **preview diff**, then patches.
3. **Create a minimal viz from PPL**:
   - Agent runs PPL, infers chart type, creates a saved visualization, and returns a dashboard link with time preset.

---

## 5. High-Level Design

### 5.1 Architecture

```
+----------------------+         +--------------------------+
|   LLM Client / IDE   | <MCP>   |   OD-MCP Server          |
|  (Claude, VS Code)   | <-----> |  (TS/Go, HTTP over MCP)  |
+----------------------+         +------------+-------------+
                                              |
                                              | REST / (optional gRPC 3.0+)
                                              v
                                     +---------------------+
                                     | OpenSearch          |
                                     | + Dashboards        |
                                     | + Security (RBAC)   |
                                     +---------------------+
```

- **Server:** TypeScript or Go. Implements MCP **resources** (read-only context) and **tools** (actions).
- **Backends:** OpenSearch Dashboards REST; OpenSearch REST (and gRPC where available).
- **Auth:** Dashboards cookie/API key/OIDC; OpenSearch Basic/OIDC/SigV4.
- **Multi-tenancy:** Tenant/space scoping on all calls.

### 5.2 Capabilities Overview

| Area | OD-MCP (this RFC) |
|---|---|
| Query | **PPL** (native), DQL (Discover-aligned) |
| Saved Objects | dashboards, visualizations, saved searches, data views |
| Ergonomics | **summary / property(JSONPath) / patch(JSON Patch or Merge Patch)** |
| Observability | Trace search, Alerts/Monitors list/ack, Annotations |
| Links | Deep links to Discover/Dashboard/Panel with time & variables |
| Security

Vulnerability Details

Axios is a promise based HTTP client for the browser and Node.js. When Axios prior to versions 0.30.2 and 1.12.0 runs on Node.js and is given a URL with the "data:" scheme, it does not perform HTTP. Instead, its Node http adapter decodes the entire payload into memory ("Buffer"/"Blob") and returns a synthetic 200 response. This path ignores "maxContentLength" / "maxBodyLength" (which only protect HTTP responses), so an attacker can supply a very large "data:" URI and cause the process to allocate unbounded memory and crash (DoS), even if the caller requested "responseType: 'stream'". Versions 0.30.2 and 1.12.0 contain a patch for the issue.

body:
**Describe the bug**

After taking a snapshot from a data stream index, if one were to try to restore a data stream snapshot, it claims to be restored... but it is not visible to a pre-existing index pattern in Dashboards.  Its marked as 'hidden', and has the same name as the prior index name... but you cannot see any data in the histogram of the Discover mode or find data.

Interestingly, if you simple 'close' the original index, and then perform a snapshot restore... the index continues to appears closed, but the data can be seen in Dashboards as expected.

I am reporting this as a bug... but I'm actually not sure its a bug.   There are no errors reported in any of this process that are visible on any node in the cluster.  However, There is also no documentation that I can find suggesting that data streams may work differently with snapshots than other indexes.  If this is intended behavior, maybe this is just a documentation problem?


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Take a snapshot of a data stream index (.ds-<name>-<num>).  It is helpful to use one in the middle of a series of them to make the data easier to spot if its missing.
2. Delete the original index
3. Try to restore the stream from the snapshot
4. See if you can see the data in Discover.


**Expected behavior**
I would simply expect that one of the following behaviors would occur
1. The data would be restored, to the original data stream index name, and that data would be usable again in Dashboards
2. An error or warning would occur to suggest that the data was restored in a way that it would not be visible


**OpenSearch Version**
3.1

**Dashboards Version**
3.0

**Plugins**

opensearch-alerting
opensearch-anomaly-detection
opensearch-asynchronous-search
opensearch-cross-cluster-replication
opensearch-custom-codecs
opensearch-flow-framework
opensearch-geospatial
opensearch-index-management
opensearch-job-scheduler
opensearch-knn
opensearch-ltr
opensearch-ml
opensearch-neural-search
opensearch-notifications
opensearch-notifications-core
opensearch-observability
opensearch-performance-analyzer
opensearch-reports-scheduler
opensearch-search-relevance
opensearch-security
opensearch-security-analytics
opensearch-skills
opensearch-sql
opensearch-system-templates
opensearch-ubi
query-insights


**Screenshots**

N/A

**Host/Environment (please complete the following information):**
RHEL 9 on a on-prem intel-based server
Opensearch 3.1 installed from RPMs downloaded from opensearch.org

**Additional context**

I discovered this while attempting to do "restores" using remote snapshots from an attached NFS partition.  The same problem exists and there are also no warnings or errors that anything went wrong.  I have circumvented this issue by using the following snapshot restore parameters to both make the restored index available to the existing Index Pattern configured in Dashboards.  In the example below... (assuming the index to be restored is something like ".ds-foobar-000001", and the index pattern in Dashboards is configured as "foobar*" ) :
{
"rename_pattern": ".ds-(.+)",
"rename_replacement":"foobar-$1",
"storage_type": "remote_snapshot",
"index_settings": { "hidden":"false"}
} 
However... this is not something that can be done in the UI as part of the ISM process at the moment.  Not to mention the whole convert_local_to_remote policy isn't well documented to explain what exactly that policy does in the context of a data stream.

author: ruanyl
title: [Workspace] Enable workspace by default for future OpenSearch-Dashboards distribution
body: ## Background Workspace is an OSD feature which allows user to create different workspaces by selecting use cases for different purposes, this also enables users to organize visuals(stored in saved_objects), such as dashboards and visualizations in a logical way which categorized by workspaces. The initial workspace implementation was introduced in `2.14.0` and rapidly evolved to `2.19.0`, during the release cycle, a lot of UI/UX enhancements introduced together with workspace, including the new look & feel, new homepage design, etc. Related configurations: ```yaml workspace.enabled: true data_source.enabled: true savedObjects.permission.enabled: true #optional opensearchDashboards.dashboardAdmin.users: ['admin'] #optional uiSettings: overrides: 'home:useNewHomePage': true ``` Screenshot: --- Creating this issue to discuss the possibility to enable workspace and the UI/UX improvements for future OpenSearch-Dashboards distributions. ## Known issues 1. Workspace conceptually overlap with multi-tenancy, though technically they can work together. 2. When enabling workspace, it would require data migration for the existing saved objects

author: pep1t0
title: [Feature Request] Add a countdown timer for auto-refresh intervals in Dashboards
body:
Hello OpenSearch Dashboards Team,

I would like to propose a feature enhancement for the auto-refresh functionality in OpenSearch Dashboards.

Current Behavior:
When enabling the “Refresh every” option to automatically refresh dashboards at a specified interval, the dashboard refreshes accordingly. However, there is no visible countdown timer or indicator within the dashboard UI that shows how much time is remaining before the next automatic refresh.

Proposed Feature:
Add a visible countdown timer or progress indicator in the dashboard interface (e.g., in the top bar near the auto-refresh control) that clearly displays the time remaining until the next automatic refresh. This feature would provide users with a better sense of timing and control over the refresh cycles without guessing or manually tracking time.

Benefits:

Improved user experience by giving clear feedback about refresh intervals

Enhanced situational awareness when monitoring live or near real-time data

Reduced user uncertainty, especially in cases with longer refresh intervals

Additional Context:
Similar functionality is common in other data visualization tools and dashboards and is highly appreciated by users who rely on timely data updates.

Thank you for considering this enhancement. I believe it would be a valuable addition to OpenSearch Dashboards.

title: After a login timeout occurs, search criteria on the "Discover" view is lost
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

When I'm using the Discover view, leave the tab for a bit, return to that tab and try to use it again I often find that my session has expired. I'm fine with user sessions expiring as a security measure BUT it is super annoying that when this happens all of my search criteria is lost and I have to navigate back to the Discover view only to find that I have to select the timeframe again and reenter all of my search criteria.

Note that [this other issue](https://github.com/opensearch-project/security-dashboards-plugin/issues/159) aims to reduces the frequency that user session expiry occurs. I suspect that some of the folks that want a fix to that one are really motivated by the inconvenience of losing the state of their Discover view.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

I'm open to other solutions but this might work:

Don't navigate the user away from the Discover view when they re-authenticate. Pop up a modal that forces them to log in and then once the session cookie is established hide the modal so that they're still on the Discover view with all of their search selections still present.

author: joshuali925
title: [RFC] Integrate Automated AI-based Code Reviews
body:
## Summary

This RFC proposes the integration of Amazon Q Developer as an automated AI-assisted code review tool within OpenSearch-Dashboards PR workflow to complement human reviews. The purpose is to reduce code review effort and improve code quality. While it would still require efforts from maintainers to merge the PR, AI-assisted review comments can be a good starting point.

## Problem Statement

Code review is often a time-consuming and tedious process. Maintainers spend a lot of time reviewing PRs, but sometimes they might miss potential problems or not able get to PRs quick enough. PRs not reviewed in time often become staled with conflicts, which wastes development effort and delays potential features and bug fixes.

Currently there are over 100+ open PRs in this repo, the oldest PR is from 2 years ago. 

## Proposed Solution

Integrate Amazon Q Developer as an automated AI-based code review assistant within our PR workflow. This integration would:

- Automatically scan all PRs for common issues and vulnerability
- Highlight areas that might need human reviewer attention
- Suggest fixes for each comment that developers can accept

I proposed Amazon Q Developer because it's easy to setup and free to use for now. I have integrated Amazon Q Developer in my fork and tested its review on some PRs:
- https://github.com/joshuali925/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/7 (upstream #9953)
- https://github.com/joshuali925/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/8 (upstream #9975)
- https://github.com/joshuali925/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/1 (large diff test)

From what I see, the results are not very impressive. For example, it calls out `Lack of error handling for potential undefined or null values in nested object access` on `request.params?.body?.query?.queries?.[0]` which is protected against NPE, and gives incorrect fixes in https://github.com/joshuali925/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/7#discussion_r2167725056.

But it also points out real issues although incorrect reason for comparing `undefined === 0` in https://github.com/joshuali925/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/1#discussion_r2167573220. _(If `searchProps` is undefined, because undefined does not strictly equal `0`, it will render the else block with `ReactExpressionRenderer` and cause NPE)_
https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/5bd7642b9ebf84600d9e074200ce351bc1b62bab/src/plugins/explore/public/embeddable/explore_embeddable_component.tsx#L31-L41

It seems the Amazon Q Developer review is matching code patterns based on a list of rules, and it does not understand suggestion diff format well that most suggestions cannot be directly applied. But sometimes it points out code where there might be problems.

## Implementation Details

This needs to be added by admins, I opened an issue in .github: https://github.com/opensearch-project/.github/issues/342

## Request for Developer Feedback

1. Does integrating Amazon Q help the review process or does it introduce too much noise from your perspective?
2. Is there a solution that provides better results or you would like to use?

## Alternatives Considered

- https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/using-github-copilot/code-review/using-copilot-code-review: this requires premium requests with monthly per-person quota
- https://github.com/qodo-ai/pr-agent: this is an open source solution that requires custom API providers

title: [BUG] Prometheus Data source index is not created
body: **Describe the bug** When a new valid Prometheus data source is created then no data index is created for it. Consider `docker-compose` configuration with security from https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/9915 Technically, the issue is reproducible without security as well, but for the sake of completeness we will be using demo security configuration because the `admin` user has `all_access` privs which include `cluster:admin/*` which covers all the [required privs for data-sources](https://docs.opensearch.org/docs/latest/security/access-control/permissions#data-source-permissions) according to official documentation. ```shell # Previous docker cleanup: # docker rm `docker ps -a -q` # docker volume rm `docker volume ls -q` docker-compose -f docker-compose.yml up ``` Once all services are up access Dashbaords at `http://localhost:5601`. To enter the OpenSearch Dashboards use the following admin credentials: `admin`/`Sup13#!P1##w0rd`. Navigate to **Manage** -> **Data sources** -> **Create direct query connection** and select **Prometheus**. Fill in the form, notice the Prometheus URI `http://prometheus:9090`: New data source is created, click the Prometheus data source: and ignore https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/9917 if it happens (in which case navigate to **Data sources** in the left hand list and select Prometheus data source again). Go to **Query data** and in the **Metrics source** drop-down list select **Prometheus**. You will be presented with list of many **Available metrics** (the Prometheus has been scraping itself from the `docker-compose` start). However, there is not data for any of those available metrics. You can compare specific metrics in the Prometheus web UI and Dashboards web UI. For example we can compare Prometheus chart for `prometheus_http_requests_total` metric and Dashboards chart: I think the main problem here is that the data from Prometheus is not pulled into data source assigned index. We can pull the data source configuration from OpenSearch: ``` curl -k -X GET https://localhost:9200/_plugins/_query/_datasources -u admin:Sup13#\!P1##w0rd ``` The only data source: ```json [ { "name": "Prometheus", "description": "", "connector": "PROMETHEUS", "allowedRoles": [], "properties": { "prometheus.auth.type": "basicauth", "prometheus.uri": "http://prometheus:9090" }, "resultIndex": "query_execution_result_prometheus", "status": "ACTIVE" } ] ``` According to this configuration the Prometheus data should be found in `query_execution_result_prometheus` index but there is not such index: ``` curl -k -X GET https://localhost:9200/_cat/indices -u admin:Sup13#\!P1##w0rd green open .opensearch-observability _kFmSF6_SGGq5eD4urZh2A 1 0 0 0 208b 208b green open .plugins-ml-config szpWcXyVSG-KSiAHdOIaiw 1 0 1 0 3.9kb 3.9kb green open .ql-datasources a6r518F_Qy-7-CIimqd9hQ 1 0 1 0 6.7kb 6.7kb green open .kibana_92668751_admin_1 U8bZIFrWQsKwhV1F4n_uyw 1 0 1 0 5.1kb 5.1kb yellow open security-auditlog-2025.06.17 h38Ze9QDR9G0ta1LMGamjg 1 1 68 0 208.5kb 208.5kb green open .opendistro_security lWJKn4VbTyGxE236LG3WCw 1 0 10 0 80.9kb 80.9kb green open .kibana_1 vVy9A4tPS0OPqdWKoRT03g 1 0 0 0 208b 208b ``` Just for tran

author: lukas-vlcek
title: [Meta] Docker-compose configs for Prometheus data-source integration
body:
This is a META ticket.

This ticket define two common `docker-compose` configurations that consists of:
- Single **OpenSearch** node
- Single **OpenSearch Dashboards** node
- Single **Prometheus** service

The first configuration does not use any security, the second configuration uses the demo OpenSearch security. They are used in follow up tickets:
- #9916 
- #9917
- #9918 

These configurations use OpenSearch version `2.17.1` but in some follow-up tickets different versions of OpenSearch can be used as well (`2.19.2` or `3.0.0` - _pay attention to this please_).

Prometheus is always the latest version.

## Without Security

File: `docker-compose-no-security.yml`

```yml
services:
  opensearch-node1: # This is also the hostname of the container within the Docker network (i.e. https://opensearch-node1/)
    image: opensearchproject/opensearch:2.17.1
    container_name: opensearch-node1
    environment:
      - cluster.name=opensearch-cluster # Name the cluster
      - node.name=opensearch-node1 # Name the node that will run in this container
      - discovery.type=single-node
      - bootstrap.memory_lock=true # Disable JVM heap memory swapping
      - "OPENSEARCH_JAVA_OPTS=-Xms512m -Xmx512m" # Set min and max JVM heap sizes to at least 50% of system RAM
      - "DISABLE_INSTALL_DEMO_CONFIG=true"
      - "DISABLE_SECURITY_PLUGIN=true"
      - "plugins.query.datasources.encryption.masterkey=5e3dc78f06ef582dedbb5154"
    ulimits:
      memlock:
        soft: -1 # Set memlock to unlimited (no soft or hard limit)
        hard: -1
      nofile:
        soft: 65536 # Maximum number of open files for the opensearch user - set to at least 65536
        hard: 65536
    volumes:
      - opensearch-data1:/usr/share/opensearch/data # Creates volume called opensearch-data1 and mounts it to the container
    ports:
      - 9200:9200 # REST API
      - 9600:9600 # Performance Analyzer
    networks:
      - opensearch-net # All of the containers will join the same Docker bridge network
  opensearch-dashboards:
    image: opensearchproject/opensearch-dashboards:2.17.1 # Make sure the version of opensearch-dashboards matches the version of opensearch installed on other nodes
    container_name: opensearch-dashboards
    ports:
      - 5601:5601 # Map host port 5601 to container port 5601
    expose:
      - "5601" # Expose port 5601 for web access to OpenSearch Dashboards
    environment:
      - data_source.enabled=true
      - 'OPENSEARCH_HOSTS=["http://opensearch-node1:9200"]' # Define the OpenSearch nodes that OpenSearch Dashboards will query
      - "DISABLE_SECURITY_DASHBOARDS_PLUGIN=true"
    networks:
      - opensearch-net
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus
    ports:
      - 9090:9090
    expose:
      - "9090"
    networks:
      - opensearch-net

volumes:
  opensearch-data1:

networks:
  opensearch-net:
```

## With Security

File: `docker-compose.yml`

```yml
services:
  opensearch-node1: # This is also the hostname of the container within the Docker network (i.e. https://opensearch-node1/)

author: annuaicoder
title: [BUG] Plugin Configuration Changes Require Restart – Lack of Hot Reload Support
body:
Currently, when modifying the configuration for various OpenSearch Dashboards plugins (such as opensearch_security, customBranding, or other third-party extensions), the changes do not take effect unless the entire Dashboards instance is restarted. This results in reduced operational efficiency, unnecessary downtime, and confusion, especially when changes appear to be applied but are not reflected in the UI or behavior.

Steps to Reproduce:

Install and configure a plugin (e.g., OpenSearch Security or Custom Branding).

Apply a change to its configuration in opensearch_dashboards.yml (e.g., update logo, title, authentication setting).

Reload the Dashboards page in the browser.

Observe that the changes do not take effect until the server is manually restarted.

Expected Behavior:
Plugin configuration changes should either:

Apply dynamically without requiring a server restart (hot reload), or

Be accompanied by a clear indication (in logs or UI) that a restart is required for changes to take effect.

Actual Behavior:
Changes silently fail to take effect until the instance is restarted, which can lead to misconfiguration, wasted debugging time, and service interruption.

Impact:

Increases administrative overhead in production environments.

Causes confusion due to lack of feedback or documentation.

Interrupts workflows that require frequent plugin tweaks (e.g., during staging/testing).

Suggested Solution:

Implement hot-reloading support for plugin configurations where feasible.

Clearly document and surface which configurations require restart, possibly with warnings in logs or UI.

Environment:

OpenSearch Dashboards version: [insert version, e.g., 2.13.0]

Operating System: [e.g., Ubuntu 22.04]

Plugins used: [List any relevant plugins]

Browser: [e.g., Chrome 123, Firefox 117]

Additional Context:
This limitation is not clearly documented in the official guides or plugin README files. Adding hot-reload support (or warnings) would align OpenSearch Dashboards more closely with modern UX expectations and reduce maintenance overhead.

The middleware can either work with the physical filesystem when reading the files or it can use a virtualized in-memory "memfs" filesystem. If "writeToDisk" configuration option is set to "true", the physical filesystem is used. The "getFilenameFromUrl" method is used to parse URL and build the local file path. The public path prefix is stripped from the URL, and the "unsecaped" path suffix is appended to the "outputPath". As the URL is not unescaped and normalized automatically before calling the midlleware, it is possible to use "%2e" and "%2f" sequences to perform path traversal attack. Developers using "webpack-dev-server" or "webpack-dev-middleware" are affected by the issue. When the project is started, an attacker might access any file on the developer's machine and exfiltrate the content. If the development server is listening on a public IP address (or "0.0.0.0"), an attacker on the local network can access the local files without any interaction from the victim (direct connection to the port). If the server allows access from third-party domains, an attacker can send a malicious link to the victim. When visited, the client side script can connect to the local server and exfiltrate the local files. Starting with fixed versions 7.1.0, 6.1.2, and 5.3.4, the URL is unescaped and normalized before any further processing.

title: [BUG] Custom Branding Asset Unavailability Causes OpenSearch Dashboards UI to Hang or Fail to Load
body:
Describe the bug

When using custom branding in OpenSearch Dashboards (e.g., opensearch_security.ui.basicauth.login.brandimage, opensearchDashboards.branding.logo, faviconUrl, etc.), if the external server hosting these branding assets (logos, icons) becomes unreachable, the Dashboards UI does not load properly.     Try to access the Dashboards login page (/app/login).

Expected behavior

OpenSearch Dashboards should:

    Fall back gracefully if the branding URLs are unreachable.

    Not block UI rendering due to unreachable images or branding assets.

author: gaobinlong
title: [BUG] Data source client should honor the timeout settings in opensearch_dashboards.yml
body:
**Describe the bug**

For now, the data source opensearch client doesn't honor the `opensearch.requestTimeout` settings in the yaml file, so the [timeout is 30s by default](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/0fed5eb1a95ba4c143bd48ae1f9508dc21c739bf/src/plugins/data_source/server/client/client_config.ts#L62) even though a bigger value is set in the yaml file, this makes users confused.

We should make the data source opensearch client honor the timeout settings specified in the yaml file.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Set `opensearch.requestTimeout` to 120s in the yaml file.
2. Trigger a search request in Discover page against a OpenSearch cluster which runs in debug mode an will sleep 65s when searching.
3. After 2 minutes, you can see that there's a frontend error 'Failed to fetch', which is not as expected, the search request should get response from OpenSearch after 65s. So why we wait 2 minutes, that's because the node server will retry the search request 3 times if the first request didn't get response after the default timeout 30s, so after 4*30s=120s, the frontend still cannot get any response, an error 'Failed to fetch' is thrown.

**Expected behavior**
 The data source opensearch client honor the timeout settings specified in the yaml file.

**Describe the bug**

As of v2.19.1, when using the OpenSearch Dashboards REST API and `zstd` is in the `Accept-Encoding` headers, the response from the OpenSearch Dashboards API hangs.

This seems very similar to https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/issues/17339

Have seen this breaking when using [traefik](https://traefik.io/) as a proxy which seems to automatically insert zstd into the header.  This means that OpenSearch Dashboards will not work with traefik.

author: kavilla
title: [BUG][tracking] Saved Search: Inconsistent Loading Behavior in Discover
body:
## Description

We are tracking an inconsistency in how saved searches behave in the Discover plugin. Users are experiencing different results depending on how they access their saved searches. 

Please help us understand the impact by adding a 👍🏼  reaction if you're experiencing this issue.

**STATUS**:              `Under active investigation`
**WORKAROUND**: `No current workaround available`
**PREREQUISITES**: 
 -`query:enhancements:enabled` must be set to `true` in Advanced Settings
or 
    - snapshot URL created from with a saved search

## Known Impact
Impacts direct/indirect loading of saved searches.

**Direct Loading**: When accessing a saved search through OpenSearch's standard navigation paths (Discover menu, saved objects list, dashboard panels) where the application has full context of the saved search configuration
> _example_: User clicks on a saved search titled "Error Logs" from the Discover sidebar
> _expected_: Saved search should load with all configured filters, and field selections intact

**Indirect Loading**: Accessing a saved search through external paths where the application needs to rebuild the search context (shared URLs, browser navigation, session restore)
> _example_: User opens a shared saved search snapshot URL in a new browser tab
> _expected_: Saved search should maintain the updates made by the user at the time of the snapshot url was created

### Issues
- Inconsistent (direct/indirect) loading of the following:
  - Query
  - Saved filters
  - Selected columns
- Snapshot URL prioritizing saved search over snapshot updates 

### Affected Versions
- `^2.16.0`
- Please comment if you're seeing this in other versions

## Additional Context

If you're experiencing this issue, it would be helpful to include in comments:
- Your access method (direct/indirect)
- OSD version
- Browser type and version
- Steps to reproduce the inconsistency

Please react with 👍🏼 to help us track impact. Please add a comment with your specific use case if it differs from the examples

We'll update this issue as we make progress on the investigation.

author: yubonluo
title: [RFC] Integrate Identity Source Service into Dashboards
body:
# Overview
In the current OpenSearch Dashboards (OSD), users can only obtain identity information through the "Internal users" page provided by the Security Plugin. However, after introducing workspace feature, there is no existing mechanism to obtain identity information when assigning collaborators to a workspace, which makes it difficult to avoid manual input. Meanwhile, users are also unable to obtain identity information that may come from other services in the future (such as AWS).

To address the above challenges, the following service need to be used: The Identity Source Service is a core service designed to manage handlers for various identity sources. It allows developers to register and access identity source handlers, which are responsible for performing identity-specific operations.

**Goals**
 - Provide a centralized service for managing identity source handlers.
 - Enable flexible registration and retrieval of handlers for diverse identity sources.
 - Allow extensibility for custom identity sources.

# Requirements

For user:
 - I should obtain the identity information when I assign some users/groups to a workspace.

For developer:
 - I should have the ability to register my identity source.
 - I should have the ability to obtain identity information from my identity source.

# Out of scope
 - Login OSD as anonymous.
 - Login in OSD with google account.
 - Identity information saved in other datasources other than local_cluster.

# API Design
The Identity Entries API provides endpoints to obtain identity information from various identity sources. It supports retrieving identities based on type, pagination, filtering, and fetching specific identities by their IDs.

## Base Path
All API endpoints are prefixed with:
```
/security/identity/_entries
```
## 1. Get Identity Entries
### Endpoint
```
GET /api/security/identity/_entries
```
### Description
Obtain identity entries from the specified identity source with optional pagination and filtering.

### Request Query

Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description
-- | -- | -- | -- | --
source | string | ✅ | - | The identity source name.
type | string | ✅ | - | The type of identity entries to fetch (e.g., internalusers, roles).
perPage | number | ❌ | 20 | Number of results per page. Must be ≥ 0.
page | number | ❌ | 1 | Page number to retrieve. Must be ≥ 0.
keyword | string | ❌ | - | Optional keyword to filter identity entries.

## 2. Get Identity Entries by IDs
### Endpoint
```
POST /api/security/identity/_entries
```
### Description
Obtain identity entries from a specified identity source by their IDs.

### Request Body

Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description
-- | -- | -- | -- | --
source | string | ✅ | - | The identity source name.
type | string | ✅ | - | The type of identity entries to fetch (e.g., internalusers, roles).
ids | array | ✅ | - | List of identity entry IDs to retrieve.

# Approach

## Server
PR: https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/9137

## How to register the identity source
Assuming the security plugins registered the identity source.

`plugins/security-dashboards-plugin/server/plugin.ts`
```

      getIdentityEntries: async ({type}, request, context) => {
        try {
          const typeMap: Record<string, string> = {
            internalusers: '/_plugins/_security/api/internalusers',
            roles: '/_plugins/_security/api/roles',
          };

          if (!typeMap[type]) {
            throw new Error(`This type "${type}" does not exist.`);
          }

          const client = context.core.opensearch.client.asCurrentUser;
          const response = await client.transport.request({
            method: 'GET',
            path: typeMap[type],
          });
          const result = Object.keys(response.body).map((name) => ({ name: name, id: name }));
          return result;
        } catch (error) {

author: joshuali925
title: [BUG][Query enhancements] Discover state partially resets when switching between plugins
body:
**Describe the bug**

When query enhancements is enabled, switching from Discover to Dashboard would set query language back to DQL, and switching back to Discover would reset the selected index pattern to the default one. This becomes problematic when there are no index patterns in the current workspace. It would show the previously selected dataset with an empty "SQL" query bar, but it is actually sending DSL requests to `/internal/search/opensearch-with-long-numerals`


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a new workspace with a opensearch connection. Ensure there are no index patterns in this workspace
2. Click on discover and select an index from the opensearch connection with SQL language
3. Run some query like `SELECT request,response FROM apachelog where response = '501' limit 2`
4. Click on Dashboards and click back to Discover
5. See index is still selected, language says "OpenSearch SQL", and query bar is empty
6. Now try to run the same SQL query, discover shows different results
7. In network tab, it calls `POST /w/czLj6e/internal/search/opensearch-with-long-numerals` instead of `/w/czLj6e/api/enhancements/search/sql`

**Expected behavior**
UI appearance and underlying state should be consistent

**OpenSearch Version**
main

**Dashboards Version**
main

**Plugins**

none

**Screenshots**

Notice SQL query is inside DSL
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af41f86c-8c38-4421-bd59-2b5d6297a18b)


**Host/Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: [e.g. iOS]
 - Browser and version [e.g. 22]

**Additional context**

One root cause is in `setQuery`, 
https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/0be70a72634e1d78f7b4f0e70bd21ff618ff1116/src/plugins/data/public/query/query_string/query_string_manager.ts#L168-L171

When there's no index pattern, on switching from Dashboard to Discover, it resets the query to default by passing `query` with `dataset` being `undefined`. The current logic will keep the original dataset in this case, but language still got reset to DQL. Now we have a `index` type dataset with incompatible language.

I've tried small effort fixes like 
```ts
    if (!query.dataset) {
      newQuery.dataset = undefined;
    }
```

and the index is no longer selected, but clicking on "Run" still sends DSL queries to the `apachelog` index. Apparently there are more places causing issues and need to be fixed

I respectfully request that you contact your map provider in order to update the maps to reflect the internationally recognized status of Crimea as part of Ukraine, in accordance with international law. This change would ensure the accuracy and neutrality of the OpenSearch platform. I am going to register a corresponding request on OpenStreetMap, as the society responsible for the map, but meanwhile, I would appreciate your attention to this matter to resolve this law violation in the shortest terms possible. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Deploy the latest version of the OpenSearch Dashboards 2. Create a Map visualization 3. Use a standard Vector map "World countries" 4. Navigate to the Crimia 5. author: Smjert
title: [BUG] Invalid handling of geopoint field types when joining multiple indexes in SQL
body:
**Describe the bug**

When doing a JOIN over a `geo_point` field, the resulting joined on field is null, which doesn't help in understanding which fields contents were matching.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Login anonymous in the future playground.
2. Select the **OTEL demo environment**.

6. Click into the query textbox
7. Select all fields and join two different indexes on a field that contains values in common, like `SELECT * FROM opensearch_dashboards_sample_data_logs as a JOIN opensearch_dashboards_sample_data_flights as b ON a.geo.dest = b.DestCountry`
    * Documents with the union of both index fields are returned, but the **a.geo** field is null, so it’s not possible to understand if **b.DestCountry** was the same.


**Expected behavior**

6. Ensure PPL queries are chosen and type `source = opensearch_dashboards_sample_data_logs` in the search box.
7. Search by hitting `<cmd>+<enter>`
8. Notice how the time filter resets to either the default `Last 15 minutes` or some other prior time range specified and the results are filtered according to the incorrect time range.

title: [BUG] Multitenancy: separate tenants cannot be used in different browser tabs
body:
**Describe the bug**
If I have two browser tabs open, and I select Tenant A in one tab, and then select Tenant B in the second tab, requests made in the first tab will get mapped to the tenant that was selected in the second tab. So, in the first tab, even though it says Tenant A is the current tenant, all saved objects that are pulled up will in fact be from Tenant B.

**To Reproduce**
- Configure Dashboards to have two or more tenants
- Change to one of those tenants (Tenant A)
- Open a new tab
- Select another tenant in the 2nd tab (Tenant B)
- Go back to the first tab and search for dashboards, visualizations, etc.

**Expected behavior**
The first tab should return results from Tenant A

**Actual behavior**
The first tab returns results from Tenant B, despite saying Tenant A is the current tenant

**OpenSearch Version**
2.18.0

**Dashboards Version**
2.18.0

**Plugins**
- Security

**Screenshots**

If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.

**Host/Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows 11
 - Browser and version: Chrome 131

**Additional context**
I believe this is because the selected tenant is being saved in a cookie, which is being reused across browser tabs

author: elmbrain
title: [BUG] Search query is not saved when clicking on a link with saved search
body: **Describe the bug** The search query is not saved when you click on a link with saved search. It can be either a short link or a full link, with all the request parameters. It can be seen that in the request parameters contain ```code query:(language:lucene,query: test) ``` or ```code query:(language:kuery,query: test) ``` but when the page loads, the line disappears from the search. This is most likely due to the order in which the parameters are applied. The search parameter is applied first, and then it is overwritten by the saved search. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Go to 'Discover' 2. Select index-pattern for search 3. Click "Save" and save search 4. Click "Open", select saved search 5. On the left upper corner you can see "Discover/${your_saved_search}" 6. Enter something in the search bar 7. Press "Share"->"Copy link" 8. Open the tab and follow the link 10. You will see that the search parameter has disappeared and it has disappeared from the query string 11. If in the same tab you follow the full link with search parameters, then everything works correctly **Expected behavior** It is expected that the link will open a search with the saved search parameter and search string **OpenSearch Version** 2.18.0 **Dashboards Version** 2.18.0 **Plugins** Only default plugins and Security **Screenshots** **Host/Environment (please complete the following information):** - OS: macos - Firefox/Chrome **Additional context** Full link of search ```code https://test-cluster.com/app/data-explorer/discover/#/view/17562920-b3e5-11ef-9242-cd847e376417?_q=(filters:!(),query:(language:kuery,query:Connection))&_g=(filters:!(),refreshInterval:(pause:!t,value:0),time:(from:now-15m,to:now))&_a=(discover:(columns:!(_source),isDirty:!f,savedSearch:'17562920-b3e5-11ef-9242-cd847e376417',sort:!()),metadata:(indexPattern:'security-auditlog-*',view:discover)) ``` Search link after follow ``` https://test-cluster.com/app/data-explorer/discover/#/view/17562920-b3e5-11ef-9242-cd847e376417?_q=(filters:!(),query:(language:kuery,query:''))&_g=(filters:!(),refreshInterval:(pause:!t,value:0),time:(from:now-15m,to:now))&_a=(discover:(columns:!(_source),isDirty:!f,savedSearch:'17562920-b3e5-11ef-9242-cd847e376417',sort:!()),metadata:(indexPattern:'security-auditlog-*',view:discover)) ``` Search query param erased

author: xinyual
title: [Alignment] Align the description for visbuilder aggregation config parameters
body:
We aim to develop a feature that translates natural language into VisBuilder configurations. Specifically, when a user poses a question related to an index, we will leverage LLMs to generate the following based on the user's query and the index:

1. Filters
2. Chart type
3. Aggregation configuration parameters (AggConfigParams)

To ensure accuracy, we have compiled parameter descriptions for various aggregations based on the source code in this [directory](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/tree/539675e688061e689b362801bcb05a3ef78431b2/src/plugins/data/common/search/aggs), as summarized in the table below.

We want to confirm the correctness of these descriptions and align them with the code owners. Please review the information and provide comments if you identify any errors or missing details.

## Metric aggregation
### normal metric aggregation
| Agg | Field Name | Type | Description | Optional |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| median | field | string | The name of the field for which the median value will be calculated. The field must be of type 'number', 'date', or 'histogram'. | False |
| standard_deviation | field | string | The name of the field for which the standard deviation will be calculated. The field must be of type 'number'. | False |
| unique_count | field | string | The name of the field for which the unique count will be calculated. Supports all data types except histograms. | False |
| min | field | string | The name of the field for which the minimum value will be calculated. The field must be of type 'number' or 'date'. | False |
| max | field | string | The name of the field for which the maximum value will be calculated. The field must be of type 'number' or 'date'. | False |
| sum | field | string | The name of the field for which the sum will be calculated. The field must be of type 'number' or 'histogram'. | False |
| top_hit | field | string | The field from which the top hit(s) will be retrieved. Supports most data types except histograms. | False |
| top_hit | aggregate | string | Specifies the aggregation operation to perform on the top hits, such as 'min', 'max', 'sum', 'average', or 'concat'. | False |
| top_hit | size | number | The number of top hits to retrieve. | True |
| top_hit | sortField | string | The field to sort by when determining the top hit(s). Supports numeric, date, IP, and string fields. | True |
| top_hit | sortOrder | string | The sort order for the top hit(s). Can be 'desc' for descending or 'asc' for ascending. | True |
| avg | field | string | Specifies the numeric or histogram field on which the average aggregation will be performed. | False |
| percentile | field | string | The name of the field for which percentiles will be calculated. The field must be of type 'number', 'date', or 'histogram'. | False |
| percentile | percents | array of numbers | Defines the percentiles to compute. The default set includes common percentiles such as 1st, 5th, 25th, 50th, 75th, 95th, and 99th. | True |
| cardinality | field | string | The name of the field for which the unique count will be calculated. Supports all data types except histograms. | False |

### parent metric aggregation
| Agg | Field Name | Type | Description | Optional |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| moving_avg | buckets_path | string | Specifies the path to the buckets from which the moving average is calculated. It must reference a metric or aggregation result. | False |
| moving_avg | window | number | The size of the moving average window, specifying how many data points to include in the calculation. | True |
| moving_avg | script | string | A script that defines the calculation logic for the moving average. Defaults to an unweighted average. | True |
| moving_avg | customMetric | object | Defines a custom metric to be used for the moving average calculation. Allows overriding the default metric configuration. | True |

author: brijos
title: [Feedback Capture] Discover Enhancements
body:
We are excited about the work that is being done on the new discover.

A new experimental [Discover](https://opensearch.org/docs/2.4/dashboards/discover/index-discover/) interface enhances the query experience and offers greater customization options. The interface allows analysts to collapse unused sections and streamline their workspace. Over the past year, we've gathered valuable feedback from users across OpenSearch's query interfaces, including Piped Processing Language (PPL) in Log Explorer (for observability) and SQL in Query Workbench. In response, we're adding PPL and SQL as query options in Discover alongside Dashboards Query Language (DQL) and Lucene, allowing analysts to use their preferred query language. We've also improved the data selector and added autocomplete functionality—a highly requested feature. The new experience is available behind a feature flag, which you can enable by navigating to Dashboards Management, selecting Advanced Settings, and toggling "Enable query enhancements" to ON.

As mentioned above, we've received great feedback from the community on Discover and want to keep that momentum. In the feedback, please include likes, dislikes and a little background on what you were trying to accomplish to help us understand better.

author: Acta
title: [BUG] Heatmap/Histogram on X-axis
body:
**Describe the bug**

Histogram charts doesn't respect the order asked when buckets are along the X-axis

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

In real life I work with inversed coordinates that's why I'm here but I've found a simple way to reproduce the behavior on playground server. Forget the fact that the x-Axis is time in this example and timeline goes normaly from left to right. It's only to illustrate!

1. Go to opensearch playground site (https://playground.opensearch.org/)
2. Go to `(Heatmap) Source vs OS` vizualisation 
3. Go to the Data->Buckets->X-axis and change:
 - sub aggregation: Histogram
 - Field: Hour_of_Day
 - Show empty buckets
 - Extend bounds (min: 0, max:24)
 - Advanced: `{"order": { "_key": "desc" }}`
4. Update

**Expected behavior**
The X-axis should be reversed: starting on left with 24 and ending with 0 on right

**OpenSearch Version**
Last 2.17.1, I suppose

**Dashboards Version**
Last 2.17.1, I suppose

**Plugins**
you know better than me

**Screenshots**

If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.

**Host/Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Ubuntu
 - Browser and version: firefox

**Additional context**

I'm not an expert in js and all the internal stuffs of opensearch code. I give it a try with my poor english :)

In the file `src/plugins/vis_type_vislib/public/vislib/components/zero_injection/ordered_x_keys.js`, the X-axis seems to be re-sorted even if the histogram have an explicit orderby clause during the query:
```
.sortBy(function (d) {
      if (d[1].isDate || d[1].isOrdered) {
        return +d[0];
      }
      return orderBucketsBySum ? -d[1].sum : d[1].index;
    })
```

In the file `src/plugins/vis_type_vislib/public/vislib/components/zero_injection/uniq_keys.js`, the isDate and isOrdered const are defined:
```
const isDate = charts.every((chart) => {
    return chart.ordered && chart.ordered.date;
  });

const isOrdered = charts.every((chart) => {
    return chart.ordered;
  });
```

In the file `src/plugins/discover/public/application/components/chart/utils/point_series.ts`:
```
chart.ordered = {
    date: true,
    interval,
    intervalOpenSearchUnit,
    intervalOpenSearchValue,
    min: bounds.min,
    max: bounds.max,
  };
```
If the `date` field is always `true`, the statement in the `sortBy` function could be only `if d[1].isOrdered` but... Why is `date` always `true`? Pure speculation, but for me it should be `true` for `date histogram` agg and `false` for "regular" `histogram` agg perhaps. So the statement should be `if d[1].isDate` only. author: joshuali925
title: [Discover] Support selecting multiple datasets
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Currently discover only supports selecting single dataset (ie. single index-pattern, single index, etc). It would be useful to support multi-select.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Basic implementation for multi-select is added in https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/8255, but it takes a shortcut by combining selected datasets into one dataset after user configuration. Discover still keeps one reference of dataset. This has some limitations such as we cannot display fields separately per dataset, and the implementation hard codes the logic when combining datasets. It should be more flexible. See https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/8255#discussion_r1768140348

Additionally multi-select component should display proper error message when incompatible datasets are selected together, see https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/8255#discussion_r1777847999

author: ruanyl
title: [Proposal] [query-assistant] Move query assistant feature to dashboards-assistant plugin
body:
## Overview

This proposal suggests migrating the recently added Query Assistant feature from the core query-enhancement plugin to the dashboards-assistant plugin.

## Reason
As the dashboards-assistant plugin is intended to serve as a central hub for OSD AI-related functionalities, consolidating the Query Assistant feature within this plugin will provide several benefits:

1. By grouping all AI-related features and APIs under a single plugin, we can reduce the maintenance efforts, ensuring consistent API contracts across all AI functionalities.
2. Users will have a single, clear location to find all AI-driven enhancements. This will improve the discoverability and usability of these features.
3. Moving the feature to a dedicated plugin reduces the complexity of the core query-enhancement plugin. This can help reduce potential dependencies between plugins.

## Plan
1. Migrate and refactor the current query-assistant feature in core query_enhancement plugin to dashboards-assistant plugin.
2. Remove the query-assistant feature related implementations in core.
3. Make sure this change is clearly communicated across stakeholders: @joshuali925 @kavilla @ashwin-pc 

## Question
1. How to deal with the query-assistant feature in Observability plugin?

author: Swiddis
title: [BUG] No truncation callout for Discover when query default record count isn't exactly 500
body: **Describe the bug** Following [this comment](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/8060#discussion_r1752765242) on #8060: Discover infinite scrolling queries are currently hardcoded to assume that for every available query language, running it with no limit configured will truncate the records after exactly 500 records. This is true for DQL and Lucene queries, but not for PPL or SQL, which have default limits of 200. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Create an index that has more than 500 records, using e.g. [this docker-compose](https://github.com/Swiddis/opensearch-utils/blob/main/docker/docker-compose.yml) to generate data. 2. Enable query enhancements 3. Run a DQL query on the index -- notice that there's a truncated search callout indicating the records are truncated 4. Do the same thing with a PPL query, where the default limit is 200 5. Observe there's no such callout **Expected behavior** Depending on the selected language, there should be a callout for either `200` or `500` records as a default limit (possibly even pulling from a configured setting somewhere). It's maybe not sufficient to add the callout for `200` or `500` both with the same hardcoding, as this would lead to cases where it says it's truncated when more data is still being pulled (albeit only for some intermediate render steps). It's worth noting that due to this hardcoded check, the callout also shows up if you run a SQL query with `LIMIT 500` or PPL with `HEAD 500` as the returned records matches the expected truncation threshold, when no truncation is occurring. These callouts ideally shouldn't show up if the query returns exactly 200 or 500 records without truncation (although knowing this ahead of time may be equivalent to the halting problem). **OpenSearch Version** 2.16.0 **Dashboards Version** Current `main`, pre-2.17 but post-2.16 **Plugins** Observability, Reporting, Query Workbench. The SQL plugin on the backend is important. **Screenshots** See above. **Host/Environment (please complete the following information):** - OS: Mac OS - Browser and version: Firefox 129.0.2 **Additional context** N/A

body:
**Describe the bug**

The index pattern service updated the cached index pattern title to contain the datasource title in it, but this behaviour is not consistent and calling the get method on the index pattern service shows only the saved object title without the datasource in title. This leads to inconsistent behaviour in the UI.

https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/2.16/src/plugins/data/common/index_patterns/index_patterns/index_patterns.ts#L124-L135

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Call indexPatterns.getIdsWithTitle()

3. Compare the titles

**Expected behavior**
Instead of modifying the cache, we shoud store the datasource title as well if we want to avoid another call for the datasource and only append it where we display it to the user. We should ideally never modify the raw title attribute since without it we no longer know what the index pattern title was without making a raw call to the saved object service.

author: BionIT
title: [Meta][2.17] Support Multiple Data Source in OpenSearch Dashboards Plugins
body:
### Context
Since 2.4.0, multiple data source feature is enabled as a core plugin(see RFC https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/1388 and PR https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/2334). 

With multiple data source enabled, users of OpenSearch Dashboards are able to create data source connections and query local and remote OpenSearch clusters(see documentation https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/dashboards/management/data-sources/). Enabling multiple data source at dashboards plugin would ensure users that have been using the multiple data source feature to have a consistent experience in the dashboard, and allows users to use the same dashboard for different clusters.

**This meta issue is used to track the PR/Issues for supporting multiple data source in OpenSearch Dashboards Plugins**
- [x] https://github.com/opensearch-project/dashboards-observability/issues/2010


### Data source connection picker
In https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/5717, we introduced a picker to select data connection. This picker is within the data source plugin bundle, and when loaded, it will fetch data source connection which is a type of saved object and then populate the available data connections as single selected options in the drop down. 

In order to consume this picker from a plugin, follow the steps as below:

1. in the opensearch_dashboards.json file, add dataSource as required bundle, eg. "requiredBundles": ["dataSourceManagement"]
2.  import the component in the file where this picker is needed, eg.  import { ClusterSelector } from '../../data_source_management/public'
3. this picker exposes onSelectedDataSource which can be used to get the selected option from the picker component

### Data source client
Data source plugin was released in OpenSearch Dashboards 2.4.0 as part of the multi data source feature.
The plugin exposes OpenSearch client wrapper and this is the design https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/main/docs/multi-datasource/client_management_design.md, it can be acquired from context via the following:
`client: OpenSearchClient = await context.dataSource.opensearch.getClient(dataSourceId);`
For legacy client, we can initiate the client via the following 
`apiCaller: LegacyAPICaller = context.dataSource.opensearch.legacy.getClient(dataSourceId).callAPI;`
Note that we need to pass in the data source id as argument, and this id can be acquired by passing a function to the child component by following instructions above.

### PoC
PoC commit for query bench dashboards plugin to support MDS: https://github.com/opensearch-project/dashboards-query-workbench/compare/main...BionIT:dashboards-query-workbench:mdinteg

A few things to notice:
1. to consume the client, we need to add `"optionalPlugins": ["dataSource"]` in opensearch_dashboards.json in the plugin repo
2. to consume the React component to pick data source, we need to add `"requiredBundles": ["dataSourceManagement"]`
3. during plugin set up, in order to register the plugin API schema/spec, we can do the following `dataSource.registerCustomApiSchema(sqlPlugin)` 
4. most plugins might need to depend on the data source picker, please follow to set it up, and once we acquire the selected data source id, we need to pass it to plugin `const {dataSourceId} = request.query;` then the datasource Id can be passed to the data source client wrapper `context.dataSource.opensearch.getClient(dataSourceId)`

author: wanglam
title: [Workspace] Optimize Performance by Caching Workspace Saved Objects During Permission Validation
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

In the current implementation, when validating permissions for workspace saved objects, the system needs to call bulkGet for each workspace saved object to retrieve its permission information. This process results in numerous duplicate requests for the same workspace saved objects, leading to performance inefficiencies during the permission validation logic.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

To address this issue and improve performance, we propose implementing a caching mechanism for workspace saved objects during the permission validation process. By caching and reusing the bulkGet results within the same request, we can significantly reduce the number of redundant calls and optimize the permission validation logic.

The proposed solution involves the following three main changes:

1. Add saved objects cache-related methods in the permission control client

- Introduce the following methods in the permission control client:
    - *cacheSavedObjects(request, savedObjects)*: This method will mark the provided saved objects as cacheable for the given request, meaning that the bulkGet results for these saved objects will be cached. The permission control client can then use the cached data instead of fetching it from the network.
    - *clearSavedObjectsCache(request)*: This method will clear all cached saved objects for the given request.
    - *isSavedObjectsCacheActive(request)*: This method will check if there are any existing cached saved objects for the given request.

2. Cache workspace saved objects during bulk operations
- Modify the workspace saved object client wrapper to call cacheSavedObjects with the saved objects' workspaces during bulkCreate, bulkUpdate, and bulkGet operations.
- This change will ensure that the workspace information is cached during the same request, eliminating the need for duplicate bulkGet calls for workspaces.

3. Clear saved objects cache before responding
- Register a pre-response hook in the workspace plugin's permission setup logic.
- Within the pre-response hook, call isSavedObjectsCacheActive to check if there are any cached saved objects.
- If cached saved objects exist, call clearSavedObjectsCache to clear the cache before responding to the request.

By implementing this caching mechanism, we can significantly reduce the number of bulkGet calls made during the permission validation process, thereby improving performance and optimizing the overall system efficiency.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

N/A

**Additional context**

#4944
#6051

author: BionIT
title: [Proposal][Multiple Data Sources] Introduce Dashboards Tour With Multi Data Sources
body:
## Overview
With 2.14 and 2.15 releases, we introduced multi data source into 13 dashboards plugins and feature anywhere and see them live in https://playground.opensearch.org/app/home#/
- 2.14: https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/5870
- 2.15: https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/6596 

In order to introduce the new experience to the community, we published blog(https://opensearch.org/blog/Top-3-Scenarios-Where-Managing-Multiple-Clusters-with-One-OpenSearch-Dashboards-is-a-Life-Saver/) and tutorial (https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/dashboards/management/multi-data-sources/#using-multiple-data-sources-with-external-dashboards-plugins).

We had been receiving feedback about the new capability and to better serve our dashboards users, we propose to introduce a new tour feature, which can be enabled or turned off. Its main purpose is to guide our users to interact with this new multi data source experience when enabled.  

## Alternative
### Better documentation/video demo 
Study indicates that people remember approximately 10% of what they hear, 20% of what they read, and 80% of what they see and do. For users who interact with the dashboards most of the time, the best way to learn the new experience might not start with reading the documentation again, but to actually by start to interact with it.

## PoC

author: artur-borys
title: [BUG] Undocumented server.ssl.cipherSuites in opensearch_dashboards.yml
body:
**Describe the bug**

Hi! First of all - thanks for the great work that you're doing. It's an important project and I value your time and dedication.

I treat security very seriously and I've noticed that the default ciphersuites contain a lot of ciphers which are not considered to be secure anymore.

I've noticed that the example ``opensearch_dashboards.yml`` file doesn't contain any description for ``server.ssl.cipherSuites`` key.

I was able to limit the enabled ciphersuites to a secure list by setting:
``` yaml
server.ssl.cipherSuites:
  - TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
  - TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256
  - TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
  - ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
  - ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305
  - ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
```

It would be nice if the parameter was mentioned in the example ``opensearch_dashboards.yml`` file, as I think it's an essential parameter when it comes to security.

**To Reproduce**

title: [Feature] Visualization table type without metrics/buckets

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

It is not possible to display unaggregated data in table form in a dashboards.

Desired flow:
Create visualization > Pick type (Table) > Choose a source (Saved search in my case to select fields) > Save
Done! This should render a table that displays all the found elements from the source within selected time period in dashboard.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Discover allows selecting fields you'd like to query and it's table displays search results without any aggregations. 
The feature I'm looking for is just the table itself being available as visualization in dashboards, selected fields would be predetermined from visualization source (Saved search)

author: huyaboo
title: [MDS] Full Timeline Support
body:
## Proposal
As of today, [Timeline](https://opensearch.org/docs/2.13/dashboards/visualize/viz-index/#timeline) does not support multiple datasource or MDS). #6009 provides most of the building blocks to support Timeline. However, to fully integrate Timeline in MDS, there is a need to support exporting/importing to another datasource. With #5712, users can specify which datasource to import from. Timeline should seamlessly import from different datasources. 

## High-Level Approach
Timeline, like other visualizations, stores visualization configuration info in the `visState`. An example is shown below:
```
{
  title: '(Timeline) Avg bytes over time',
  type: 'timelion',
  aggs: [],
  params: {
    expression: '.opensearch(opensearch_dashboards_sample_data_logs, metric=avg:bytes, timefield=@timestamp).lines(show=true).points(show=true).yaxis(label="Average bytes")',
    interval: 'auto'
  }
}
```

As shown, the `visState` stores the entire `expression` as a string. To properly support import/export, the data source references can be appended when the visualization is saved to the datasource by extracting out the `data_source_name` from the expression. Then, upon import to a specified data source, the data source id reference is appended, and any local cluster queries can be modified to use this new data source. This is a similar approach to [#5975](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/5975). However, to implement this approach will require significant effort. There are two main challenges:
1. How to append data source references
2. How to update the `expression` string safely

### Challenge 1: Appending data source references
To reliably determine the `data_source_name` from the `expression`, the `expression` will have to be parsed. However, since `Timeline` syntax can specify named arguments, unnamed arguments, or a combination of the two, this will be a challenge to parse. Some investigation will need to be done on how the `.opensearch()` function resolves the input values to arguments. 

### Challenge 2: Changing the `expression` so that it uses a specified data source
Unlike other visualization types, Timeline syntax is *specific* to this visualization. To define this syntax, Timeline makes use of [pegjs](https://github.com/pegjs/pegjs), a JS implementation of a PEG parser. A PEG parser provides a way to parse an input from a grammar. Think of PEG parsers as context-free-grammar (CFG) except that PEG parses are unambiguous in their parse and always parse an input string to the same parse tree. In Timeline's case, the grammar can be found in `chain.peg`.

https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/46b17e4bb96e8b1293b23ac12a3ba739c2c83701/src/plugins/vis_type_timeline/common/chain.peg#L1-L3


The `expression` is parsed in the `parseSheet()` function when the request is being processed:

https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/46b17e4bb96e8b1293b23ac12a3ba739c2c83701/src/plugins/vis_type_timeline/server/handlers/lib/parse_sheet.js#L39-L60


One major hurdle with import/export logic is that `expression` will have to be modified if export/import to another data source is supported. To modify this expression in a structured manner, the `expression` will have to be parsed. However, `pegjs` only supports an asymmetric parse (see [this closed issue](https://github.com/pegjs/pegjs/issues/571)). In other words, it is not possible with `pegjs` to parse a string into a parse object, modify that object, and transform that object back into a string.
```
// Supported
expression string -> parse object

// Refer to Challenge 1
modify parse object with data_source_name

// NOT Supported
parse object -> expression string
```

This means that the reconstruction of the `expression` back from the `parse` object will require a manual implementation to modify the text and store it in the `visState`. This is possible to accomplish

author: wanglam
title: [Workspace] Add permission setting for workspace create update page
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

In #6052, we add workspace permission control logic. User can create a workspace with permission control by calling workspace create or update API. For most users, calling workspace related API won't be a convenient way. We can add a permission setting section in workspace create and update form. For workspace create page, the workspace create API will automatic grant creator as workspace admin. For workspace update page, we need to keep at least one admin permission to ensure workspace can be controlled by some user.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Since workspace CRUD API already support creating and updating workspace, we only need to change the UI side. We prefer adding a permission setting tab in workspace form. The user can set user and group permission in the permission tab. The permission setting value will be send to the workspace create API after create button clicked. For workspace update page, the fetched workspace permission setting will be filled in the permission setting tab. User can modify the settings, and then will call workspace update API after update button clicked.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

N/A

**Additional context**

#6051

title: [RFC] Proposal for Adding Cache in App Config
body:
# Introduction

In open source 2.13.0 release, we add the support of dynamic application configuration. The feature stores the configuration in a new OpenSearch index and allows dynamic read and write. We onboard the first use case of CSP rules to the configuration. However, as the team evaluates it to support more use cases (e.g workspace https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/6300), there are concerns about its performance when large traffic routes to the underlying storage. The API under concern is `getEntityConfig` which is for getting the configuration value given an entity name. To address the concern, we are proposing to add cache in dynamic application configuration.

# Challenges

We will evaluate the technical approaches from several challenges. 

The first challenge is whether we will allow custom cache technique. OSS OSD could have a default cache technique and exposes registration of other cache techniques. This could give other OSD offerings the flexibility to choose their cache technique. As a contrast, we could fix a cache technique in OSS OSD and then all other offerings will inherit it.

The second challenge is choosing between distributed cache and local cache. In a multi-node cluster, a local cache in a node may be updated when the same node receives an update request while local cache in other nodes may keep returning the old value until the cache expiry. The distributed cache has a mechanism to sync data across the network but requires extra complexity to build.

The third challenge is the call pattern. Since application configurations are infrequent to change, the number of reads will be much larger than the number of writes.

The fourth challenge is between new dependencies and existing dependencies. New dependencies may introduce new vulnerabilities into our code base. If the existing dependency can meet the business requirement, we will prefer it.

# Proposed Approach

We propose to use the existing cache library `lru-cache` to add a cache layer before querying the configuration index. It is a in-memory local cache that deletes the least-recently-used items. The key is the entity name of string type and the value is the configuration value of string type.

We plan to initialize the cache with the following parameters.

```

max: 100
maxAge: 5 * 60 * 1000

```
The parameter `max` indicates the maximum size of the cache. The parameter `maxAge` indicates the time to live in ms. 

For `getEntityConfig` function, we will first attempt to get its cached value. If the value exists, we will use it. Otherwise, we will query the index to get the value. When `updateEntityConfig` function is called, we will update the value in the cache. When `deleteEntityConfig` function is called, we will remove the value from the cache.

Below is the list of functions provided by the cache which we plan to call.

```
   /**
     * Will update the "recently used"-ness of the key. They do what you think.
     * `maxAge` is optional and overrides the cache `maxAge` option if provided.
     *
     * If the key is not found, will return `undefined`.
     */
    get(key: K): V | undefined;



   /**
     * Will update the "recently used"-ness of the key. They do what you think.
     * `maxAge` is optional and overrides the cache `maxAge` option if provided.
     */
    set(key: K, value: V, maxAge?: number): boolean;



   /**
     * Deletes a key out of the cache.
     */
    del(key: K): void;

```
The cache will be initialized inside the constructor of the plugin `applicationConfig`. Whenever a `OpenSearchConfigurationClient` object is created, the cache will be passed into it. It will stay in memory until the OSD server stops and will not persist during a server restart.

We plan to directly use this cache library and do not expose registration of other cache clients into OSD.


# Alternative Approaches

## Approach 1 In-memory Cache Li

author: kavilla
title: [OE] Plugins should bootstrap with --single-version=loose
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

By default, plugins will bootstrap as strict. This will compare dependencies with a lazy string compare and fail the build completely. Even for semvers that are the same, it will still fail.

This blocks developers from implementing with other plugins easily and prevents the distribution from being built with the plugin causing issues to be caught last minute. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/5675 adds the support to be less strict about the version.

Within OpenSearch Dashboards `main` we should default the single-version to be loose. As we can do that with breaking changes.

Within 2.x we should audit all the OpenSearch Dashboards plugins within this OpenSearch project and create an issue or update their script to pass this value.

Thus we can ensure successful builds within the build pipeline and rely on integration tests to verify the run time of the application.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

n/a

**Additional context**

Related issue:
https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/5953

As of today, [Time Series Visual Builder (TSVB)](https://opensearch.org/docs/2.12/dashboards/visualize/viz-index/#tsvb)  does not support remote datasource connections (also referred to as multiple datasource or MDS). [#6005](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/6005) provides most of the building blocks to support TSVB. However, there are a few features to consider to fully integrate MDS into TSVB:
- **Export/import logic:** With [#5712](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/5712), users can specify which datasource to import from. TSVB should seamlessly import from different datasources.
- **Timeseries annotations:** One feature of the timeseries graph visualization is the ability to place annotations or markers on the graph. Each annotation has its own index pattern to fetch data from.

In this issue, these features will be the main focus. For details on how TSVB can support MDS, refer to [#6005](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/6005).

author: cwperks
title: [Multiple Datasource] Support datasource-specific TLS configuration
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Related PR that introduces common TLS configuration across _all_ configured datasource: https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/6171

This feature request is to extend the settings introduced in https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/6171 and make them datasource-specific. 

The settings to add are:

```
ssl.verificationMode
ssl.certificateAuthorities
```

These settings are utilized when configuring the opensearch client for a particular datasource. For instance, with configuration-per-datasource you can configure one datasource with no SSL verification while enforcing SSL verification on another datasource.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

The TLS could either be configured:

- When adding a datasource through OSD
- Through a yml file that contains all datasources and their configuration

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Without datasource-specific TLS configuration, all configured datasources must share the same TLS settings.
