author: ananzh
title: Understand Discover -- (draft)
body:
Discover is an internal plugin in OpenSearch Dashboards core. There are three major functions:

* *Select* data for your exploration, and then set a time range for that data, search it with the OpenSearch Dashboards Query Language, and filter the results.
* *Explore* the details of your data, view individual documents, and create tables that summarize the contents of the data.
* *Present* your findings in a visualization.

## Required plugins

* charts
* *data*: access data from OpenSearch. discover uses data plugin to do filter query and search.
    * $scope.searchSource: construct and run search 
    * data.query: construct and run filters, time range query, match query and etc
        * data.query.state
        * data.query.filterManager: manager filters
        * data.query.queryString: query string
        * data.query.timefilter: time range filter
    * autocomplete wired in TopNavMenu
* embeddable
* inspector
* opensearchDashboardsLegacy
* urlForwarding: redirect and navigate to legacy url
* navigation: provide TopNavMenu component
* uiActions
* visualizations: create histogram for aggregate data
* opensearchDashboardsUtils: state manager and state sync service
* home
* *savedObject**: loading and saving. discover uses savedObject plugin to save search.
    *  a saved object type, called searchSavedObjectType
    * a saved object class, called SavedSearch, with all convenient functions
* opensearchDashboardsReact

# Setup and Start Discover

## Server
### Setup discover

* [setup application](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/d7004dc5b0392477fdd54ac66b29d231975a173b/src/core/server/bootstrap.ts#L128) 
    * [setup server](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/d7004dc5b0392477fdd54ac66b29d231975a173b/src/core/server/root/index.ts#L64) 
        * [get plugin dependency tree](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/d7004dc5b0392477fdd54ac66b29d231975a173b/src/core/server/server.ts#L130)
            * [discover plugins](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/d7004dc5b0392477fdd54ac66b29d231975a173b/src/core/server/plugins/plugins_service.ts#L115)
                * [create PluginWrapper](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/d7004dc5b0392477fdd54ac66b29d231975a173b/src/core/server/plugins/discovery/plugins_discovery.ts#L83) 
            * [process plugin](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/d7004dc5b0392477fdd54ac66b29d231975a173b/src/core/server/plugins/plugins_service.ts#L119)
                * [get plugin definition](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/d7004dc5b0392477fdd54ac66b29d231975a173b/src/core/server/plugins/plugin.ts#L152-L153)
                    * [get DiscoverServerPlugin’s imports and modules](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/d7004dc5b0392477fdd54ac66b29d231975a173b/src/plugins/discover/server/index.ts#L31)
                        * [get uiSettings](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/d7004dc5b0392477fdd54ac66b29d231975a173b/src/plugins/discover/server/plugin.ts#L32)

                        * [get searchSavedObjectType](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/d7004dc5b0392477fdd54ac66b29d231975a173b/src/plugins/discover/server/plugin.ts#L34)

author: joshuarrrr
title: [Enhancement] Export existing visualizations to vega
body:
Posting on behalf of a user who doesn't have a GitHub account

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

We have a dashboard that we manually filter by using the Controls visualization. When adding a filter, the whole dashboard is affected, but we would like some of the visuals to stay the same and not inherit/implement dashboard filters. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

The only current way to build visualizations that ignore filters is to use the `vega` visualization (where global query, filters, and time range can be selectively included as part of the spec. But because we already have many existing visualizations, we'd prefer not to re-create them from scratch. It would be easier to just export them to vega, tweak the dashboard filter part and import them back. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Alternatively, or additionally, it should be possible to configure dashboard visualizations to ignore global filter updates; a filter equivalent to what's proposed for date ranges in https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/1242

author: ashwin-pc
title: Enhanced toast notifications
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Today toast notifications provided by the notifications service have a few drawback and limitations that can cause user frustration and require hacky solutions by individual plugins to overcome. Some of these issues are:

1.  It can easily overwhelm the user since they have very little controls to prevent frequent rerender errors from spewing out multiple toasts for the same event. 
2. Once dismissed or timed out, there is no way for the user to see past notifications
3. No way to act on a notification

**Describe the solution you'd like**

There are a few ways we can address the different problems:

1. Notification ID: Multiple notifications with the same ID will result inthe notification being displayed only once with the timeout being reset each time and the count displayed with some truncation limit (e.g. 99+)
2. Notification Drawer: Notifications when emitted can be optionally be added to a notification drawer that the user can manually clear or take action from.
3. Notification actions: Add a provision to add actions to toasts that the user can take to act on a notification directly

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

-

**Additional context**

Here is an example of how the dashboards plugin makes sure that no more than one notification is shown at a time.

https://github.com/ashwin-pc/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/0640b4646415b18da84414199d2331d6dfba4d61/src/plugins/dashboard/public/application/actions/replace_panel_flyout.tsx#L64-L79

author: abbyhu2000
title: [Proposal] Data persistence using session storage by default instead of using URL
body: **Overview** Current dashboard plugins such as dashboards, discover, timeline and visualize implement data persistence using URL or session storage. The default option is to persist global data and app data in the URL, so the actual data are being embedded within the URL. **Problem** However, since it stores everything in the URL itself, the URL can easily get super long. A sample URL of metric visualization: `http://localhost:5603/jtn/app/visualize#/create?type=metric&indexPattern=ff959d40-b880-11e8-a6d9-e546fe2bba5f&_g=(filters:!(),query:(language:kuery,query:''),refreshInterval:(pause:!f,value:86400000),time:(from:now-90d,to:now))&_a=(filters:!(),linked:!f,query:(language:kuery,query:''),uiState:(),vis:(aggs:!((enabled:!t,id:'1',params:(),schema:metric,type:count),(enabled:!t,id:'2',params:(customLabel:counting),schema:metric,type:count),(enabled:!t,id:'3',params:(field:products.base_price,percents:!(50)),schema:metric,type:median),(enabled:!t,id:'4',params:(field:order_date,ranges:!((from:now-1w%2Fw,to:now))),schema:group,type:date_range)),params:(addLegend:!f,addTooltip:!t,metric:(colorSchema:'Green%20to%20Red',colorsRange:!((from:0,to:10000)),invertColors:!f,labels:(show:!t),metricColorMode:None,percentageMode:!f,style:(bgColor:!f,bgFill:%23000,fontSize:60,labelColor:!f,subText:''),useRanges:!f),type:metric),title:'',type:metric))` When user creates complicated visualizations, this URL will embed every single information, and will be super long. This is hard to manage and it might even cause issues. (microsoft edge apparently breaks with URLs of just 2083 characters) **Proposal** I propose that instead of persisting data in the URL as default, we should persist data in session storage by default (make `Store URLs in session storage` toggle in advanced setting on by default). Now since the actual data is not embedded in the URL, the URL will be much shorter by only storing the hash key for those data. For example, `"http://localhost:5603/jtn/app/discover#/?_g=h@87a7a5c&_a=h@9a51110"` is the new URL. **1. Concerns of the proposal** One setback is that if we want to share this URL to someone else, they won't be able to use the URL to retrieve those persisted data since they don't have access to the session storage and the URL itself only embeds information of the hash key. For example, I cleared my session storage and refresh the page, and it shows this error: **2. Solution to the concern && todos** However, this can be solved if they use the share functionality if they want to share the URL with someone else. The share functionality will provide users the URL with the actual data embedded so they can share the link with others with the data being persisted. If we are going to make session storage the default option for data persistence, I think we should also have some tutorial or instructions on the share functionality for users.

author: ohltyler
title: [Feature Anywhere] Add a `vis_layers` expression function type
body:
As part of #2880, we propose to have a standardized way for plugins to format their overlay data into a `VisLayer` that can be processed by the downstream visualizations for rendering this additional data. For more information on the `VisLayer` overlay data model, see #2882.

To accomplish this, we can introduce a `vis_layers` expression function type, and allow plugins to register their own functions of this type. During the visualization rendering process, all relevant expression functions can be fetched via saved objects (see #2893 for details on the saved objects design), and built into a single pipeline that can be ran to compile an array of `VisLayer`s. The visualization can then process these `VisLayer`s accordingly, and render the additional data.

The I/O of this new expression function will be the same - an array of `VisLayer`s. The purpose of the function itself will be to take in the array, construct a `VisLayer` of their own using their own data, append it to the array, and pass it on as output. This design allows for an arbitrary number of these function types to be executed in an arbitrary order, allowing any plugin to add any number of `VisLayer`s to a particular visualization.

We can illustrate how this may work with a simple example:
`[]` -> `plugin-1-expr-fn` -> `[vis-layer-1]` -> `plugin-2-expr-fn` -> `[vis-layer-1, vis-layer-2]`

Open questions:
1. Similar to #2893, where should this function be maintained & registered inside of OpenSearch Dashboards? My preferred solution is that this is maintained in a standalone `feature-anywhere` plugin

author: ohltyler
title: [Feature Anywhere] Add a `augment-vis` saved object type
body:
As part of #2880, we propose to create a new saved object type called `augment-vis`. The purpose of this new type will be to store the relationships between a plugin resource (e.g., anomaly detector or alerting monitor) to a visualization. The main components/fields include:
1. Plugin resource ID (e.g., detector id)
2. A reference to a `vis_layer` expression function, including the name of the function and the args needed (for more details on this expression function, see #2894)
3. A reference to the visualization that can be stored in the `references` field.

To create and register this new type, we can do the following:
Client/public-side:
- [ ] Create a saved object class that extends `SavedObjectClass`
- [ ] Create a saved object loader that extends `SavedObjectLoader` to use as a wrapper for performing CRUD operations on the new saved object class / type
- [ ] Create `extractReferences`/`injectReferences` helper fns for creating and parsing the stored `references` to the saved objects
- [ ] Instantiate the loader in the `start` lifecycle of dependent plugins (e.g., visualizations plugin, downstream plugins like Anomaly Detection), such that they can use the loader for creating/fetching the saved objects
- [ ] Register in the `saved_objects_management` plugin (this may not be needed)

Server-side:
- [ ] Create a saved objects type that extends `SavedObjectsType`, used for defining how the object as managed, and how the particular mappings will be stored in the system index
- [ ] Register this type in the `setup` lifecycle of the plugin

Open questions:
1. ~~Should this new type be registered & integrated with the `saved_objects_management` plugin? This will allow visibility into what is stored in the saved objects, but ideally users don't need or want access to it. Making changes to it may result in weird behavior~~ UPDATE: yes we will support it see [here](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/3109#discussion_r1055837516)
2. ~~Should this new type be created in a standalone plugin, or in an existing plugin? If in an existing plugin, such as `Visualizations`, it allows for less boilerplate code, but may not be logical if the `feature-anywhere` type is used for integration with other saved objects in the future, such as dashboards, saved searches, index patterns, other new saved object types, etc.~~ UPDATE: it will live in a standalone plugin - see #2958

author: ohltyler
title: [Feature Anywhere] Add a generic interface for overlaying data on a Visualization
body:
There are many ways we may want to support adding to and/or augmenting the source visualization data to provide additional insights. We can introduce a generic `VisLayer` interface that can be extended, to define a variety of ways we can layer data onto a visualization. We list out a few below:

1. Point-in-time-event layering (`PointInTimeEventsVisLayer`). This layer can be used when we want to show a set of particular events occurring, such as anomalies or alerts.
2. Time-series layering (`TimeSeriesVisLayer`). This can be used to add an additional time series onto a visualization, possibly even changing the global time range for the visualization. An example of when this layer may be used is using forecasting to project forecasted data points in the future.

author: joshuarrrr
title: [Discuss] Separate out data source configurations from existing visualization types
body:
Today, one of the implicit assumptions in OpenSearch Dashboards visualization and dashboard implementations is that the data source for any visualization is likely the result of a query to OpenSearch. As we move toward support for [multiple datasources](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/1388), we need to make sure our visualization abstractions clearly separate visualization options and configurations from the source of the data.

We already have some existing abstractions to assist with this - for example most visualization rendering expression functions take `OpenSearchDashboardsDatatable` as their input. But we need to make sure the visualization types themselves are data source agnostic. In addition, it should be much easier for developers to "bring their own data" to a visualization - including doing so without understanding or knowing about the expression plugin.

We may even need to add support for other types of data formats or structures, in order to efficiently render data results from PPL queries (as currently implemented in the [Observability plugin](https://github.com/opensearch-project/observability).

author: ohltyler
title: Support vega-lite v5
body:
Currently Dashboards has a hard dependency on [vega-lite v4](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/main/package.json#L457). [v5](https://github.com/vega/vega-lite/releases/tag/v5.0.0) was released in early 2021 and provides a lot of functionality and simplicity improvements related to interactivity on the charts using _parameters_.

Upgrading will provide a lot of benefits:
- allow users to render vega-lite specs with v5 schema in the `vega` plugin
- simplify the implementation for annotation interaction functionality as part of the ongoing feature-anywhere projects
- prevent wasted dev work of migrating any chart types with vega-lite, which will need to be re-done when moving to v5

I've tried to get a v5 version of vega-lite working in Dashboards, but have run into some issues:
- Dashboards is using an [ES5-compatible build of vega-lite](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/main/src/plugins/vis_type_vega/public/lib/vega.js#L31-L32), which is offered by default in vega-lite v4's NPM packages
- v5 no longer supports ES5 builds out-of-the-box (see [breaking changes](https://github.com/vega/vega-lite/releases/tag/v5.0.0))

To address this, I've tried to follow guidance [here](https://vega.github.io/vega/usage/internet-explorer/) to use babel for transpiling the files into an ES5 bundle. I've played around with changing the [webpack config for the osd-optimizer package](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/main/packages/osd-optimizer/src/worker/webpack.config.ts) to specifically transpile the vega-lite package before bundling:
- commenting out the `noParse` arg [here](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/main/packages/osd-optimizer/src/worker/webpack.config.ts#L92)
- excluding the `vega-lite` node_module [here](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/main/packages/osd-optimizer/src/worker/webpack.config.ts#L208) so it would use the default babel loader
- adding a new entry specifically for `vega-lite` npm package, and trying different babel loaders (`@babel/preset-env`, the default `BABEL_PRESET_PATH`)

However, even when getting to transpile, it still seems to find non-ES5 code:
```
/node_modules/vega-lite/build/vega-lite.js:727
      deepMerge_(dest, s ?? {});
                          ^

SyntaxError: Unexpected token '?'
```

This seems to be a known issue - see https://github.com/vega/vega-lite/issues/7759, https://github.com/vega/vega-lite/pull/7595#issuecomment-888794365

From the comment [here](https://github.com/vega/vega-lite/issues/7759#issuecomment-946370406) it should be possible to configure the bundler to point to a correct target that will work, but I was unable to resolve the nullish operator error shown above.

author: abbyhu2000
title: Add manual instruction for VisBuilder saved object migration
body:
Here is an instruction on how users can manually migrate the previous visualizations created using earlier release version of VisBuilder. There are two changes to the stucture of the saved objects that created from VisBuilder since we release VisBuilder:

1. In 2.3 release, we change the way of storing index pattern: previously we save index pattern in the visualizationState, now we save index pattern following other saved object structure and using `kibanaSavedObjectMeta` attribute and the `references` array.
2. In 2.4 release, we change the type name of the visualizations created by VisBuilder from `wizard` to `visualization-visbuilder`.

### Migration steps

1. Before updating to later release version, export the existing visualizations created by VisBuilder:
    a. Navigate to `Stack Management` page
    b. Select `Saved Object` page
    c. Select the visualizations created using VisBuilder
    d. Click `Export` button that's next to the `Delete` button
    e. Toggle off `Include related objects` option and click `Export`
2. If any visualizations are associated with any dashboards, for each associated dashboard, also export into json files following similar steps
3. Open the exported json files for visualizations, make the corresponding changes and save the changes
    a. If the visualizations are created using VisBuilder in release version 2.3, for each visualization: 
        - locate `type` attribute, and change `wizard` to `visualization-visbuilder`
    b. If the visualizations are created using VisBuilder in release versions earlier than 2.3, for each visualization: 
        - locate `type` attribute, and change `wizard` to `visualization-visbuilder`
        - locate `visualizationState` and delete the index pattern related string
        - add a new attribute name `kibanaSavedObjectMeta` with `indexRefName: kibanaSavedObjectMeta.searchSourceJSON.index`
        - locate attribute named `references` and add a new object with index pattern information
        For example, previous json
           
```
           "attributes":{
                "description":"",
                "styleState":"{\"addTooltip\":true,\"addLegend\":false,\"type\":\"metric\",\"metric\":{\"percentageMode\":false,\"useRanges\":false,\"colorSchema\":\"Green to Red\",\"metricColorMode\":\"None\",\"colorsRange\":[{\"from\":0,\"to\":10000}],\"labels\":{\"show\":true},\"invertColors\":false,\"style\":{\"bgFill\":\"#000\",\"bgColor\":false,\"labelColor\":false,\"subText\":\"\",\"fontSize\":60}}}",
                "title":"wizard 1",
                "version":1,
                "visualizationState":"{\"searchField\":\"\",\"activeVisualization\":{\"name\":\"metric\",\"aggConfigParams\":[{\"id\":\"1\",\"enabled\":true,\"type\":\"cardinality\",\"params\":{\"field\":\"currency\"},\"schema\":\"metric\"},{\"id\":\"3\",\"enabled\":true,\"type\":\"cardinality\",\"params\":{\"field\":\"customer_full_name.keyword\"},\"schema\":\"metric\"}]},\"indexPattern\":\"ff959d40-b880-11e8-a6d9-e546fe2bba5f\"}"},
                "id":"bfe96550-5ae8-11ed-abb8-dbba5c796c9a",
                "references":[],
                "type":"wizard",
                "updated_at":"2022-11-02T19:58:41.701Z",
                "version":"WzUxLDFd"
            }
```
  
          
should change to


            
```
            "attributes":{
                "description":"",
                "kibanaSavedObjectMeta":{
                    "searchSourceJSON":"{\"indexRefName\":\"kibanaSavedObjectMeta.searchSourceJSON.index\"}"
                },
                "styleState":"{\"addTooltip\":true,\"addLegend\":false,\"type\":\"metric\",\"metric\":{\"percentageMode\":false,\"useRanges\":false,\"colorSchema\":\"Green to Red\",\"metricColorMode\":\"None\",\"colorsRange\":[{\"from\":0,\"to\":10000}],\"labels\":{\"show\":true},\"invertColors\":false,\"style\":{\"bgFill\":\"#000\",\"bgColor\":false,\"labelColor\":false,\"subText\":\"\",\"fontSize\":60}}}",

author: zhongnansu
title: [MD] multiple datasource doesn't throw 401 error as expected when security plugin enabled
body:
### Issue description
Security-dashboards-plugin has below logic to detect any 401 error on the page, and enforce reload of the page to achieve log out. This was intended to handle the session time out. However, in MD use case, since data source client could also throw 401 error during connection, if provided with invalid auth. Current logic in security plugin couldn't distinguish if 401 is from `default opensearch cluster` or from `data source`.  And it will apply a reload, which overwrite the error toasts MD has, leading to a bad user experience.

https://github.com/opensearch-project/security-dashboards-plugin/blob/5d018b0130d311be625ad5dd00466054607a907b/public/utils/logout-utils.tsx#L38

### Solution
short term solution is to find places to cast all 401 error thrown by data source client to 400

- 401 error is returned by OSD request `/internal/search/<search-strategy>` which is defined in `data` plugin
- the request flow is 
Create DS with wrong credential -> create index-pattern with this DS -> use index pattern to search  ->  `search_intercepter.ts`(client) issue the request -> `search_strategy`(server side) get the request -> `opensearch-js client` forward the request to talk to OS -> get 401  --> **`data plugin server side` error handler -**>  **http router error handler** -> **security plugin error intercepter at http router layer** -> **search intercepter error handler** -> Browser(client)

author: abbyhu2000
title: Reminder for unsaved dashboard when navigating away
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

If we need to make changes to a current dashboard, we click Edit button. Then the dashboard will be in edit mode, and the changes will only be saved when we click save button. 

The only indication of an unsaved dashboard is the (unsave) string on the breadcrumb. However, if we navigate to a different page, there is no reminder that the dashboard is not saved. Should we consider adding a pop up reminder window? 

Also one interesting thing is that even we navigate to a different page without clicking 'save' on that dashboard, and later we click dashboard tab under the menu, it will just take us back directly to that unsaved dashboard page, and the changes we made earlier will remain there on the UI. It seems like they embedded the information in the URL.

For example, if we create a new visualization on the dashboard, the visualization will show up on the dashboard. Without clicking the save button for dashboard, we navigate to saved object page. The relationship will not be shown under saved object since we did not save. But if we click dashboard tab(it will just navigate to that unsaved dashboard page), or we just traverse back to that old URL, the new visualization will remain shown on the UI. But if we do something else like clicking the dashboard breadcrumb so we see a list of current dashboard, and then go to that specific dashboard again, the changes will be lost.

![Screen Shot 2022-10-14 at 4 04 30 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43937633/195955867-3d8d4bb6-a245-4cd5-b1f4-cac47226ba1a.png)

author: ashwin-pc
title: [BUG] count and value_count Metric aggregation types misclassified and missing
body:
**Describe the bug**

In OpenSearch Dashboards, we have `count` defined as a [metric aggregation](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/2.2/src/plugins/data/common/search/aggs/metrics/metric_agg_types.ts#L38). There is however no metric aggregation of type `count` in OpenSearch Core and it seems to use the `bucket.doc_count` metadata field as its value.

Similarly `value_count` is in fact a [valid **metric** aggregation type in OpenSearch Core](https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/opensearch/metric-agg/) but is missing in the list of [metric aggregation types](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/2.2/src/plugins/data/common/search/aggs/metrics/metric_agg_types.ts) in OpenSearch Dashboards. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/2.2/src/plugins/data/common/search/aggs/metrics/metric_agg_types.ts to see the listed aggregation types

**Expected behavior**

There should not be a discrepancy between the different aggregation types and their classifications between OpenSearch Core and OpenSearch Dashboards and what they do.

2.2

2.2

author: MonishaSukumar
title: [BUG] No data to display message due to missing data points
body:
ES query was optimized in a way to filter the buckets with null values and this has caused the missing data points from different resources resulting in No Data To Display.

In the series aggregation plugin basic sum function, we are trying to access the missing element in-between which breaks the loop, and data is not returned.

Input series we get:
[ 

    [ [ T1 , 1 ] , [ T2 , 0 ] , [ T3 , 1 ] ]  , 

    [ [ T1 , 1 ], [ T2 , 1 ] , [ T3 , 0 ] , [ T4 , 5 ] ]  ,  

    [ [ T1 , 0 ] , [ T3 , 1 ] , [ T4 , 0 ] ]  ,

]          

Expected Series:

[  

     [ [ T1 , 1 ] , [ T2 , 0 ] , [ T3 , 1 ] , [ T4 , 0 ] ]  , 

     [ [ T1 , 0 ] , [ T2 , 1 ] , [ T3 , 0 ] , [ T4 , 5 ] ]   ,  

     [ [ T1 , 0 ] , [ T2 , 0 ] , [ T3 , 1 ] , [ T4 , 0 ] ]   ,

]

So that above is in the expected form, the OpenSearch plugin takes each index data, performs the sum, and returns the total aggregated data.

Now we have added a fix in a way to fill the missing data points with empty values.

Can you please validate this approach / fix the issue?

How to use this issue

Please contact them or @mention them on this issue for help. Any release related work can be linked to this issue or added as comments to create visiblity into the release status. ## Release Steps There are several steps to the release process; these steps are completed as the whole component release and components that are behind present risk to the release. The component owner resolves the tasks in this issue and communicate with the overall release owner to make sure each component are moving along as expected. Steps have completion dates for coordinating efforts between the components of a release; components can start as soon as they are ready far in advance of a future release. The most current set of dates is on the overall release issue linked at the top of this issue. ## The Overall Release Issue Linked at the top of this issue, the overall release issue captures the state of the entire OpenSearch release including references to this issue, the release owner which is the assignee is responsible for communicating the release status broadly. Please contact them or @mention them on that issue for help. ## What should I do if my plugin isn't making any changes? author: joshuarrrr
title: [D&D] Make new "meta" state slice to keep track of things we don't want to save and load
body:
After #1870, we need to further [expand and refine the behavior of `hasUnappliedChanges`](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/8c50d0f87d4036e5bdb7bb18a09a3f52f214e6b3/src/plugins/wizard/public/application/components/top_nav.tsx#L29-L31).

We should keep track of whether the canvas is in a savable state or not, and only enable the save button when the current state is valid _and_ the canvas is rendering the current state. The best way of doing so may be creating a new "meta" state slice, which we can use to keep track of this (and other properties) that we don't want to include in save and load payloads.

- [ ] Save button should be disabled with an empty canvas, or any time there's not yet enough required information to render a vis
- [x] Save button should be disabled when agg editing suspends realtime updates
- [ ] Save button should be disabled when there have been no changes to a loaded vis
- [ ] [Tooltip](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/8c50d0f87d4036e5bdb7bb18a09a3f52f214e6b3/src/plugins/wizard/public/application/utils/get_top_nav_config.tsx#L75-L81) and/or toast should provide info on why the vis is not saveable and how to fix
- [ ] Savable state should not be part of `Visualization` or `Style` slices, because it should not be saved/loaded.

author: ashwin-pc
title: [Discuss] Developer docs website
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

This has been brought up a few times in different places. Opening the issue here since it looks like the goal of the documentation and project website do not cover developer docs. There are 2 personas that i'm trying to solve for here.

1. A plugin developer: These are users that ideally should not need to look at the OSD codebase to make plugins that extend OSD. This is mostly possible today with the current plugin architecture, but the documentation needed to help such a developer is incomplete and scattered across the repo. This makes it such that a plugin developer must also be very familiar with OSD code and adding unnecessary friction to developing plugins.
2. OSD Developers: These are users who contribute directly OSD. They too require some of the information that plugin developers need, but they should also be familiar with OSD code and can rely to some extent on readme's in the code.

While markdown is powerful, there are some pitfalls by only relying on it to address our gaps in documentation for the two persona's mentioned above:

- The docs are scattered (they are kept local to the component they are describing) so finding the relevant information can become tedious.
- Cant incorporate features such as tutorials, search and nav tree to name a few
- Requires the user to explore the OSD repo (For plugin developers, this is not ideal)

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A developer docs website that contains informations such as:
- Overview
  - Core concepts
  - High level architecture
- Plugins
  - Plugin Architecture
  - Plugin framework
  - Core plugins and docs for each plugin
- Tutorials
  - How to build a plugin
  - How to add a visualization
  - How to create a new expression
- Best practices
  - Performance
  - Styleguide
  - Testing
- API's
- Other resources
  - Local env setup (this is the same for contributors and plugin developers today but that might change in the future)
  - Design system (EUI or its equivalent that we will use)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

This could also be an auto generated doc site using the readme's in the repository. However this will be quite limiting for the breath of information that we have. Once we decople plugin development from having to build Dashboards, plugin developers should not have to refer to docs from the repo directly. A separate developer doc site solves that problem too. 

**Additional context**

Existing issues for context:
- https://github.com/opensearch-project/documentation-website/issues/492
- https://github.com/opensearch-project/documentation-website/issues/419#issuecomment-1048102288
- https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/778
- https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/1100

author: zhongnansu
title: [PoC] Efficient client management to support multiple OpenSearch clusters
body:
## Problem Statement

As part of https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/1388, to support Dashboards connecting to multiple OpenSearch Cluster, the thread discussed adding a new saved object `datasource`, and referenced to the data model of `index-pattern`. There's also a proposed [POC PR](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/1430). 

There's an issue with the POC code. When it establishes the connection with external datasource, it was using the @opensearch-js client in the search strategy. 

https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/beb46f55cb86d076f3d8c7a4a3fb454cf538ab56/src/plugins/data/server/search/opensearch_search/ext_opensearch_search_strategy.ts#L87-L93

This is not resource efficient since it creates a connection for each and every query. We need better approach to do client management. 

## Proposed Solution [WIP]
We can take a look at how clients are managed in Dashboards core. The lifecycle starts when Dashboards-core plugin is spinning up, it creates 2 client and registers to the core context to expose to other modules through http services. It can spawn child clients as needed(AsScopedClient) from auth in request, which returns a new client instance that shares the connection pool with the parent client. If you call `close` in any of the parent/child clients, every client will be closed. The connections close when Dashboards stops.

We may consider adding one more client only for external data source, to the `ClusterClient` class. And wire our logic to spawn child clients as needed, from `datasource`. Similar to `asScoped` function.

https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/4469d174ad119556357a1fdb4633b8aa62cd59a6/src/core/server/opensearch/client/cluster_client.ts#L76-L79

https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/4469d174ad119556357a1fdb4633b8aa62cd59a6/src/core/server/opensearch/client/cluster_client.ts#L91-L98


### POC is needed and I am currently working on it
Changes need to make
- [x] 1. Along with `asCurrentUser` and `asInternalUser`, define a new interface `asDataSourceUser`, for `context.core.client` to call
- [x] 2. Create the third client in `cluster_client` only for data Source
- [x] 3. Register above client to core context
- [x] 4. import save_object client to the `core Context`, in order to retrieve data source meta info, that will be used to establish connection
- [ ] 5. adjust client config as needed(header, ssl). May need add new parsing logic specific for `dataSourceClient`
- [ ] *code style adjustment. Expose clean interfaces

title: type mismatch issue in src/core/server/saved_objects
body:
**Describe the issue**

When hook up node js client, we found some type mismatch issue in src/core/server/saved_objects. Most of them are from test files. Currently we ignore the errors. Might need to take further investigation to find mitigate the mismatches. Use one example here:

**src/core/server/saved_objects/migrations/core/index_migrator.ts** (line 210)
// @ts-expect-error @opensearch-project/opensearch _source is optional

This is because:
`const docs = await read() and type is opensearchtypes.SearchHit<SavedObjectsRawDocSource>[]`

SearchHit is defined in nodejs client as:
```
export interface SearchHit<TDocument = unknown> {
  _index: IndexName
  _id: Id
  _score?: double
  _type?: Type
  _explanation?: ExplainExplanation
  fields?: Record<string, any>
  highlight?: Record<string, string[]>
  inner_hits?: Record<string, SearchInnerHitsResult>
  matched_queries?: string[]
  _nested?: SearchNestedIdentity
  _ignored?: string[]
  _shard?: string
  _node?: string
  _routing?: string
  _source?: TDocument
  _seq_no?: SequenceNumber
  _primary_term?: long
  _version?: VersionNumber
  sort?: SearchSortResults
}
```
Here _source is optional. But migrateRawDocs function requires docs `rawDocs: SavedObjectsRawDoc[],`

src/core/server/saved_objects/serialization/types.ts :
```
export interface SavedObjectsRawDoc {
  _id: string;
  _source: SavedObjectsRawDocSource;
  _type?: string;
  _seq_no?: number;
  _primary_term?: number;
}
```
Here _source is not optional.

**Files and issues**

**src/core/server/saved_objects/migrations/core/index_migrator.ts** 
// @ts-expect-error @opensearch-project/opensearch _source is optional

**src/core/server/saved_objects/service/lib/repository.ts**
// @ts-expect-error MultiGetHit._source is optional
// @ts-expect-error @opensearch-project/opensearch _source is optional
// @ts-expect-error MultiGetHit is incorrectly missing _id, _source

author: kavilla
title: [Docs] Onboard release-drafter for release notes
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

For the [1.3 release](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/1282), we had to generate release notes for the build. Our usual process has been checkout on `main`, install a package, enter the range of commits for that package then the notes will be built. However, since `main` has commits that cannot go into `1.x` and some commits are not the same as the commits on `main`. So we would have to cross check, the commits from the previous release to the major release to make sure duplication isn't there which is human-error prone. So for 1.3 the [PR](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/1348), we checked out on `1.x`, then continued the process. 

Then also cleaned up what was generated. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Onboard https://github.com/release-drafter/release-drafter, like other @opensearch-project repos, and add the workflow to pull the commits that are labelled for that specific release and add it to a release notes doc.

n/a

author: jbuchmueller
title: TSVB Time Series Custom Color Mapping
body: **Problem Statement** I am creating a dashboard for visualizing states of a process (see image). The data I use consists of temporal event data in four categories (1-4). The dashboard displays different views on this dataset: First, a gantt chart i coded in Vega Lite displaying the event sequences and durations. Second, a OS-native pie chart visualization displaying the ratios between the event types aggregated for 24 hours. And lastly, a TSVB time series visualization displaying the ratios between the event types for the past 7 days in steps of 24 hours. This is how it looks like: Naturally, the same information should be encoded in the same color in each view. While I can customize the color mappings in vega lite and OS-native visualizations, to the best of my knowledge, this does not seem to be possible for TSVB time series, which rely on some sort of serverside predefined color mapping. Yet, I would like to be able to edit the color mapping to create consistent dashboards that are more accessible to observers. **Solution Proposal** Ideally, I would like to have a menu option in the TSVB time series GUI to assign colors to categories, maybe with a color picker as in the standard visualizations, if possible (While the color picker also should allow for individual selection instead of only predefined palettes). Preliminary, I would also be fine with a possibility to configure the colors using the saved objects editor, as I did for the Pie/Donut Chart by setting the uiStateJSON. I sincerely hope, that this possibility does not already exist. In case it did, it would need much better documentation, as I was not able to find any information on the topic.

author: tmarkley
title: [Build] Upgrade from Webpack 4 to 5
body:
Webpack 5 was [released in October, 2020](https://webpack.js.org/blog/2020-10-10-webpack-5-release/#root) and provides performance and compatibility improvements.

Additionally, Webpack 4 is blocking at least one CVE fix. #1066 requires an upgrade to `webpack@5.x` because `node-sass@6.x` depends on a vulnerable version of `json-schema`. In order to bump to `node-sass@7.x` to mitigate this vulnerability, `sass-loader` also has to be upgraded from v10 to v12. However, [v11 dropped support](https://github.com/webpack-contrib/sass-loader/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#1100-2021-02-05) for `webpack@4.x`.

Webpack provides a [complete list of changes required](https://webpack.js.org/migrate/5/) for the migration from 4 to 5.

## WS-2020-0026 - High Severity Vulnerability
Vulnerable Library - ammo-3.0.1.tgz

HTTP Range processing utilities

All versions of ammo are vulnerable to Denial of Service. author: peterzhuamazon
title: [Build] Plugin Zip naming using MIN version instead of Plugin Version
body:
### Describe the bug

In Dashboards, when plugin is generated using build workflow, the zips will be named as `pluginName-<3digits>.zip`, example: `reportsDashboards-1.1.0.zip`. 

This is different from OpenSearch, which is using 4 digit as it should `index-management-1.1.0.0.zip`, and cause more issues in the building process.

The 3digit number is coming from the Dashboards Core version, not the plugin version at all. If I want to build 1.1.1.0 dashboards plugin with 1.1.0 core (core not change), the output zip will still be `reportsDashboards-1.1.0.zip`, adding up confusion.

Suggest dashboards changing their plugin naming to `reportsDashboards-1.1.1.0.zip` format for all plugins.
Plugin owner is actually running cp commands to rename zips after they build it in their ci workflow to avoid this confusion.
https://github.com/opensearch-project/dashboards-reports/blob/1.1/.github/workflows/dashboards-reports-test-and-build-workflow.yml#L69

We should not do this anymore and the plugin zips should have the correct naming from the start.

Thanks.

author: rursprung
title: Support JWT for service to service (Dashboards to OpenSearch) communication
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
currently, OpenSearch Dashboards can only be configured to use basic authentication or certificate-based authentication to talk to OpenSearch. this means that even if these two are not used for anything else one of these realms would have to be enabled & configured in OpenSearch in order to use OpenSearch Dashboards - and with that then also comes the overhead of either managing a shared secret (basic auth) or managing certificates.

note: this is *not* about the authentication of GUI users (where JWT is possible), this is about the stuff which is configured with the `opensearch.username` & `opensearch.password` config parameters (which, btw, don't seem to be documented yet? it's only visible in the docs of other topics as part of the examples where they're also still set to `kibanauser` even though the Kibana name should be gone?)

**Describe the solution you'd like**
it should be possible to use other authentication methods in OpenSearch Dashboards (best-case: any realm supported by OpenSearch).
for our specific setup we'd like to use JWT. for that, a callback (could e.g. be provided as a plugin?) would have to be available which can then obtain the token (this would be specific to the environment, AFAIK there's no global standard (yet) on how to do this).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
* using basic authentication would force the usage of a shared secret. in a fully automated deployment world this would have to be generated upon initial deployment and the user would have to be created in OpenSearch with this login information and the secret would have to be provided to OpenSearch Dashboards (e.g. as a Kubernetes `Secret`, requiring the creation logic to also have the rights to create such resources in the k8s cluster)
* using certificate-based authentication would require managing such certificates and ensuring that they also work when certificate rotations happen. AFAIK (there's 0 documentation about this in OpenSearch Dashboards, but if it's still similar to Search Guard then their caveat applies (see the note at the end of [their docs](https://docs.search-guard.com/latest/kibana-plugin-installation)) this also means that the rights associated with the certificate are combined with the rights of users in any calls done by users which is of course not the intention.

**Additional context**
i'm explicitly asking for JWT here, but depending on the way this is being built this could be a refactoring where the authentication mechanism is moved to a plugin and the possibility exists to drop in any plugin which implements the API for a specific auth mechanism, meaning even people who run their custom auth realm could use this auth realm also for / instead of the `kibanaserver` user.

author: carloseustaquio
title: Add proxy option on Router
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I'm working on an OpenSearch Dashboard plugin where I need to handle the front-end requests on a different back-end server. Request: `client ==> /server ==> /custom-backend`. 
I was using a BFF approach, redirecting every request manually, but it's been very painful and verbose.
```
client ==> /server/endpoint-1 ==> /custom-backend/endpoint-1
client ==> /server/endpoint-2 ==> /custom-backend/endpoint-2
client ==> /server/endpoint-3 ==> /custom-backend/endpoint-3
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Since the hapi.js server has a route proxy option, I'd like to propose exposing this proxy option as a method in the router interface. This way, we only need to set up the proxy endpoint and it will redirect every request to my backend service.
```
path= "/server"
proxyPath = "/custom-backend"

client ==> +----------------------+ ==> /custom-backend/endpoint-1
client ==> |  Proxy  /server    | ==> /custom-backend/endpoint-2
client ==> +----------------------+ ==> /custom-backend/endpoint-3
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

I considered turning my custom back-end public and sending the front-end requests directly to it, but, doing so, I would lose the integration with the Dashboard Security plugin that is handling authentication in my application.

**Additional context**

I forked the OpenSearch and worked out a solution. I'd like to share it with the community, and see if it would be a good feature for other people.

author: kavilla
title: [BUG] artifact downloading fails for RC
body:
**Describe the bug**
[artifact.js](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/main/packages/osd-opensearch/src/artifact.js) downloads artifacts so that integration tests and functional tests work right out of the box. The artifacts need to exist and the URL needs to be a certain format to access the artifacts and download them. However, the release-candidates URL format has changed.

 It went from `https://artifacts.opensearch.org/snapshots/core/opensearch/VERSION=SNAPSHOT-rcN` to `https://artifacts.opensearch.org/release-candidates/core/opensearch/VERSION/`

If we version bump and running integ/func tests, it will try to search for an artifact that might not exist for the default format in which case it will revert to searching the release candidates. A RC artifact should exist but it wont be able to find it in the current format so some integ tests and all the functional tests will fail out of the box.

**Workaround**
Set `TEST_OPENSEARCH_FROM` locally to the current version of OpenSearch. But this breaks all CI pipelines.

**Expected result**
Integ tests and functional tests work out of the box and works in any automation.

author: kavilla
title: [BUG] Node-RE2 build missing for ARM
body:
**Describe the bug**
This bug existed pre-fork with the error message including: `node_modules/re2/build/Release/re2.node: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory`. It turns out the application uses node-re2 so that it can safely use the regular expressions specified by end-users within Timeline, but [Node-RE2](https://github.com/uhop/node-re2) does not contain a hosted build for ARM. So it fails while hosted on machines with ARM architecture since it doesn't exist.

**Steps to reproduce**
* On an applicable platform for example something like graviton2 
* Logon to OpenSearch Dashboards and load sample web log data
* Go to visualize and create a Timeline visualization
* type in query .es(split=host.keyword:50, index=opensearch_dashboards_sample_data_logs).label("Host Name: $1", "^.:(.) >.*")

**Additional context**
The pre-fork repo issue number was: #83012

What the pre-fork did to solve this was build an ARM version and hosted on their own archives site then updated [patch_native_modules_task.ts](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/main/src/dev/build/tasks/patch_native_modules_task.ts#L50) to pull that hosted build (pre-fork repo PR #84163).

Since they own that site we probably don't want to just simply pull that build so we should find a replacement to be hosted or verify legally if that falls under the "magic category". The magic category meaning it is required to build and run so we can't change it right away, for example like the default index remaining the same. If we do find out we need to host it we need to figure out where it can be hosted for easy access. We could also verify if the dependency host builds for ARM now or if there exists a better dependency with full builds.

**Requirements to solve**
* Verify the error exists for OpenSearch Dashboards
* Verify if we can reuse the link provided by the pre-fork of the hosted build or if we need to host it
  * If we do need to host our own build we will need to build and then figure out where to host perhaps under: https://artifacts.opensearch.org
* Implement the solution

For clusters with a lot of data to move or large clusters, this could manifest as a long maintenance window or outage.

**To Reproduce**

1. Bootstrap ES (OSS) 7.10 cluster.
2. Join OpenSearch node to ES cluster.
3. Install OpenSearch-Dashboards on OpenSearch node.
4. Start OpenSearch-Dashboards and tail the log.
5. Observe `{"type":"log","@timestamp":"2021-07-02T19:53:50Z","tags":["error","savedobjects-service"],"pid":14817,"message":"This version of OpenSearch Dashboards (v1.0.0-SNAPSHOT) is incompatible with the following OpenSearch nodes in your cluster: v7.10.2 @ 172.16.4.117:9200 (172.16.4.117), v7.10.0 @ 172.16.4.21:9200 (172.16.4.21)"}`
6. Run `curl localhost:5601`
7. Observe `OpenSearch Dashboards server is not ready yet`

**Expected behavior**
OpenSearch-Dashboards should function against a transitioning-to-OpenSearch 1.0 cluster.

**OpenSearch Version**

Tried both

- 1.0.0-rc1
- 1.1.0-SNAPSHOT@8082604ec273ffdb50046f53af3d2553a106c9fb

**Dashboards Version**
1.0.0-SNAPSHOT@45df886890f2039d88f9675d401f2c7c85ce781e

**Plugins**

None

**Screenshots**

N/A

**Host/Environment**
 - OS: Debian Buster

**Additional context**

The two nodes referenced in the above error message are the two remaining ES nodes of a 5-node cluster.

I also tried kibana-oss 7.10 and received a similar error message: `{"type":"log","@timestamp":"2021-07-02T20:16:31Z","tags":["error","savedobjects-service"],"pid":15725,"message":"This version of Kibana (v7.10.0) is incompatible with the following Elasticsearch nodes in your cluster: v1.0.0 @ 172.16.1.86:9200 (172.16.1.86), v1.1.0 @ 172.16.2.223:9200 (172.16.2.223), v1.0.0 @ 172.16.3.147:9200 (172.16.3.147)"}`

author: peterzhuamazon
title: De-Couple Dashboards building process with modular approach
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

When running `yarn build --skip-os-packages` it will build 4 tarballs for Dashboards (2x linux, 1x macOS, 1x windows) and takes 10+min to do so.

Compares to OpenSearch, running `./gradlew :distribution:archives:linux-tar:assemble` will only build 1 tarball (1x linux) to be exact and takes 2min.

Overall, Dashboards takes longer to build artifacts compares to OpenSearch, and produces additional outcomes that are not needed for specific builds (e.g. I want to only build linux x64 artifacts, not all of them at once).


**Describe the solution you'd like**

It would be beneficial if we break down Dashboards building process modularly into small tasks, so that each task can take significantly less time.

This would also benefit robust CI/CD workflows and reduce the overhead for Dashboards later on.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered.

author: geekygirldawn
title: Maintainer Areas of Responsibility
body:
It would be great if we could also add people's areas of responsibilities to the new [MAINTAINERS file](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md). This helps people understand which of these maintainers is responsible for a particular area. We could add this as a new column to the existing table or as a separate section of the file. I'm happy to do if someone wanted to let me know which people are responsible for what.

Here's an [example](https://github.com/goharbor/community/blob/master/MAINTAINERS.md).

The motivation for my suggestion is to help the rest of us outside of Amazon better understand the maintainers and what they are likely to be working on. The key here is likely and not exclusively. Having a bit more info helps the rest of us:
* understand who to talk to if we need to escalate a PR if it gets neglected for a long time or if something urgent comes up.
* learn about potential gaps that we could fill - maybe no one from Amazon is focused in a particular area that one of us has expertise in.
* we're all individuals interacting with each other, and if we all know a bit more about the people in leadership positions, it can help the rest of us understand where you're coming from.

author: yubonluo
title: [RFC] Explore dashboard UX Simplification Proposal
body: # Background In OpenSearch Dashboards, the Observability workspace provides a dedicated environment focused on observability use cases. Within this workspace, Dashboard is the primary interface for users to view and analyze data. Currently, the Dashboard header area contains the following components: * DQL (Dashboards Query Language) search bar: for global data querying and filtering at the Dashboard level * Filter button: for adding and managing field-level filter conditions * Time picker: for controlling the data time range In the Observability workspace, Dashboards primarily host Explore-type visualization panels. Explore is a more modern visualization approach where each panel has its own built-in query editor and data exploration capabilities, allowing users to write and adjust queries directly within the panel. Additionally, Dashboard supports defining [Variables](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/11550). Variables allow users to define reusable parameters and dynamically inject them into queries through explicit template syntax. Variables are primarily designed to work with Explore visualization panels — when a user changes a variable value in the Dashboard, Explore panels automatically receive the variable update and re-execute their queries, enabling dynamic data filtering. This means that in the Observability workspace, the user's primary data filtering and interaction paths are: 1. Switching filter conditions dynamically through Variable dropdown selectors 2. Performing more granular data exploration through the built-in query editor within each Explore panel The DQL search bar and Filter button in the Dashboard header become redundant in this context — they overlap with the interaction model of Explore panels while adding unnecessary complexity to the interface. # Intent We want to simplify the Dashboard header in the Observability workspace by removing the DQL search bar and Filter button UI, with the following goals: 1. Reduce interface complexity: Remove unnecessary UI elements to make the interface cleaner and more focused 2. Streamline the interaction path: Guide users to filter and explore data through Variables and Explore panels, rather than relying on global DQL queries and non-explore visualization 3. Avoid interaction confusion: Eliminate potential conflicts and confusion between Dashboard-level global queries and Explore panel-level queries # Scope ## In Scope * Hide the DQL search bar in the Dashboard header within the Observability workspace * Hide the Filter button in the Dashboard header within the Observability workspace * Disable Controls Visualization (interactive dropdown lists and range sliders) in the Observability workspace, as they fundamentally generate Dashboard-level filters * Retain the time picker, as time range control remains a universal need at the Dashboard level ## Out of Scope * No changes to Dashboard behavior in non-Observability workspaces * No changes to the query and interaction capabilities of Explore panels themselves * No changes to the existing Filter/DQL search/Controls Visualization functions for the dashboard that had utilize them. * No changes to Variable functionality and behavior # Discussion Points ## Impact on Dashboards already using Filters and Search Bar There are approximately a lot of dashboards in Observability workspaces currently using filters or DQL queries. Here are several options for handling this: ### Option1 Direct Removal UI Hide the DQL search bar and filter button in the Observability workspace unconditionally. Saved filters/queries remain in the saved object but the UI entry points are removed. Pros: - Cleanest code, no extra conditional

author: ruchidh
title: [Infra] Add GitHub repo health agent for automated maintenance
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem?

The OpenSearch Dashboards repo has growing maintenance overhead:
- 100+ stale issues with no activity for 30+ days (some since 2021)
- 50+ stale PRs sitting open with no updates
- Unlabeled issues that don't get triaged
- No automated visibility into repo health trends (issue/PR velocity, review bottlenecks)
- Manual effort needed to track what's happening across the repo

### Describe the solution you'd like

A GitHub repo health agent that runs automatically via GitHub Actions:

**Daily (8 AM UTC):**
- Detect stale issues/PRs (30+ days no activity) and add `stale` label
- Auto-label unlabeled issues and PRs using keyword matching (bug/enhancement/question/security + component tags like Discover, Query Editor, Visualization, etc.)

**Weekly (Monday 9 AM UTC):**
- Generate a health summary: issue/PR velocity, avg merge time, PR review bottlenecks, top components, hot issues
- Post formatted report to Slack via Block Kit

**On-demand:**
- Available as a Claude skill and Kiro prompt for interactive use

### Additional context

Tested against live repo data (April 2026):
- 25 issues opened vs 5 closed this week (net +20, backlog growing)
- 23 PRs merged, avg 39h to merge
- 10 PRs stuck without review for 7+ days
- Auto-labeling correctly classified unlabeled issues (#11730 -> Dashboards/Plugins, #11705 -> enhancement)

Phase 1 implementation is ready. Future phases include Claude-powered smart labeling, duplicate detection, trend analysis, and frontend oncall knowledge sharing.

Related: exploring collaboration with OpenSearchDevAICapabilities package for reusable skills.

author: ruanyl
title: [RFC] Multi-Field Axis Support in Explore Visualizations
body:
# Multi-Field Axis Support in Explore Visualizations

## 1. Motivation

Explore's visualization system maps data columns to axis roles (X, Y, Color, Facet, etc.) to determine how a chart is rendered. Today, each axis role accepts exactly one column. This creates a gap for common analytical workflows:

- A user querying `| stats avg(cpu_usage), avg(memory_usage) by span(timestamp, 1h)` cannot plot both numerical fields on the same Y-axis without first reshaping the data into a long format with a COLOR split dimension.
- Comparing multiple measures side-by-side (e.g., revenue vs. cost over time) requires workarounds that don't exist in the current UI.

## 2. Requirements

### Functional

1. Users can assign multiple data columns to a single axis role where it makes sense (e.g., multiple numerical fields on Y-axis for line, bar, and area charts).
2. The axis selector UI supports adding, replacing, and removing individual fields within a multi-field axis.
3. Chart type auto-detection and rule matching correctly handle multi-field axes — a rule declaring `multi: true` on an axis accepts one or more columns of the specified type.
4. Existing single-field workflows remain unchanged — single-field axes are a degenerate case of multi-field axes.

### Non-Functional

1. Backward compatible with existing persisted URL state (single-string axis mappings).

## 3. Technical Design

### 3.1 Type System

The design introduces a `multi` flag at the rule definition level and lifts axis column mappings from single values to arrays.

**Rule-level declaration** — Each axis in a `VisRule` mapping can optionally declare `multi: true`:

```typescript
// A line chart rule: X takes one date field, Y takes one or more numerical fields
{
  [AxisRole.X]: { type: VisFieldType.Date },
  [AxisRole.Y]: { type: VisFieldType.Numerical, multi: true },
}
```

**Internal column mappings** — `AxisColumnMappings` changes from `Partial<Record<AxisRole, VisColumn>>` to `Partial<Record<AxisRole, VisColumn[]>>`. Every axis uniformly holds an array; single-field axes are arrays of length 1.

**Serialized form** — A new `AxisFieldNameMappings` type (`Partial<Record<string, string | string[]>>`) is used for URL state and cross-component communication. Single strings and string arrays are both valid, ensuring backward compatibility with existing persisted state.

### 3.2 Visualization Registry

The registry is the central authority for rule matching and auto-mapping. Three capabilities are extended:

**Auto-mapping columns to axes** — When the registry encounters a `multi: true` axis during auto-mapping, it assigns all remaining columns of the matching type to that axis (instead of just one). This means a dataset with three numerical columns and one date column can auto-map to a line chart with X=date, Y=[num1, num2, num3].

**Rule matching** — When determining which rule fits a given axis configuration, the registry now considers cardinality: a `multi` rule axis accepts both single and multiple fields, while a non-multi rule axis rejects multiple fields. This prevents a single-Y rule from matching when the user has selected multiple Y fields.

### 3.3 Data Aggregation

The `aggregate()` transformation function accepts `field: string | string[]`. When given an array, it aggregates each field independently within the same group key. The grouped accumulator collects values per field (`valuesByField: Record<string, number[]>`), and the output row contains one aggregated value per field. This avoids running separate aggregation passes for each field.

### 3.4 Chart Option Builders

Each chart type's `to_expression.ts` receives strongly-typed axis mappings from the render function. For multi-field axes, the builder maps over the array of value fields to produce multiple ECharts series entries. For example, a line chart with Y=[sales, revenue] generates two line series sharing the same X-axis dataset.

The expression builders no longer perform axis swapping. A new `getAxisConfig(

## CVE-2025-62718 - Critical Severity Vulnerability
Vulnerable Library - axios-1.13.5.tgz

Library home page: https://registry.npmjs.org/axios/-/axios-1.13.5.tgz

Path to dependency file: /package.json

Found in HEAD commit: 53692bfb36eeaf93c526143e17e23f6ec54b4c23

Found in base branch: main

Vulnerability Details

Axios is a promise based HTTP client for the browser and Node.js. Prior to 1.15.0, Axios does not correctly handle hostname normalization when checking NO_PROXY rules. Requests to loopback addresses like localhost. (with a trailing dot) or [::1] (IPv6 literal) skip NO_PROXY matching and go through the configured proxy. This goes against what developers expect and lets attackers force requests through a proxy, even if NO_PROXY is set up to protect loopback or internal services. This issue leads to the possibility of proxy bypass and SSRF vulnerabilities allowing attackers to reach sensitive loopback or internal services despite the configured protections. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.15.0.

author: seraphjiang
title: [Proposal] Cross-Datasource Federated Query Engine for OpenSearch Dashboards
body:
# Cross-Datasource Federated Query Engine **Project:** Federated Query Engine **Status:** Incubation / Proposal **Date:** 2026-04-07 **Author:** Huan Jiang (seraphjiang@gmail.com) --- ## 1. Problem Statement OpenSearch Dashboards supports multiple data sources since v2.4, but with a critical limitation: **each data source is an isolated OpenSearch cluster**. Users cannot: - Run a single query that spans multiple OpenSearch clusters and merges results - Query heterogeneous data sources (OpenSearch + S3 + Prometheus) from one interface - JOIN, correlate, or aggregate data across different datasource types - Build dashboards that blend data from OpenSearch indices and S3 data lakes The existing federated PPL query engine (opensearch-project/sql#561) added Prometheus support on the backend, but explicitly scoped out cross-datasource JOINs and distributed execution. The multi-datasource UI plugin only provides a cluster selector — it doesn't federate queries. **There is no unified query layer that federates across heterogeneous datasources from the Dashboards UI.** --- ## 2. Opportunity | Use Case | Today | With Federated Engine | |----------|-------|-----------------------| | Search logs across 3 OpenSearch clusters | 3 separate queries, manual merge | `SEARCH logs FROM cluster_a, cluster_b, cluster_c WHERE status=500` | | Correlate OpenSearch logs with S3 archived data | Export → ETL → re-ingest | `SELECT * FROM os.logs JOIN s3.archive ON trace_id` | | Dashboard mixing live metrics + cold storage | Not possible | Single dashboard, federated panels | | Aggregate across OpenSearch + Prometheus | Switch tools | `stats avg(cpu) FROM prometheus_prod UNION os_metrics` | This fills a gap that no existing OpenSearch component addresses and positions OpenSearch Dashboards as a true multi-source analytics hub. --- ## 3. Architecture ### 3.1 Current State ```mermaid graph TB subgraph OSD["OpenSearch Dashboards"] DSP["DataSource Plugin
(client mgmt)"] DSMP["DataSourceManagement Plugin
(UI selectors)"] end DSP -->|"getClient(dataSourceId)"| OS["OpenSearch Cluster A/B/C
Only OpenSearch clusters"] ``` ### 3.2 Proposed Architecture **Design decision:** The Federated Query Engine will be built as a **separate, standalone service** — not embedded in the OSD Node.js process. This allows us to choose the right language and stack optimized for performance, security, scalability, and resilience. The engine runs independently and is accessed by OpenSearch Dashboards via API. ```mermaid graph TB subgraph OSD["OpenSearch Dashboards (UI Layer)"] QB["Query Bar / Visual Builder"] DP["Dashboard Panels"] end QB --> API["Federated Query API"] DP --> API subgraph FQE["Federated Query Engine Service (Separate Service)"] QP["Query Parser
& Rewriter"] QPO["Query Planner
& Optimizer"] RM["Result Merger
& Transformer"] QP --> QPO --> RM QPO --> OSC["OpenSearch
Connector"] QPO --> S3C["S3/Glue
Connector"] QPO --> PC["Prometheus
Connector"] QPO --> MC["...more
connectors"] end API --> FQE OSC --> OS["OpenSearch
Cluster A/B/C"] S3C --> S3["S3 + Glue
Data Lake"] PC --> PM["Prometheus
Server"] style FQE fill:#e1f5fe,stroke:#0288d1,stroke-width:3px style OSD fill:#f3e5f5,stroke:#7b1fa2 style API fill:#fff3e0,stroke:#f57c00,stroke-width:2px ``` **Why a separate service:** | Concern | Embedded (Node.js) | Separate Service | |---------|-------------------|------------------| | Performance | Single-threaded, GC pauses, memory-bound JOINs | Choose language optimized for compute (Rust, Go, Java) — true parallelism, zero-copy, streaming | | Security | Runs in OSD process with full UI context | Isolated process with minimal permissions, per-connector credential scoping, no UI attack surface | | Scalability | Scales with OSD instances

author: ishag4
title: Add OAuth2 / OIDC authentication support for Prometheus data source
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Currently, OpenSearch Dashboards supports only No Auth, Basic Auth, and AWS SigV4 for Prometheus data sources. However, many Prometheus deployments are secured using OAuth2 / OIDC (e.g., via identity providers or OAuth proxies).

This prevents integration with secure environments without introducing insecure workarounds.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- Add OAuth2 / OIDC authentication support
- Support client credentials flow
- Automatically attach Bearer tokens to requests
- Handle token refresh
- Provide UI configuration (client ID, secret, token URL, scopes, audiences)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Reverse proxy for token injection
- Disabling auth (not acceptable)

**Additional context**

Impact:
This would enable integration with modern, secure Prometheus deployments and align OpenSearch with industry-standard authentication mechanisms.

Please let me know if this direction makes sense. I’d be glad to help contribute to the implementation.
