author: angle943
title: [RFC] New Discover experience for Observability Workspaces
body:
## New Discover Experience for Observability Workspaces

The OpenSearch Dashboard(OSD) team is working on vastly improving the Discover experience in 2025 for [Observability Workspaces](https://docs.opensearch.org/docs/latest/dashboards/workspace/workspace/). We want OSD to be the tool users reach for when they want to dive deep into logs. To achieve this goal, we are making several changes:

### Make PPL the default language

While [Dashboard Query Language (DQL)](https://docs.opensearch.org/docs/latest/dashboards/dql/) has been a great experience for many users in discovering their OpenSearch data, it is not compatible with exploring data outside of OpenSearch indexes. Therefore, one of the decisions we are taking for observability workspaces is that we are going to make [Piped Processing Language (PPL)](https://docs.opensearch.org/docs/latest/search-plugins/sql/ppl/index/) the default query language for Discover. We are also expanding our PPL language support to include commands such as JOIN, LOOKUP, and SUBQUERY operations. This decision also opens up other means for users to explore their data, such as...

### Aggregated Queries will generate Visualizations

One powerful feature PPL gives us is to calculate an aggregation from a search result, such as using the [stats command](https://github.com/opensearch-project/sql/blob/main/docs/user/ppl/cmd/stats.rst). But instead of viewing these results in a table format, OSD will auto-detect an aggregated query and generate sensible visualizations such as a bar chart or line chart, depending on the query. These visualizations will be customizable by the user, and even be able to switch the visualization type if needed. And these visualizations will be able to be saved to the dashboard.

The way we are going to achieve is is by having separate tabs within the Discover page. We will have a "logs" tab that will work almost identically as our current Discover experience. We will create a "visualization" tab that will show you the associated visualization based on your query. If users want to see the underlying logs that makes up the visualization, they can switch to the logs tab.

### Curated experience for log patterns

Another feature that PPL provides are [patterns](https://github.com/opensearch-project/sql/blob/main/docs/user/ppl/cmd/patterns.rst). Users when digging into logs will often times want to find patterns in their results, and to enable a seamless experience for this we are building a third tab called "Log Patterns". When a user switches from the Logs tab or Visualize tab and goes to the log pattern tab, OSD will automatically fire a pattern query and display the results in a table format that we are building exclusively for log patterns.

### Query-Driven Experience

To achieve a seamless and consistent experience to the users, we are going with what we are calling a "query driven experience." The query will now be the source of truth for the results that are displayed, including things such as filters, sort, and displayed columns. For example, adding a filter for a specific value by selecting it from our left filter panel will now update the query string.

### UX tailored for data discovery and consumption

We will also be making several changes to the UI/UX, including big changes to the query editor as well as the results table. Our goal will be to make the UI intuitive to all users as well as optimize the space for users to be able to dive into the data with minimal UI disturbances that deter from that experience.

## How to enable the new experience

Run [`yarn start:explore`](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/main/package.json#L71) and open an observability workspace to see our current development!

## Questions and Answers

### When will this experience launch?

We are currently in active development, but we are planning on releasing a working build of this new experience in mid July 2025. After this launch, we will continue on devel

author: angle943
title: [RFC] (Re)Introduction of Storybook.js in OSD
body:
## Introduction

This RFC reintroduces [storybook.js](https://storybook.js.org/) to OpenSearch Dashboards (OSD). As our project grows in complexity and attracts more contributors, we need to elevate our component development process and enable parallel feature development while minimizing merge conflicts.

Storybook enables us to "Build UI components and pages in isolation," offering three key benefits:

1. Isolated component development and visual testing without app integration
2. Simplified testing of edge cases for both PR authors and reviewers
3. Encouragement of modular component architecture

## Key Benefits in Detail

### Isolated Component Development

Previously, developers faced several challenges without Storybook:

- Mandatory app integration for visual testing, leading to larger PR diffs
- Merge conflicts when multiple developers worked on components within the same container
- Forced "top-down" development approach instead of flexible "bottom-up" development

Storybook eliminates these constraints, providing greater development flexibility.

### Simplified Edge Case Testing

Testing edge cases (e.g., overflow handling in table cells) traditionally required cumbersome DOM manipulation. Storybook simplifies this process by allowing:

- Easy prop manipulation through the Storybook interface
- Quick visualization of various component states
- Streamlined review process for edge cases

This approach encourages both developers and reviewers to consider and test edge cases more thoroughly.

### Promoting Modular Architecture

Storybook naturally encourages:

- Breaking down complex components into smaller, manageable pieces
- Clear separation between business logic and rendering logic
- More maintainable and testable component structure

## Historical Context

Storybook was previously removed from OSD ([PR #1172](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/1172)) due to:

- Low adoption in new component development
- CVE issues in dependencies

With the CVE issues now resolved, we're bringing Storybook back.

## Implementation Strategy

### For Contributors

While retrofitting Storybook to existing components isn't mandatory, we strongly encourage creating stories for new components to leverage the benefits mentioned above.

### Technical Setup

We've implemented a plugin-specific approach:

- Stories are organized by plugin
- Each plugin requires minimal setup to enable Storybook
- Run stories using `yarn storybook PLUGINNAME`

Detailed setup instructions are available in our [documentation](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/main/packages/osd-storybook/README.md).

## Community Input

We recognize that Storybook offers many more benefits beyond what we've outlined. If you're experienced with Storybook and have suggestions for improving our implementation, we welcome your contributions! Please share your ideas in the comments of this RFC.

author: raintygao
title: [RFC] Introduce a Core Notebook Plugin in OpenSearch Dashboards
body:
## Summary

This RFC proposes introducing a new **Notebook plugin** as a core component of OpenSearch Dashboards, referencing the foundational design and motivation outlined in [RFC: Move Notebook from Observability to OpenSearch Dashboards Core](https://github.com/opensearch-project/dashboards-observability/issues/2442).

As the importance of notebook functionality continues to grow—extending beyond the initial scope of the Observability plugin—there is a clear need to integrate Notebooks more deeply with OpenSearch Dashboards' core features such as **Discover**, **Visualizations**, and **Dashboards**. To support this integration, we propose creating a new plugin under `src/plugins/` that will expose core interfaces and APIs for Notebooks.

This proposal covers **Phase 1: Interface Establishment** as described in the original RFC.

## Solution

We propose the following implementation approach:

- Create a new core plugin under `src/plugins/notebooks/`.
- This plugin will contain public interfaces and APIs that allow other core and external plugins to register or consume notebook functionalities.
- The actual notebook implementation will remain in the `dashboards-observability` plugin during this phase.
- In **Phase 2**, the full implementation will be migrated.

### Interface 
```ts
interface INotebookClient {
  startInvestigation: (context: IInvestigationContext) => void;
}

interface NotebookPluginSetup {
  registerNotebookClient: (notebookClient: INotebookClient) => void;
  getNotebookClient: () => INotebookClient;
}

interface NotebookPluginStart {
  getNotebookClient: () => INotebookClient;
}
```

These interfaces will act as contracts for interaction between the core notebook service and other plugins.

### Benefits
This refactor offers several key advantages:

- Decoupled Integration: Other core plugins (e.g., Discover, Visualizations) can leverage notebook capabilities via defined interfaces without tight coupling or external dependencies.
- Developer Experience: Shared interfaces and types exposed from core make it easier for developers to adopt and implement Notebook interactions without deep knowledge of file structures in external plugins.
- Unified Platform Capability: Aligns with the vision of Notebooks as a first-class analytical and documentation tool within OpenSearch, beyond just Observability.
- Simplified Maintenance: Centralizing notebook capability in core allows better governance, testing, and upgrade coordination.

Additional benefits are outlined in detail in [RFC: Move Notebook from Observability to OpenSearch Dashboards Core](https://github.com/opensearch-project/dashboards-observability/issues/2442).

## Scope of This RFC
This RFC only covers Phase 1, which includes interface establishment and initial plugin scaffolding. Phase 2 (full migration) will be proposed separately after the foundation is complete.

## References
[RFC: Move Notebook from Observability to OpenSearch Dashboards Core](https://github.com/opensearch-project/dashboards-observability/issues/2442)

## Conclusion
Introducing a core Notebook plugin is a strategic step in evolving OpenSearch Dashboards into a more cohesive and extensible platform. By treating Notebooks as a fundamental capability, we not only simplify integration but also empower developers and users across a broader range of use cases.

author: rvora2000
title: [RFC] Datasets in OpenSearch UI
body:
### Introduction

This RFC proposes introducing a new concept called "Datasets" to OpenSearch UI. Datasets would serve as a unified abstraction layer for data management, enabling users to work with data from various sources—including OpenSearch indices and external data sources—through a consistent interface. This RFC outlines the concept, benefits, and proposed implementation of Datasets, and seeks community feedback on the approach.

### Motivation and Problem Statement

Tpday, OpenSearch UI relies on index patterns for data access—a concept specific to OpenSearch that doesn't support non-OpenSearch data sources. This approach presents several challenges:

1. **Conceptual complexity**: Users unfamiliar with OpenSearch struggle to understand index patterns and how they relate to data selection.
2. **Limited abstraction:** There's no unified way to combine data from multiple sources (both OpenSearch and external) for comprehensive exploration, visualization, and analytics.
3. **Technical barrier:** The current approach exposes underlying data source complexities to users who may want to focus on data analysis rather than infrastructure details.
4. **Data distribution reality:** In real-world scenarios, data is often distributed across various clusters or storage systems. For example, logs might be spread across different clusters or time periods, with no straightforward way to append or join this data.

We have an opportunity to address these challenges by creating an abstraction layer that simplifies data access and combination, while preserving the power and flexibility of OpenSearch.

### Proposed Solution: Datasets

Datasets would provide a logical representation of data stored in and across various sources. A Dataset is fundamentally a user-friendly way to define, organize, and access data within OpenSearch UI.


**What is a Dataset?**

A Dataset is a new artifact in OpenSearch that defines and manages data from various sources, both OpenSearch and non-OpenSearch. It serves as a LOGICAL REPRESENTATION of data stored in one or more data sources, including:

* OpenSearch indices
* SQL databases
* Object stores (like S3)
* APIs and other data sources

Datasets would facilitate:

* **Data Exploration:** Enabling users to explore and analyze data through a unified interface
* **Data Combination**: Supporting both union operations (combining data with identical schemas) and join operations (relating data through common fields)
* **Visualization**: Allowing users to create visualizations and dashboards based on single or combined data sources
* **Collaboration**: Enabling users to share common data definitions across individuals and teams

**What Datasets are NOT**

To be clear, Datasets would NOT be:

* A directly queryable storage entity. Datasets don't store data; they serve as a logical reference that OpenSearch uses to execute queries against the actual underlying data sources.
* A replacement for direct query access to data sources. Advanced users can still query data sources directly when needed.
* An organizational construct like tags or folders. Datasets focus on data access and representation, not artifact organization.

### Core Concepts

Dataset Types

1. **Single-Source Datasets:** Reference data from a single source, such as an OpenSearch index, SQL database, or object store.
2. **Composite Datasets**: Combine data from multiple sources using:

    * **Union Operations**: Appending data with identical schemas (e.g., logs spread across different indices)
    * **Join Operations**: Relating data through common fields (e.g., joining application logs with user data)

Key Components

1. **Data Source Selection**: Connecting to OpenSearch indices or external data sources
2. **Schema Management**: Defining and customizing fields, including calculated fields
3. **Field Configuration**: Setting field types, formats, and descriptions
4. **Time-Based Configuration**: Configuring date/time fields and time ranges
5. **Permissi

2. Parse through raw JSON responses
3. Mentally visualize patterns and issues
4. Repeat this process frequently during troubleshooting

For example, to check circuit breaker issues, we need to run '_nodes/stats/breaker' and manually analyze the data, making it difficult to quickly identify problematic nodes or track changes over time.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A native health dashboard in OpenSearch that:
1. Automatically fetches and visualizes critical DevTools API metrics
2. Displays clear, ASCII-based visualizations or other visualizations on demand e.g. :

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Manual DevTools: Continue using manual DevTools queries, but this is time-consuming and prone to missing important patterns
Third-party Visualization Tools: Export DevTools commands output to external visualization tools, but this requires data export and additional tool and time management which is critical during troubleshooting 

**Additional context**

I've created proof-of-concept visualizations using breaker stats that demonstrate the value of visual representation. The ASCII-based approach ensures:

author: franco-martin
title: Support for Filters in Metric Aggregations
body: **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** Yes. Im using TSVB to calculate CPU usage as a percentage but it works for lots of other metrics in an opentelemetry schema. Im using the opentelemetry operator with a prometheus scraper and using data prepper to send the data to opensearch. My schema looks like this: It should be easy as calculating the sum of the idle time and divide it by the sum of time in all CPU modes, that should give us the percentage of time. Same applies to all operations that require performing an aggregation on some fields to perform a mathematical operation in some other fields, this has also happened with calculating IO latency. I need to sum the time that was spent reading from disk and divide that by the operations that were performed. This isn't an issue when prometheus sends its data to metricbeat like I explain [here](https://medium.com/a-production-ready-homelab/prometheus-and-opensearch-aaed9e31317d) since metricbeat pushes the metric name as its own field, increasing field count (which is not great). **Describe the solution you'd like** We can either support cross series operations or add another field for metric aggregations where we can add a filter. so that instead of only having Aggregation and Field, we would also have a filter like we do on the Filter Ratio aggregation **Describe alternatives you've considered** We can either support cross series operations or add another field for metric aggregations where we can add a filter. Cross series operations would be very interesting to see, but I understand that it might be more complicated to implement. **Additional context**

Performance Improvements: Yarn 4.x offers substantial enhancements in build performance compared to Yarn 1.x. This includes faster install times and better resource utilization.
Security Enhancements: Yarn 4.x introduces Hardened Mode, which adds extra validations to protect against common attacks, ensuring the integrity of the lockfile and package metadata.
Modern Features: Yarn 4.x includes new features such as Corepack integration, which simplifies package manager version management, and improved plugin support.

author: wanglam
title: [Data Source] Add Schema Validation to CustomApiSchemaRegistry to Prevent Method Overrides
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The current implementation of `CustomApiSchemaRegistry` lacks validation when registering new API schemas. This can lead to method conflicts when multiple plugins register schemas that define the same properties or methods on the OpenSearch client. When two schemas attempt to register methods with the same name, the later one silently overrides the earlier one, causing "method not found" errors when code tries to use the overridden methods. This creates hard-to-debug issues during runtime that should be caught during the plugin setup phase.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Enhance the `register` method in `CustomApiSchemaRegistry` to validate new schemas against existing ones before adding them to the registry. The validation should:

1. Analyze the schema function to detect which client properties or namespaces it's attempting to create or modify
2. Check for potential conflicts with previously registered schemas
3. Either throw an error or provide a warning when a conflict is detected
4. Optionally provide information about which plugin is attempting to register the conflicting schema

This would prevent method overrides during the plugin setup phase rather than encountering runtime errors when methods are called.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Implement a setup-time detection mechanism that dry-runs each schema registration against a test client instance before adding it to the registry. This would compare the OpenSearch client prototype before and after applying each schema to identify any properties being overridden. If conflicts are detected, we could either reject the schema or warn the developer about potential conflicts without having to deeply analyze the schema function itself.

**Additional context**

Data Source OpenSearch Client Initialization Code: https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/411e108677148524cae0397d36242bc0fd8300ac/src/plugins/data_source/server/client/configure_client.ts#L86

title: [Meta][Autocomplete Improvement] Major tracker for autocomplete improvement issues and tasks
body:
# Infrastructure and foundation

## Task 1: Monaco Editor Upgrade: From 0.17.0 to 0.52.0

### Current Limitations & Future Benefits

The current Monaco Editor version 0.17.0 has several limitations that impact the development experience and functionality in OpenSearch Dashboards:

- **Limited Suggestion Control**: The current version offers minimal control over code suggestions, with only basic options like enabling/disabling word-based suggestions.
- **Outdated UI Components**: The suggestion widget and other UI elements use older styling approaches that are difficult to customize.
- **Inflexible API**: The completion provider API lacks context-awareness and granular control options.
- **Outdated Icon System**: Uses an image-based sprite system instead of modern font-based icons.

Upgrading to version 0.52.0 will bring significant improvements:

- **Enhanced Inline Completions**: Granular word-based suggestions with options for current document, matching documents, or all documents.
- **Improved Suggestion Widget**: Preview functionality, better handling of deprecated items, and forward stability for consistent suggestions.
- **Modern API**: Provider prioritization with yieldsToGroupIds, better context-awareness, and more control over suggestion behavior.
- **Modern UI Components**: Codicon font-based icon system and improved theming capabilities.

### Technical Challenges

The upgrade process involves several significant technical challenges:

1. **Breaking API Changes**: The Monaco Editor API has undergone substantial changes between versions.
2. **Modern JavaScript Features**: Newer Monaco versions use modern JavaScript syntax (optional chaining, static blocks, nullish coalescing) that may require additional transpilation.
3. **Module System Changes**: Differences in how modules are imported and exported between versions.
4. **Worker Implementation Changes**: Updates to how web workers are configured and used.
5. **UI Component Structure Changes**: The DOM structure of components like the suggestion widget has been redesigned.

### Sub Tasks

- [ ] Upgrade to 0.30.1

author: LDrago27
title: [Enhancement] Add Cross Cluster Search Support in OpenSearch Dashboards
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The Cross Cluster Search feature has been a part of OpenSearch since version 1.0 and is accessible via APIs. However, OpenSearch Dashboards do not offer direct support for cross-cluster search. Consequently, users of OpenSearch Dashboards have never had a way to discover which data sources contain remote cluster connections, explicitly view and select remote indices, or query them.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

As part of this enhancement we plan on explicitly supporting the cross cluster search feature within core Opensearch Dashboards. In order to do so we will be updating the following pages. 

1. Data Sources (Workspace and App Specific): Identify and highlight domains with remote OpenSearch connections.
2. Create a Workspace: Identify and highlight domains with remote OpenSearch connections in the Associate the workspace with Data source workflow
3. Index Patterns: Mark domains with remote OpenSearch connections and list all remote indices in the index list.
4. Discover: Highlight domains with remote OpenSearch connections and display all remote indices in the index list.

**Out of Scope**

There are specific limitations when querying a cross-cluster index or index pattern, as outlined below. Addressing these limitations is beyond the scope of this project and would likely require support from the core backend teams to resolve.

Limitations

* SQL queries are not supported for the Cross Cluster Indexes/Index patterns
* PPL queries are supported to a certain extent for the Cross Cluster Indexes/Index patterns namely only for those remote indexes which have their mapping stored in the current cluster (https://github.com/seankao-az/sql/blob/main/docs/user/ppl/admin/cross_cluster_search.rst#limitation)

**Proposed Design**

In order to support the above requirements we need to add the following functionality in Core dashboards

* List the remote cluster connections for a Opensearch cluster
* Show indices present within the remote clusters

To power the above functions we will be leveraging the following API’s .

* List the remote cluster connections for a Opensearch cluster
    * /_remote/info : This provides a list of a connection aliases corresponding to the remote connections that the opensearch domain has with other opensearch domains.
* Show indices present within the remote clusters
    * /_resolve/index/<connection alias>:*  : This api provides a list of indexes that are present within the remote connection (connection alias)

title: Add config to set allow_no_indices when getting fieldcap
body:
### **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

#### Background
Opensearch & Dashboard Version: `2.12.0`

I use Cross Cluster Search with Remote Cluster  settings.
- Cluaster 
  - CCS Cluster: Cluster for Cross Cluster Search
  - Data1 / Data2 Cluster: Cluster to store indices
- Index Location
  - `index1`: Index: exists in Data1
  - `index2`: index: exists in Data2

#### Problem
In a situation where you are creating an Index Pattern for a Remote Cluster, the following issue occurs.

- When using the wildcard expression `*:index1*`, `*:index2*`, the Time field is not retrieved correctly.
- This is because an error occurs when requesting to get the field cap. The reason for the error is that Opensearch Dashboard does hardcoding the `allow_no_indices` option to `false` when executing the Opensearch Field Cap API. : https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/blob/9ec9a677af5f28e5450926ce07e9d6c3273717a7/src/plugins/data/server/index_patterns/fetcher/lib/opensearch_api.ts#L86-L99

### **Describe the solution you'd like*
This needs to be set to config so that the `allow_no_indice` option can be changed.

### **Describe alternatives you've considered**
Since the default value of `allow_no_indices` in the Opensearch API is true, we also set it to `true` in Dashboard.

### **Additional context**
- Field Capabilities API : https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/search-field-caps.html

title: [WIP][Initiative] Unified visualization editor / render engine in OSD
body: ## Background In current OSD, we have 3 types of editors / flows to create a visualization: - Curated visualization editor based on each types - Vega - Visbuilder ### Curated visualization editor based on each types This type of visualization is now the mostly used way to create visualizations. It offers query aggregation and fine-grained settings for different types of charts. However, users can not change the chart type from one to another, and this kind of visualizations are built based on a customized schema invented by OpenSearch Dashboards, meaning adding new chart types or multi-layers requires additional implementation effort, and it does not quite follow the style of community, making it hard for others to contribute to the feature. ### Vega Vega is a new kind of visualization editor mainly focus on using Vega, a open-sourced and popular schema, to render visualizations. It has rich features including multi-layers and varies of chart types but the editor is a pure JSON editor, requiring users to have knowledge on Vega schema and query details, which is not user friendly. ### Visbuilder Visbuilder is a new type of visualization editor that focus on: - Support changing chart type while creating the visualization. - A more light-weighted editor using both legacy visualization and vega as its render engine, the engine type is controlled by an advanced settings. - Support drag-drop user experience. **Describe the solution you'd like** ### Using `Vega` as the only official render engine for visualizations created by visbuilder. author: ruanyl
title: [RFC] [Draft]: Deprecation of Saved Object namespace(s)
body:
## Background
The **Saved Object namespace** was originally introduced in OpenSearch Dashboards to provide logical isolation of saved objects, allowing users to manage and access data within specific scopes. However, with the introduction of the **workspace feature**, OpenSearch Dashboards now offers a more flexible and scalable approach to handling logical isolation. Functionally, workspaces cover the same primary use cases as namespaces.

Given this overlap in functionality, maintaining both features adds unnecessary complexity to the system. To simplify the architecture, we are considering the **deprecation of the Saved Object namespace feature**.

## Deprecation plan
Saved Object namespace will be marked as deprecated feature for `3.x` and will be removed in `4.0.0`

## Impact analysis
We will review any parts of the codebase that currently reference the Saved Object namespace functionality to ensure they instead leverage the workspace model. Identify and communicate with plugin developers and third-party integrators who rely on namespaces. Provide clear migration guidelines and support channels during the transition.

> TODO: list all impacted plugins and features here

| Plugin name | Description | Links |
|--------|--------|--------|
| | | |
|  | | |
|  | | |
|  | | |
|  | | | 

## Gaps between namespace and workspace
We will review the impacted features and come up with solution to migrate them to workspace. The gaps between namespace and workspace will be listed and mitigations should be provided.

> TODO: list all gaps and mitigations

## Migration strategy

**Phase 1: Announcement.** Update developer guides, API references to include migration notice and rationale behind the deprecation. Introduce warnings in the logs and developer consoles when a namespace-based saved object is used in the next major release: `v3.x`

**Phase 2: Gradual Deprecation.** Gradually migrate features that rely on namespace to adopt workspace model. Setting up communication channel to support the migration.

**Phase 3: Removal.** Remove the namespace functionality entirely from OSD core as breaking change in the major release: `v4.0.0`

author: ruanyl
title: [enhancement] Support path alias
body:
### Problem
Currently, the path aliases `opensearch-dashboards/public` and `opensearch-dashboards/server` are defined in the tsconfig and are widely used throughout the codebase. However, these aliases are only functional for TypeScript types. They are not configured for Webpack or Babel, leading to failures during development when running dev server or production builds failed when build for release when these imports contain actual modules rather than just types.

### Expectation
The path alias should work for module imports not just only TS types, so I don't have to use relative path when importing modules like `import {...} from '../../../../src/core/public'`. Instead, I can simply type `import {...} from 'opensearch-dashboards/public'`.

### What to do
- [ ] Add path alias support for webpack to ensure browser side code can be compiled successfully during development and build
- [ ] Add path alias support for babel to ensure server side code can be transpiled  successfully
- [ ] Ensure jest unit tests also works with path alias

author: jprmachado
title: Resizable (or Expandable) Trigger Editing Window
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

While limiting the trigger editor to around 15 lines may be sufficient for simpler configurations, it becomes problematic when writing more complex or longer trigger logic. In our workflow, a single query can be used by multiple triggers, so we often embed a fair amount of logic into the trigger field itself. This results in lengthy scripts that are difficult to maintain in a small, fixed-size text box. Scrolling back and forth makes it challenging to see the full picture, spot potential mistakes, or easily modify the code.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26f90cd0-5fc2-431f-a909-ef5d5bcf2119)

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A resizable (or otherwise expandable) trigger editor where users can see more lines of code at once. Ideally, this could be implemented via:

1. A drag-to-resize handle that lets the user expand the editor’s height (and possibly width).
2. A collapsible/expandable “full-screen” or “pop-out” mode to allow for an even broader view of the trigger logic.

Having this flexibility would greatly ease editing, debugging, and reviewing longer trigger scripts.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Writing the code in an external editor (e.g., IDE) and then pasting it back in. However, AFIK there is no painless IDE and would require lots of refactoring to be usable in the dashboard context.

**Additional context**

v 2.18.0

author: billal280
title: DarkMode settings apply globally per tenant and not per user
body:
In the lastest version of OpenSearch Dashboards (2.18.0), darkmode settings is user-specific but only applies globally within the "global" tenant. This means that if a user in tenant X activates dark mode, all other users within that same tenant are affected, and vice versa.
[[#2159]](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/issues/2159)

Similarly, users must manually switch to dark mode for each tenant they have access to. However, logically, when a user decides to enable dark mode, it should apply across all the tenants they access.

This creates inconsistencies in the user experience when navigating between different tenants.

### This repository will be impacted by this brownout and deprecation, [based on this query.](https://github.com/search?q=org%3Aopensearch-project%20actions%2Fupload-artifact%40v3&type=code)

Want to avoid tracking this manually? Setup [dependabot](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-version-updates) to automatically bump version numbers of dependencies including GitHub Actions.

#### Add a .github/dependabot.yml configuration
```yaml
version: 2
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: "github-actions"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
```

author: kavilla
title: [Discover] re-add recent datasets
body:
**Description**

Recent datasets was remove apart of:
https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/pull/8816

This is because without workspaces enabled this fine but with it enabled then recent datasets was persisting across workspaces that potentially dont have the datasource available that the dataset is referencing.

The original fix we wanted to do was to save datasets with workspace id in session storage. To give users the ability to switch workspaces and have access to the previous visit of this workspace and recent datasets.

However, when investigating: the workspace is apart of core start application but dataset service is apart of a service that is apart of the setup lifecycle.

The second path could be storing the workspace in the dataset meta information. This will help with another issue as shared URLs currently take you out of a workspace. So if we add this to the dataset meta information we could recreate the dataset within workspace context. While also persisting the dataset in a specific workspace recents datasets. But the work wouldn't be large but it wouldn't necessarily small. Since the data plugin pretty much has to be enabled for the application to do anything but workspaces isn't as required (although it's a really sick feature).

The feature work should avoid placing it in a way that the data plugin is now a dependency of the workspaces service

author: gupta-mayank
title: Supporting dynamic paths for application launch
body:
We are using OpenSearch and OpenSearch dashboards. For Open search Dashboards (OSD), 

1. We use the spaces to support multiple tenants.
2. As we have our authentication application, we use proxy authentication of OpenSearch dashboards (OSD) to launch respective tenants using headers.
3. We use NGINX as a reverse proxy from our application to proxy pass OSD. The NGINX URL is launched from our authentication application.
4. There is a new ask to support URLs containing a tenant-unique ID in our main application. <application>/tenant1 , <application>/tenant2
5. As we use a single instance of OSD ( with spaces for multi-tenant support), we want the OSD to return the tenant ID like tenant1/tenant2 in calls or give a way to dynamically append the base path in the OSD application.
Is there a way to support this use case?

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A dynamic way of supporting different mount points or a way to return data from OSD ( headers or otherwise)

**A clear and concise description of what you want to happen.**

We want to launch OSD using a proxy from different URLs like application/tenant1 or application/tenant2 so that in our NGINX we can pass on the right headers.

A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered.

An alternative, we are still discussing like maintaining a session or storage to check tenant-based launch.

**Additional context**

author: huyaboo
title: Adding keybinds to CodeEditor/text editor components
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
One of the painpoints when creating visualizations is the lack of keybinds. When typing longer queries in Dev tools or making Vega visualizations, the text body can get lengthy. It would be nice if the editor components within these visualizations had some sort of a "Vim mode" toggle so users familiar with vim-like keybinds can type.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The `@osd/monaco` package provides the `monaco` text editor that OSD consumes. Specifically, inside `CodeEditor` component, it provides a common component for text-based visualization editors to consume. There already exists a package [monaco-vim](https://www.npmjs.com/package/monaco-vim) that integrates Vim mode into monaco. 

To configure, we can add a global advanced UI setting to toggle on keybind mode and have some UI setting for each individual editor such that these configs override the global default (needs investigation)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Introducing a plugin to provide the components would be useful to other plugins, but core cannot consume this plugin. In general, we could find a better way to import custom plugin components into core but this is orthogonal to feature request
- Introducing a new OSD component that uses [CodeMirror](https://github.com/codemirror/dev/) as the editor and using [codemirror-vim](https://github.com/replit/codemirror-vim). This is convenient, but would require creating a whole new component for plugins to consume
